text:
CHRIST JESUS—THE ULTIMATE REDEEMER

📖In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace (Ephesians 1:7).

Redemption is one of the beautiful truths in the Gospel because it reveals not only what Christ accomplished, but also who He is. The Scriptures present the picture of a redeemer as one who has both the legal right and the ability to secure another's freedom. In the Lord Jesus Christ, we find the perfect and ultimate fulfilment ofthat picture. He is the Redeemer who paid the full price for our salvation and brought us into everlasting freedom. 

In the law of Moses, a kinsman-redeemer could redeem a relative who had fallen into debt or bondage. The redeemer had a legal right to act on behalf of the one in need, but he also had to pay the required price. Freedom wasn't obtained by mere desire or good intentions; a price had to be paid. 

This helps us understandthe significance of Christ'ssacrifice.Humanity'sgreatest problem was notmerely the devil's oppression; it was the issue of sin. Sin had brought separation from God and placed mankind under judgment. The righteousdemandsofjusticehad to be satisfied.A price had to be paid. 

What a blessing to know that the Lord Jesus took our place and paid the full price required for our redemption. The payment wasn't silver or gold; it was His precious blood. The Bible says, *“Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold…But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”* (1 Peter 1:18-19). 

When He shed His blood, He obtained eternal redemption for us. The debt was settled. The claims against us were satisfied.The penaltyofsinwasfullyaddressed. The Lord Jesus paid the price you could never pay. He accomplished what you could never accomplish for yourself. 

Through His sacrifice, you've been brought into righteousness and fellowship with God. He met every demand of divine justice, paid the full price with His own blood, and secured your eternal liberty. Therefore, live with gratitude and confidence, knowing that your salvation is eternally secure in Him.

       *🙏PRAYER*
Dear Father, I thank you for the redemption that is mine through the blood of Jesus Christ. I rejoice in the knowledge that the full price for my salvation has been paid. I walk in righteousness, in fellowship with you, and in grateful acknowledgment of the fulfilment of the full blessings of the Gospel in my life, in Jesus' Name. Amen.

*FURTHER STUDY📖=>*
 *1 Peter 1:18-19 NIV*
For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors, [19] but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect.

*Hebrews 9:11-15 KJV*
 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; [12] Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. [13] For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: [14] How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? [15] And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

*📖DAILY SCRIPTURE READING📖*

author: rupertpitt1

text:
The Long March Through France's Institutions Has Reached the Streets

France's burning town halls and barricaded schools did not emerge from nowhere. Grievances over teacher shortages, neglected buildings and public spending were real. So was the willingness of revolutionary activists to exploit them. Behind the disorder lies a question European governments have avoided for decades: what happens when institutions become battlegrounds for competing ideologies while foreign powers exploit the divisions?

In the late 1960s, the revolutionary Left embraced the long march through the institutions. Universities, education, journalism and public administration offered opportunities to reshape society over generations. France already possessed a formidable communist tradition, but 1968 gave institutional radicalism new momentum. Fifty years later, the language remains familiar. Capitalism is oppression, Western power is imperialism, and established authority exists to be challenged.

Alongside this developed another movement with different ambitions. The Muslim Brotherhood pursued influence through religious associations, education, charities and community representation. France's Interior Ministry warned in 2025 about its institutional strategy. Its report identified Étudiants musulmans de France as associated with Brotherhood-linked organisations. In February's student welfare elections, EMF-backed lists gained eleven representatives. On 15 October, EMF publicly supported the school demonstrations.

The revolutionary Left and political Islam envisage profoundly different societies. One draws upon Marxism, the other religious authority. Yet Gaza has demonstrated how readily their campaigns converge. Communist student organisations, Islamist-associated networks and pro-Palestinian movements can advance the same immediate cause despite disagreements about what follows. The Iranian Revolution offers a warning. Secular leftists helped overthrow the Shah alongside Islamists, only to discover that Khomeini's victorious movement had little tolerance for former allies.

Then there is the money. Investigative reporting has documented Qatar's historical financing of religious and cultural institutions in Europe. A French judicial investigation has examined alleged Qatari payments to political and media intermediaries. Le Monde reported evidence pointing towards Qatari entities in an influence operation involving French contacts. None establishes Qatari involvement in the riots, but the findings raise questions about foreign money purchasing influence inside democratic societies.

China, Russia and Iran present further concerns. Reporting has linked a Shanghai-based financier accused of promoting Beijing's interests to international activist media networks. French intelligence has documented Russian disinformation operations. Iran maintains intelligence and proxy networks across Europe. On 13 October, France's foreign minister warned that foreign actors were exploiting divisions over immigration, secularism and Israel-Palestine. Their role in the violence remains unproven, but their interest in exploiting it is clear.

The danger lies in examining everything separately. University radicalism becomes education policy. Islamist influence falls to religious regulators. Foreign financing goes to investigators. Disinformation becomes an intelligence matter. Meanwhile, the political consequences accumulate across institutions entrusted with preserving a common civic culture.

France must establish who organised the violence, who financed the surrounding networks and whether foreign interests played any operational role. But the deeper questions will remain when the streets are cleared. Decades of ideological influence cannot be undone by arresting rioters.

A republic cannot preserve its authority indefinitely while refusing to examine who shapes the loyalties, assumptions and ambitions of the generations it educates.

text:
Bitcoin Movies and Documentaries

Media Man Crypto Watercooler

Money Electric: The Bitcoin Mystery (2024, HBO) Directed by Cullen Hoback, this documentary investigates Bitcoin’s origins and the identity of its creator, Satoshi Nakamoto. It offers a thrilling, globe-spanning narrative with new clues about Bitcoin’s rise. Available on HBO and Max.

Banking on Bitcoin (2016, Netflix) A popular documentary exploring Bitcoin’s roots, its potential to disrupt traditional banking, and its early challenges. Features interviews with key figures like Erik Voorhees and Charlie Shrem. Available on Netflix and other platforms.

The Rise and Rise of Bitcoin (2014) Follows programmer Daniel Mross, an early Bitcoin enthusiast, documenting Bitcoin’s volatile journey and its community. Ideal for beginners, it avoids technical jargon and includes figures like Brian Armstrong. Available on Prime Video, iTunes, and Fandango at Home.

Bitcoin: The End of Money as We Know It (2015) A concise 60-minute crash course on money’s evolution and Bitcoin’s role as a decentralized alternative. Features Andreas Antonopoulos and Roger Ver. Won awards at the Amsterdam Film Festival. Available on various platforms.

God Bless Bitcoin (2025, YouTube) Explores Bitcoin as a solution to broken monetary systems, featuring Bitcoin advocates and interfaith leaders. Free to watch on YouTube.

text:
Virginia Board of Psychology revokes license of psychologist Katie S. Kelly for sexual relationship with patient

The Virginia Board of Psychology has entered a consent order affecting the license of clinical psychologist Katie Sinclair Kelly after finding she engaged in a romantic and sexual relationship with a patient while continuing to provide therapy.

Kelly was first licensed on June 29, 2017. Her license was summarily suspended on February 12, 2026. The Board found that, beginning in March 2022, she violated regulations governing confidentiality, boundaries, and professional conduct by initiating and maintaining a sexual relationship with “Patient A,” a woman she treated from January 2021 to August 2023. Patient A had a reported history of childhood sexual abuse and later multiple sexual assaults, including rape.

Findings detail progressive boundary violations: personal disclosures about Kelly’s marriage and substance-use history, invitations to her home, offers of alcohol, requests for rides when intoxicated, and physical contact such as sitting on the patient’s lap. Text messages and other evidence showed the relationship became romantic and sexual after Kelly kissed the patient; sexual activity then occurred regularly, primarily at Kelly’s home, while therapy continued. Patient A reported one instance of non-consensual digital penetration of her rectum. Kelly instructed the patient to keep the relationship secret, delete messages, and refer to her as “Dr. Kelly” only during sessions. The patient’s mental health deteriorated, including worsening of an eating disorder requiring residential treatment, increased self-harm, and a suicide attempt after the relationship ended.

Additional violations committed by Kelly included practicing outside the scope of psychology by giving the patient medication advice and providing her a controlled substance; inadequate record-keeping for Patient A and other clients, and serving simultaneously as therapist and parenting coordinator in a dual role. Under investigation, Kelly denied the romantic and sexual allegations.

Source: Consent Order in re: Katie Sinclair Kelly LCP, lic. no. 0810-005728, case nos. 230850 & 234034, Virginia Board of Psychology, June 22, 2026.

text:
Today, I flagged off the distribution of additional 49,337 agricultural inputs, productive assets, and processing equipment for local farmers and vulnerable households in Kwara State.

The initiative is being implemented under FADAMA CARES 2.0, a programme powered by the World Bank-supported Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES), with the active involvement of the state government.

At least 186,230 people had earlier benefitted from a similar initiative in the past. This newly launched 49,337 brings the total beneficiaries to 235,567.

Our farmers face costly inputs, unpredictable weather, limited equipment, the difficulties of moving and processing produce. Our duty as government is to remove these barriers and obstacles so that their labor pays.

This phase of the flag-off offers rice, maize, soyabeans inputs. It also provides equipment ranging from sprayers, water pumps, and power tillers to rice mills. We also have cassava processors, fish smoking plants, and commercial boats. Our goal is to help farmers produce more, lose less, process better, reach wider markets, and earn more with opportunities for women and young people.

In my remarks at the event, I congratulated the prospective beneficiaries and enjoined them to see the inputs and assets as investment opportunities and not as handouts. I also acknowledged the active roles played by different stakeholders to make the programme a huge success.

Also today, I launched the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT) Door-to-Door Movement in our state. The group, which is being led nationally by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, is a great platform to mobilise support for the re-election of President Tinubu and communicate the life-changing policies and programmes of the Federal Government to the people.

I commended the leadership of the movement and tasked them to cooperate with all APC structures from the national leadership down to ward officials and polling unit committees. We are all working for a common goal. I also tasked the newly inaugurated executives of the movement at the state level to work hard in their mobilisation campaigns and convey the impacts of the Renewed Hope Agenda to all the nooks and crannies of Kwara.

VETERANS FOR AMERICA FIRST ANNOUNCES ENDORSEMENT OF U.S. NAVY VETERAN THEODIS DANIEL FOR TEXAS HOUSE DISTRICT 147

Endorsement Issued by Devarjaye “DJ” Daniel  
National Ambassador  
Veterans for America First

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

HOUSTON, TEXAS — Veterans for America First proudly announces its endorsement of Theodis Daniel, United States Navy veteran and Republican candidate for Texas House District 147, recognizing his legacy of military service, family dedication, and commitment to American values.

Long before entering the political arena, Daniel answered his nation's call to duty, serving in the United States Navy as a Machinist's Mate and Fireman. In naval engineering, where operational readiness depends upon discipline, technical skill, and unwavering teamwork, Daniel became part of a proud tradition of American sailors who keep our fleet mission-ready.

His legacy of service extends beyond the uniform. As a father of three, Daniel has demonstrated a commitment to family and community, passing down a respect for service and sacrifice to the next generation.

His campaign emphasizes constitutional freedoms, stronger families, public safety, educational opportunity, combating human trafficking, and government accountability.

Kimberly Taiko Moyers, National Vet Force Director for Veterans for America First and fellow United States Navy veteran, offered this statement:

"Those of us who served in the Navy understand that the oath we took does not expire when we leave the service. Theodis Daniel carries the legacy of that service into his family, his community, and his pursuit of public office. That commitment to duty and country deserves recognition."

Texas was built by generations who understood that freedom carries responsibility and that service to one's country does not end when the uniform comes off.

Veterans for America First recognizes Theodis Daniel's military service, his dedication to family, and his commitment to the people of Texas House District 147.

Devarjaye “DJ” Daniel  
National Ambassador  
Veterans for America First

Physical Brent Squeeze: Screen Selloff is a Trap

Brent fell 1.48% to $108.24/bbl while Dec Gasoil rose 2.39% to $1,402.25/t. The implied Gasoil crack widened to ~$80.13/bbl.

Paper crude weakened. The physical product market tightened.

Physical Dislocation

Crude is offered, gasoil is bid, and the crack is widening—the signature of a physical squeeze.

Cargo and Freight

Vitol absorbed 19 of 22 prompt WTI/BFOET cargoes. Bids met no sellers. At $20.29/bbl Houston-to-Rotterdam freight, cheap external product does not become a cheap European barrel.

Curve and Substitutes

Dec–Jan backwardation remains +$2.97/bbl. WTI Midland delivered into Rotterdam is +$2.27/bbl versus Dated, leaving substitute supply impaired.

Market Implication

The screen sold headline relief. The deliverable barrel remains trapped. The selloff is a trap.

text:
Non-committal offers are common in high school. They’ve always been apart of the recruiting game.
This is not the same tho. 
Bear’s offer from Notre Dame was presented as a bona fide committable scholarship. 

Why wouldn’t it be?
Bear was a four-star QB ranked 9th nationally. 
(For ref. he was ranked significantly higher than Ian Book coming out of high school, and ND signed Book as a three-star QB)

The telling part is Deuce Knight sat on his ND offer from March 2023 until Sept. 

On September 14, 2023, just two days before Bachmeier’s visit for the ND v. Central Michigan game, Notre Dame recruiting reporter Mike Singer submitted a prediction that Bear would commit to Notre Dame that weekend. Because even he expected it to be a real offer. 

Crazy thing happened though…
Bear never got that Coach’s meeting after the game. Deuce Knight suddenly committed to the program the next day.

Notre Dame got the QB they wanted even though he didn’t want them.
(Needless to remind everyone Knight de-committed and chose Auburn in the end.) 

The whole experience was humiliating and heartbreaking for Bear & his family. 
He obviously had this game circled ever since.

text:
To my American and Canadian friends: I am French, and I am watching my country slowly surrender.

On October 17, France witnessed another eruption of violence. Shops looted, buildings set ablaze, police officers attacked. In Limoges, even the city hall went up in flames.

And what did our political leaders offer? Expressions of sadness, appeals for unity, endless promises to restore order.

I grew up in a country that taught the world about liberty, sovereignty and the rule of law. Today, that same country seems increasingly incapable of protecting an ordinary shopkeeper from a mob.

We have built a state that can scrutinize your bank account, regulate your speech and tax your inheritance, yet struggles to guarantee your physical safety.

This is the great French paradox: an increasingly intrusive government presiding over an increasingly fragile society.

I believe compassion without accountability becomes an invitation to disorder. A civilization cannot survive indefinitely when those who obey the law bear the consequences of those who break it.

I love France too much to accept this decline as inevitable.

And I hope you understand something: what you are witnessing here is a warning to every Western democracy.

The foundations of a civilization can erode long before its monuments begin to crumble.

text:
How Did Napoleon’s Nephew Become Emperor of France?

The answer lies in the extraordinary power of a name.

Napoleon Bonaparte died in exile on St. Helena in 1821. Yet his legend refused to die. In 1840, his remains were returned to Paris, where enormous crowds gathered to welcome the fallen emperor home.

To many French people, Napoleon represented more than military victories. He symbolized national glory, social mobility, order, and a France that had once dominated Europe.

His empire had fallen, but his political legacy remained alive.

In 1848, France was once again engulfed in revolution. The monarchy had collapsed, and the Second Republic was born. That December, Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte, Napoleon’s nephew, won the presidential election by a landslide.

His greatest political asset was his surname.

For millions of rural voters, the name Napoleon evoked memories of national greatness and the social changes that had transformed post-revolutionary France. Many valued stability, property, and economic security more than abstract political ideals.

Louis-Napoleon understood this sentiment. He presented himself as the heir to his uncle’s legacy and promised to restore France’s strength.

In December 1851, he staged a coup. A year later, following a plebiscite, he proclaimed himself Emperor Napoleon III, establishing the Second French Empire.

How could a country so closely associated with liberty, equality, and fraternity return to imperial rule?

Because history is rarely driven by ideals alone.

People may fight for liberty during a revolution, then seek order when instability threatens their livelihoods. They may reject hereditary monarchy yet embrace a leader whose name evokes a glorious past.

Napoleon III’s rise demonstrated the political power of collective memory. His uncle’s reputation became a form of inherited political capital, helping him win mass support and legitimize his rule.

But the story ended in disaster.

In 1870, France was defeated in the Franco-Prussian War. Napoleon III was captured at Sedan, and his empire collapsed. He died in exile in 1873.

The Bonapartes had returned to the throne through the power of Napoleon’s name. They ultimately lost it on the battlefield.

Napoleon’s greatest victory may have been the survival of his legend. Even after his empire vanished, his name remained powerful enough to bring another emperor to France.

History offers a timeless lesson: a political system can disappear, yet the memories, symbols, and emotions that sustained it may survive for generations.

text:
⚠️ 🇺🇸 🇫🇷 Trump Warns That Leftist Border Policies Are Destroying France and Threaten America

President Trump told a Kansas rally that globalist left-wing politicians had treasonously imported millions of culturally incompatible third-world migrants into Europe, a move he said is destroying France and must never be repeated in the United States.

Speaking before midterm election crowds in Park City, Trump pointed to the recent unrest across France as proof of failed open-border experiments. He described left-wing leaders as having deliberately brought in large numbers of migrants from societies that reject Western values, people who he argued despise the countries that received them. The remarks drew loud chants of “USA!” from the audience. Earlier statements on his Truth Social account and to reporters had already framed the same events in blunt terms: migrants had taken over France, Paris risked becoming a Muslim city, and European leaders must close their borders immediately or face permanent decline.

The French disorder itself is well documented. Nationwide marches against the cost of living and deteriorating schools drew hundreds of thousands of participants, with official estimates near 550,000 and union figures higher. What began as protests quickly turned into widespread looting, attacks on police, and arson. In Limoges, masked groups set fire to the historic town hall, collapsing its spire and gutting much of the nineteenth-century building. Authorities reported roughly 1,800 to 2,400 arrests and hundreds to nearly 1,000 police officers injured. French officials, including the prime minister, have blamed ultra-left agitators and opportunistic delinquents for the worst violence. Trump and Vice President Vance offered a different diagnosis: the violence reflected deeper problems of mass migration without assimilation, the predictable result of policies that prioritized volume and diversity over cultural compatibility.

Vance had already written that Western liberals imported the third world into France in the name of compassion while ignoring warnings about compatibility. Trump’s rally language went further by labeling the policy itself treasonous. The framing resonates with long-standing conservative arguments that large-scale migration from Islamic-majority regions of Africa and the Middle East has altered the demographic and social character of European cities faster than institutions can absorb it. Parallel concerns appear in reports of parallel societies, elevated crime rates in certain immigrant communities, and periodic outbreaks of street disorder. Mainstream coverage notes that French leaders reject the immigration explanation and instead emphasize economic grievances and far-left organization. Yet the visible scenes of burned civic buildings and overwhelmed police have given Trump’s warning concrete imagery for American audiences two weeks before midterm voting.

For American politics the implication is straightforward. Trump has repeatedly contrasted his own border closures and deportation priorities with the open policies he attributes to the political left. The French example, in his telling, is not an isolated European problem but a cautionary case of what follows when governments treat national identity and social cohesion as secondary to migration targets. Whether the French unrest was primarily driven by migrant populations or by leftist organizers remains contested; the demographic transformation of parts of France is not. Trump’s argument is that sovereign states have both the right and the duty to decide who enters, and that ignoring cultural fit produces lasting damage. The Kansas crowd’s reaction suggested many voters already share that assessment. https://t.co/9XPsgNgkhB

text:
I’ve spoken to many $1B+ revenue data companies in the past weeks, and these are some thoughts on where this is all headed and various types of players that will emerge: 

1) The facilitators. Think companies that offer data anonymisation technology, ‘stock x for data’ to build a universal quality standard for data evaluation so labs don’t need to waste time with low quality data and deals can happen quicker, escrow tech for buyers and sellers to put cash and data into and then exchange in order to not get scammed, banks for financing data vendors, etc. I actually think this is quite overlooked and there’s a lot really cool stuff that will emerge.  

2) The crypto-style data broker. One man operation. Operating out of a tax heaven. Great 6 month opportunity to make cash. Not all to fulfilling, but demand is there. My two cents on this if you’re considering this: act as an ‘advisor’ to the sellers. Build relationships. Almost like an investment banker on the sell-side. Build a website that depicts trust and advisory, not large scale marketplace that doesn’t care. 

3) Large market-place websites. I think there will be a couple that do very well and will make a small % margin on a large volume of deals. This is less of a venture capital play and will likely flourish better if you bootstrap, seen as you don’t need outside capital. Classic problem of getting this off the ground is the chicken and egg problem to get enough sellers and buyers in the first place. Here I would optimise for going viral on social media to achieve that first unlock. 

4) Couple deeply routed players for each type of data that completely verticalises (own deep supply roots; maybe even buy companies) and be in constant communication with the buyers (labs, enterprises) to understand their needs. Here you go the next step and don’t just sell the data raw, but utilise reinforcement learning to increase margin by 10-100x. For this you need some good technical talent and capital to get it off the ground, but comes with the opportunity to build something long-lasting.

text:
You asked an AI agent to sell your keyboard. It sold your keyboard. And your home address. 🤖

Fortune reports that Meta's new AI agent, Muse, went a little too far on Facebook Marketplace for a Toronto tech reviewer who handed it his listing as an experiment in late September.

What Muse did, all on its own:

🤝 Agreed to a deal without checking in
🏠 Shared his home address when the buyer asked
💬 Messaged "Yep, I'm here!" from his account when the buyer showed up, late at night
💸 On a different item, seemingly offered to go $100 below his set minimum

The cause: he had given Muse "always allow" permissions, assuming it would ask before doing anything big. It did not ask. The buyer and seller eventually made peace, and he has mostly unplugged Muse from his apps.

Meta, which launched Muse in September, reached out to him and acknowledged the pricing error. Its own help page admits the agent can slip up or do things you did not expect.

Why it matters: "always-on" agents from Meta, OpenAI and others now act while you're not watching. Experts warn that once an agent takes in your data, you can't fully claw it back, and your friends' data can leak too.

Lesson of the week: read the permissions screen before your assistant starts hosting open houses.

#AI #Privacy

text:
Axios Reporting: Zelenskyy Asks U.S. Senators to Pressure the White House on "Restrictions on Intelligence and Weapons for Ukraine."

On Monday, he held a video conference with a bipartisan group of senators to urge them to pressure the Trump administration to "lift restrictions on the exchange of intelligence and the supply of weapons," according to the report.

During the virtual meeting with a bipartisan group of senators led by Tom Tillis (Republican, North Carolina) and Richard Blumenthal (Democrat, Connecticut), Zelenskyy outlined the various challenges Ukraine is facing since the meeting in Miami. Axios received a transcript from Ukrainian officials.

Starlink satellites from Elon Musk and the Starshield satellite systems of the U.S. military remain partially restricted, despite statements from the White House to the contrary. "We still don't have an explanation for this. Unfortunately, we are hearing different, strange stories," Zelenskyy told the senators. This is hindering Ukraine's ability to shoot down Russian attack drones, he added.

Three times last week, including on Sunday, Ukraine did not receive early warnings from the U.S. about Russian missile attacks, Zelenskyy said, indicating that the exchange of intelligence was restricted. "We have not received clear explanations from Washington as to why this is happening," he added.

Zelenksyy stated that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is not approving the delivery of Patriot interceptors and AIM-9x missiles for the NASAMS air defense system, even though NATO countries have already paid for them. "We almost don't have any Patriot interceptors from our American partners," he said.

"All of this suggests that a political decision has been made to slow down our support," Zelenskyy said. "We want to understand what is happening, why it is happening, and where it is all leading."

Tillis, as noted in the report, stated after the conversation that Congress "remains committed to supporting Ukraine and our European allies in ending Russia's brutal aggression and ensuring a lasting peace."

Blumenthal was also quoted as saying: "Bipartisan support for Ukraine has been clear and unequivocal, and that is what we will continue to express in our upcoming actions."

On Sunday, Zelenskyy spoke with Witcoff and Kushner.
They again asked Ukraine to cease attacks on Russian oil refineries, Ukrainian officials said.

Zelenskyy told the senators that he had offered U.S. envoys a 30-day suspension of strikes on oil refineries. In return, the U.S. would supply Ukraine with Patriot interceptors so that it could defend itself against Russian ballistic missiles during those 30 days.

Zelenskyy told the senators that Witcoff and Kushner were not receptive to this idea.

Zelenskyy told the senators that he will be in Oslo, Norway, next week, and may meet with Witcoff and Kushner on Tuesday or Wednesday. Kushner and Witcoff may then travel from Oslo to Moscow for a meeting with Putin, according to a source familiar with the conversation.

Elon Daily 20261019

① ⭐ Tesla AGM: Musk’s Pay & Control

Tesla’s Dec. 3 meeting will vote on three-year board terms for Musk, Denholm and Straubel. Its proxy lists a 423.7M-share 2025 CEO award valued at $158.4B; none of its 12 milestones has been met. Musk exercised 303.96M options in June, holds nearly 20% of Tesla and has pledged about 207.5M shares.

No Tesla–SpaceX merger vote is on the agenda.

② 🔥 ARK’s Tesla 2031 Target: $4,400

ARK’s new model puts TSLA at $4,400 in its base case, $3,300 bear and $5,000 bull.

These are ARK projections, not Tesla guidance.

③ ⭐ Tesla Japan: FSD Approval Target

Tesla Japan still aims for FSD Supervised approval by year-end 2026, but says timing depends on regulators. Commercial Cybercab operations would require separate Level 4 and operating approvals.

④ Tesla Canada: Model 3 Orders Paused

Tesla paused orders for China-built Model 3 Premium vehicles, citing exhausted import quotas. Government data suggests the overall 49,000-vehicle annual quota has not been fully used.

⑤ ⭐ TSLA +3.8%; Merger Speculation

TSLA closed at $368.06 on Oct. 19. Gary Black floated a hypothetical $420/share SpaceX takeover bid; RBC discussed $480/share as an attractive scenario.

Neither is an official offer.

⑥ 🔥 Musk Pledges SpaceX Shares to U.S. Children

Musk says he plans to give every American child one of his SpaceX shares next year. Trump suggested using Trump Accounts.

At 72–73M children and roughly $146/share, the pledge could total $10.5–10.7B. Implementation details remain unclear.

⑦ ⭐ SpaceX Earnings Preview

SpaceX is expected to report Q3 results Oct. 20, followed by Tesla on Oct. 21.

Analysts forecast roughly 1.7M net new Starlink users; Evercore raised its SpaceX target from $230 to $275.

Investors will watch cash flow, margins and AI spending.

⑧ Bandwagon-5 Delayed

Weather in the booster recovery zone scrubbed SpaceX’s Oct. 19 attempt.

New target: Oct. 20, 6:30 a.m. ET.

Falcon 9 will carry 32 payloads, including a Starfall reentry capsule; the booster is set for flight No. 19.

⑨ ⭐ Starlink Facilities Targeted in Europe

A Bulgarian court approved arrest warrants for two Germans over an alleged Starlink antenna arson attack near Sofia.

Lithuania also reported an attempted attack in Vilnius and suspects Russia-linked sabotage. That link remains an allegation.

⑩ 🔥 Starlink Direct-to-Cell Reaches 11M

VEON says 11M unique people in Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Bangladesh have connected to Starlink satellite-to-phone service at least once in under a year.

That’s cumulative reach—not 11M paying subscribers.

⑪ ⭐ Grok’s Reported Pentagon Role

A Pentagon AI official’s sworn declaration reportedly describes Grok as part of Palantir’s Maven system.

The administration cited national-security concerns in litigation over xAI’s Memphis data center.

Grok’s precise role needs verification; this does not establish autonomous weapon targeting.

⑫ Neuralink: Musk Listed as CEO

Tesla’s latest proxy identifies Musk as Neuralink CEO, formalizing a title he has used before—not announcing a leadership change.

⑬ Musk on Grok Bot & Superintelligence

“Hire Grok Bot today. You won’t regret it,” Musk posted.

He also warned that highly persuasive superintelligence might sway anyone—even himself—in a single conversation.

Elon Daily 20261018

① 🔥 Cybercab Rear-Ended by Truck During Passenger Ride

On October 17, Twitch livestream footage of a Cybercab accident circulated on X. The vehicle was stopped at an Austin intersection, waiting to turn right, when it was rear-ended by a truck.

Passengers appeared unharmed, and the doors opened normally. Tesla’s remote support team checked on the passengers and assisted the vehicle in moving to a safer location.

The bigger story isn’t just the collision—it’s how a Cybercab with no steering wheel or onboard safety operator handles a real-world emergency.

There is currently no evidence that the Cybercab was at fault.

② ⭐ Driverless Cybercab Sightings Reach 87%

Community tracking data recorded 1,020 Cybercab sightings in Austin on October 17, with 889 operating without a driver—87% of all sightings, marking the third consecutive daily record.

③ ⭐ Alef Flying Car Challenges Tesla Roadster

California-based Alef released a video showing its prototype flying over a Cybertruck and an original Roadster, remaining airborne significantly longer than Tesla’s recent demonstration.

Alef declared: “Welcome to the flying car race—we’ve been here for 11 years.”

The video directly challenges Musk’s description of the new Roadster as a flying car.

The companies are pursuing different approaches: Alef emphasizes sustained flight, while Tesla combines automotive engineering with propulsion technology.

④ ⭐ Tesla × SpaceX: Employee Activity Fuels Merger Speculation

Over the past 48 hours, numerous Tesla and SpaceX employees reportedly began following one another on X. SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell also followed Tesla’s official account.

The timing is notable, with Tesla’s Q3 earnings call scheduled for October 21.

During September’s All-In podcast, Musk hinted at the possibility of further action involving the two companies.

No merger has been officially announced.

⑤ ⭐ Starlink: Ukraine Speed Restriction Dispute Escalates

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent rejected Ukrainian allegations on Sunday that Washington ordered Starlink speed restrictions, calling the claims irresponsible.

The controversy has renewed tensions over Starlink’s military use in Ukraine. Responsibility for the restrictions remains unresolved.

⑥ ⭐ US Warns EU Over Potential Starlink Restrictions

The Financial Times reports that US Ambassador to the EU Andrew Puzder warned of serious retaliation if Europe restricts satellite spectrum access for non-European operators.

The dispute involves spectrum needed for direct-to-cell satellite services and could directly affect Starlink’s expansion into Europe’s mobile communications market.

⑦ ⭐ SpaceX Prepares to Launch 32 Payloads, Including Starfall

SpaceX is targeting October 19 at 6:30 AM ET for its Bandwagon-5 mission, carrying 32 payloads, including the second demonstration flight of the Starfall reentry capsule.

Designed for microgravity research and in-space manufacturing, Starfall can reportedly carry approximately one metric ton of payload.

The launch remains pending, with a 55% probability of favorable weather.

⑧ Tesla Fatal Crash: NHTSA Report Confirms Autopilot Was Engaged

On October 18, media reports revisited Tesla’s regulatory filing concerning a fatal August 22 crash in Vineland, New Jersey.

Tesla’s Standing General Order (SGO) report listed the driver-assistance system as “Verified Engaged,” although police had not previously mentioned Autopilot.

The vehicle was traveling approximately 37 mph before striking a center median barrier.

Tesla redacted the software version and crash narrative.

Autopilot being engaged does not establish that the system caused the crash.

text:
Christ Brings Us into Communion with God: We  Must Be Spiritually Vigilant:
———
enakhena@reborn.com

(Memoria Sancti Pauli a Cruce)

Ephesians 2:12-22-
Key Verse- "For he is our peace, he made both one and broke down the dividing wall of enmity... So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God."  
Psalm 85:9-14-
Key Verse- "The Lord speaks of peace to his people."  
Luke 21:36- "Be vigilant at all times and pray that you may have the strength to stand before the Son of Man."  
 Luke 12:35-38-
Key Verse-"Gird your loins and light your lamps and be like servants who await their master's return from a wedding... Blessed are those servants whom the master finds vigilant on his arrival." 

In Ephesians 2:12-23 Apostle Paul reminds the Ephesians of their past state separated, alienated, and without hope. Through the Blood of Christ, the barrier between Gentiles and Jews was shattered, creating one unified body. In the Church, we are no longer foreigners or outsiders; we are built into a living temple with Christ as the chief cornerstone. Paul reminds us that through Jesus Christ, those who were once far from God have been brought near through the sacrifice of Christ. Sin separates humanity from God. Pride, hatred, prejudice, unforgiveness, jealousy, and selfish ambition also create divisions between people.However, Christ came to restore our relationship with God and to reconcile humanity with itself. Through His death on the cross, 

Jesus offers us the grace of reconciliation 
and invites us into a new relationship with God.Paul explains that we are no longer strangers but members of God’s household. Christ is the cornerstone upon which this spiritual household is built.This means that our Christian identity is not determined merely by our nationality, tribe, social class, education, financial status, or position in society. Our deepest identity is found in Christ. In Luke 12:35-28 Jesus uses the image of alert servants keeping lamps lit late into the night. "Girding your loins" meant tying up long garments to be ready for immediate action. Jesus promises an astounding reversal: when the Master returns and finds His servants awake, He will sit them down and serve them Himself. : 

Christ calls us to live with spiritual readiness, faithful service, and constant expectation of His coming. In biblical times, servants needed to remain prepared to respond to their master’s arrival. Their responsibility was not to predict the exact hour but to remain faithful while waiting. Likewise, Christians are not called to spend their lives speculating about the date of Christ’s return. Keeping our lamps burning symbolises maintaining the faith, love, prayer, hope, and obedience that enable us to recognise and welcome the Lord. Our spiritual lamps can become dim through persistent sin, pride, greed, unforgiveness, indifference, and neglect of prayer.However, through God’s grace, repentance, Scripture, & a renewed commitment to Christ, we can return to a life of spiritual attentiveness.

PRAYERS & MEDITATION 

Lord Jesus, keep my spiritual lamp burning.
Do not allow the distractions of this world to make me forget the purpose for which You have called me. When I become careless in prayer, awaken my heart. When temptation comes, strengthen my resolve to do what is right.
Heavenly Father, I thank You for the gift of this new day and for the grace You continue to pour into my life. Thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, to reconcile me to You and to bring me into Your family. Help me to understand the depth of Your love and to respond with a sincere heart.Remove everything within me that contradicts Your will. Teach me to live in peace with others, to remain faithful in difficult circumstances, and to recognise the opportunities You give me to serve. May my words, thoughts, and actions reflect the presence of Christ in my life. Amen

text:
For a company that only launched in January, Kirkland, Washington-based Skyband Systems is enjoying a remarkable trajectory in aviation, and is already poised to bring Iridium PNT into the cockpit.

Its M100 avionics unit, which keeps aircraft navigating when GPS and global navigation satellite system (GNSS) signals are disrupted or in question, has entered into production, and management is targeting U.S. FAA supplemental type certification (STC) on the prototype aircraft — an Embraer Praetor 600 — by as early as November.

A line replaceable unit, the M100 fuses independent onboard inertial sensing with Iridium’s positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) ASIC chip, which receives a cryptographically protected signal from Iridium’s 66-satellite Low Earth Orbit (LEO constellation.

Connecting to the aircraft’s existing Iridium antenna, the system delivers its output to the flight deck through an electronic flight bag (EFB) application and cockpit annunciator. This provides pilots with real-time GPS alerts and supplementary situational awareness.

“As GPS interference has grown into a daily concern for flight crews, Iridium PNT offers a signal that is resilient against jamming and spoofing. Skyband’s M100 brings that capability into the cockpit, and we are excited to see it reach production,” says Iridium CEO Matt Desch.

Bringing a brand new system to civil aviation at this pace is no small thing. But Skyband, whose leadership team comprises former Starlink Aviation engineers and executives, already knows the market. It’s also working with a highly respected FAA ODA, AeroMech, based in nearby Mukilteo.

Skyband is clearly cooking with gas. And so, RGN put the question to Skyband co-founder and president Robert Wiggenhorn: if the likes of Honeywell or Collins reached out to you guys and said, “We’d just like to snatch you up right now,” are you open to those types of conversations?

text:
🇺🇦⚔️🇺🇸 Zelensky tells U.S. lawmakers the Pentagon is delaying air defense missiles already paid for by partners. Washington denies changing intelligence sharing.

In a video call Monday with a bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers, Zelensky said the Pentagon is delaying Patriot interceptors paid for by European partners under the PURL program, with the shipment awaiting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature. He said European countries are also waiting for U.S. approval to transfer Patriot missiles from their own stocks, and that Ukraine received no U.S. warning before Russian ballistic missile strikes on three occasions in the past week. He said a political decision appears to have been made to slow support.

Zelensky also said Ukraine offered to stop striking Russian oil refineries for 30 days if the U.S. helped protect Ukrainian skies, and has heard no willingness. The U.S. denies changing intelligence sharing. The Pentagon did not respond to a Kyiv Independent request for comment.

These are Ukrainian claims. The "political decision" is Zelensky's inference, and the Hegseth delay rests on anonymous Ukrainian officials. The dispute follows U.S. pressure on Kyiv to halt refinery strikes over diesel prices ahead of U.S. midterms. Earlier Hegseth-ordered pauses on Ukraine aid in 2025 were reversed within days, but this one is not independently confirmed.

Sources: Reuters, Ukrinform, Kyiv Independent, AFP, Bloomberg

text:
The fact that people don't see the difference between between actors like Denzel Washington, Samuel L. Jackson, Cuba Gooding Jr, Wesley Snipes, Halle Berry and many others that made (put on the map not necessarily wrote) the characters they are known for or even did such a good job as the character that nobody even knew they weren't the original unless they saw it first.  And those that got a role simply because the studio was wanting to make the character not white. 

Not that they are less talented but it boxes them into a situation where unless they are revolutionary it is guaranteed to flop with anyone that wants substance over rampant virtue signaling. In a climate like that you get trash like lanterns that takes even a well established and beloved character like Jon Stewart and makes him unlikeable. You're literally saying out loud that black characters have to hit certain marks to be viable because racism when even my own racist father loved Denzel. We're talking about a man that hated black people so intensely because according the police at the time his father was shot and robbed after walking into his own home (whether that was the truth or not we'll never know because no one was ever caught or convicted but I honestly don't believe it) he thought that Denzel did such a good job that he saw past his own hatred and appreciated the stories he told with his characters. 

There's not a shot that anything recently could do the same. No one is taking a white character like Django making them black and setting them loose on a bunch of racists and slave owners and having racists in the audience cheering him on and on top of that doing such a phenomenal job that people prefer that version of the character. 

We aren't out here only wanting white characters, most of my favorite characters have been an even mix over the years, I was even disappointed when they went with Hal Jordan instead of Jon Stewart when they announced the Green Lantern movie, I actually ended up liking it and outside of the glowing suit I never really got why anyone didn't. 

I believe it all stems from a single lie. "You can only relate to people that look like you".

You might say, "well that is obviously false" and of course it is. But this is the blatant crap that has been shoved down the throats of all of us, young and old alike. It sickens me because it is gnawing away at our humanity. However I have seen an uptick in the last couple of years of people like the ones I grew up with, like the black man I used to go to church with named Michael. He stood out because he had the same name as my dad but he was the complete opposite inside and out. His is a smile that I will never forget, when I was going through some of the most chaotic times in my life he made me feel at home. Kinda wild considering that I had grown up in that church but many years and the divorce of my parents later and it didn't feel quite the same but every service he was the first face I looked for, I'd go get a dap and a hug and just talk for a moment. I didn't have anything to say, I couldn't relate to a grown man that was working hard and paying the bills keeping down a 9-5. But the love he showed me in those few fleeting moments helped me to keep my head up in spite of my circumstances.

He knew what a lot of us do, that the only thing that matters is our capacity for wielding the best that humanity has to offer and protecting our friends and neighbors from those who chose to wield its worst.

That is what the constitution is for, that is why we stand proudly against those that would seek to take away our God given rights. 

Your skin doesn't matter, tell a good story with what you have and people will respect it. And if they aren't then maybe you need to work on the plot.

text:
Claire Liu vs Magda Linette — the qualifier with the momentum

Preview · WTA 250 Osaka · First round · Tuesday 20 October 2026

Claire Liu came through qualifying in Osaka without dropping a set, and she now meets Magda Linette, the higher-ranked player but one whose recent results have gone the other way. The rankings separate them by only a handful of places, so the evidence has to come from elsewhere.

THE MATCHUP

The official rankings of 19 October have Linette at No. 77 and Liu at No. 95, a gap of 18 places. At that distance the number says very little about who should win. Linette, 34, is right-handed, stands 1.71m and has three career titles; Liu, 26, is also right-handed, stands 1.70m and has yet to win one.

They have met once, at Charleston in 2018 on clay, and Liu won 1-6 6-3 6-3 from a set down. That meeting came eight years ago on a different surface, so it is thin evidence, but it does sit in Liu's column.

FORM & CONTEXT

Liu has been winning matches. In September she took the title at a WTA 125 event in Barranquilla, beating Anna Blinkova 6-0 2-6 7-5 in the final. In Suzhou she beat Elsa Jacquemot 6-1 6-1 before losing to Rebecca Sramkova 7-5 6-4, and in Wuhan qualifying Lanlana Tararudee beat her 7-6(4) 6-4. She also lost to Mary Stoiana in Sao Paulo.

Her weekend in Osaka was tidy. On Saturday she beat the wildcard Kanon Sawashiro 6-1 6-1 in an hour and three minutes, and on Sunday she beat Maddison Inglis, the tenth seed in qualifying, 6-4 6-3 in an hour and 20 minutes.

Linette's recent run has been difficult. On 10 October Sinja Kraus beat her 7-6(3) 6-2 in Wuhan qualifying. Before that Katerina Siniakova beat her 6-4 6-3 in Beijing, and in Seoul she won the first set against Darya Astakhova 6-3 before losing the match in a final-set tie-break. At the US Open she lost to Francesca Jones in three sets, and in Cincinnati Elena-Gabriela Ruse beat her 6-0 6-3.

Both play on the same outdoor hard courts. Liu has two qualifying matches behind her here; that is a fact, not something that tips the context either way.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

Recent results. Liu has a title at WTA 125 level and two clean wins in Osaka qualifying, while the defeats to Kraus, Siniakova and Astakhova show how difficult Linette's autumn has been. With the ranking gap too small to mean much, the form of the last few weeks is the clearest guide on offer, and it points to the qualifier.

THE CALL

Liu's recent results and the one previous meeting both lean her way. The ranking gap is too narrow to count for either player, the old head-to-head came on clay, and the surroundings favour nobody, which keeps the confidence in the middle of the scale.

Claire Liu to win, medium confidence.

text:
Unidentified investors transferred 4.5 billion Kenya Pipeline Company shares worth Sh42.5 billion through the Nairobi Securities Exchange, moving 24.76 percent of the company’s stock. The transaction fell below the 25 percent threshold that would have required Capital Markets Authority approval. Rock Investment Bank handled the sale, while a client represented by KCB Capital bought the shares. A market report circulated by stockbrokers identified the parties as East African, but their identities remained unclear. The NSE said the transaction went through its dedicated block trading board, where individual transfers are capped at 24.99 percent of a company’s issued shares. KPC closed at Sh9.02, up 0.22 percent and close to its Sh9 initial public offering price.

The transfer puts attention on KPC’s major shareholders, including Uganda’s government, Kenya’s National Social Security Fund and the Public Servants Pension Scheme, although none was identified as a party to the trade. Confidential documents showed that Uganda and 13 State-backed pension schemes and agencies invested Sh95.8 billion in the IPO. NSSF bought Sh38.5 billion of shares, Uganda Sh33 billion and the Public Servants Pension Scheme Sh13 billion. The offer raised Sh112 billion, with subscriptions reaching 105.7 percent, before trading began on March 9. Regulatory filings show that 18 of KPC’s top 20 shareholders hold their stakes through nominee accounts, which register shares on behalf of their beneficial owners. NSSF and State agencies also split their holdings across several such accounts, obscuring their positions among the company’s largest shareholders.

Section 45(4) of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act, amended in September 2023, compels reporting institutions to verify the natural persons behind nominee accounts using independent evidence beyond the custodian’s identity. Regulation 25(2) of the 2023 anti-money laundering rules bars institutions from executing trades without upfront identity proof. Regulation 25(4) nevertheless permits intermediaries to defer beneficial ownership verification after a relationship begins to avoid interrupting normal business. Public registries still remain dark to retail investors. The block’s scale and KCB Capital’s role as a state counterparty point to a custodial rebalancing among the offering’s sovereign and pension anchors rather than a private entrant. Splitting that stake across nominees dodges the 25% buyout trigger under Regulation 3 of the 2002 takeover rules. Lawmakers must repeal Regulation 25(4) for block trades and amend Legal Notice No. 12 of February 2020 to mandate public beneficial ownership disclosure at a 5% threshold.

The nature of warfare has shifted; the world feels more vulnerable.

 We are seeing a "hybrid war of attrition" that begins long before a single missile is fired.

Before and during an armed confrontation, major powers establish a quiet, pre-positioned presence within an adversary’s networks:

Invisible sabotage: Dormant programs are installed within railway networks, airports, or seaports. Should a conflict escalate, these access points can be activated to obstruct the movement of troops or delay the arrival of humanitarian aid.

Intelligence gathering: Infiltrating technology providers and commercial satellite systems to monitor troop movements and strategic decision-making.

3. AI and the "War of Perception" (Psychological Warfare)

Cyberattacks do more than just destroy code; they shape public opinion:

AI-driven mass production of disinformation: Using deepfakes—fabricated videos and audio generated by artificial intelligence—attackers can impersonate political or military leaders to issue fake surrender orders or spread false news.

Social destabilization operations: The mass leaking of confidential data belonging to public figures or government institutions is used to stoke popular discontent and fracture the social contract during moments of vulnerability.

4. The Blurred Lines of "Undeclared Combat"

Unlike conventional weaponry, cyberspace offers near-total "plausible deniability":

States may employ hacktivist groups or cybercriminal syndicates to strike at rivals without openly claiming responsibility. This avoids triggering mutual defense pacts (such as NATO’s Article 5).

This strategy keeps rival nations in a state of perpetual, low-intensity conflict.

5.  "Cascade" Effect or Global Contagion

Due to global digital interconnectedness, a cyberattack designed to target a specific region often spirals out of control:

If a software provider with a global reach is compromised (a "supply chain attack"), the systems of companies, banks, and governments in countries entirely unrelated to the conflict can end up paralyzed as "collateral damage."

text:
From the Marquis de Lafayette, Hero of Two Worlds, to President Donald J. Trump

Château de La Grange, in the Year of Our Lord 2026 (though the post is slower than it was)

Monsieur le Président,

Permit an old soldier to take up his quill. Word reaches me, even here, that you have wondered aloud whether America owes Europe anything, and whether you would trouble yourself to save it. I write only to refresh a memory or two, as one does with old friends who have grown forgetful.

In 1777 I was nineteen years old. I bought a ship with my own money, sailed against the express wishes of my King, and offered to serve General Washington without pay. I was shot in the leg at Brandywine and wintered at Valley Forge, where the accommodations, I assure you, did not merit a single star. I did not ask the Continental Congress for a percentage.

At Yorktown, it was a French fleet under de Grasse that closed the Chesapeake, and French regiments under Rochambeau who stood beside yours while Cornwallis surrendered. My King spent so many livres on your independence that he went rather spectacularly bankrupt, and you will have heard how that ended for him. I mention this not to send an invoice, but because I understand you appreciate a good deal, and this was the finest one ever made by anyone, believe me.

I am told you also speak often of a “Russia hoax.” I must confess I took no part in it. In my day the only Russian interference in American affairs was the Empress Catherine’s League of Armed Neutrality, which, oddly enough, worked in your favor. Times change.

Allow me to continue the ledger. In 1886 we sent you a lady with a torch; I believe she still stands in your harbor, though I hear she has had some difficulty with the guest list lately. In 1917 your Colonel Stanton stood at my tomb and declared, “Lafayette, we are here.” I was very touched. In 1944 you came again, and France has not forgotten a single grave in Normandy. And when your towers fell in 2001, Europe invoked its pledge of mutual defense, the only time it has ever been used, on your behalf. Our soldiers followed yours to Afghanistan without asking who was paying.

So you see, Monsieur, the account between us is not a bill. It is a friendship, and like all friendships it is maintained by those who remember it. General Washington understood this. He named his son for me, which I note is more than any of your cabinet has done.

Should Europe one day find itself in difficulty, I do not ask that you sail a ship at your own expense, or take a musket ball in the leg. I ask only that you recall who arrived uninvited and unpaid when you were thirteen colonies, a debt, and a dream.

With the highest consideration, and a raised eyebrow,

Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette
 Major General, Continental Army (unpaid)
 Honorary Citizen of the United States, by Act of Congress
P.S. Mon cher Président, the French for “you’re welcome” is de rien. We have been saying it for 250 years.

text:
Another brilliant move on behalf of Carney’s “friends and family” benefits program.

Starlink is fully operational today with a massive consumer-focused network; Telesat Lightspeed is a planned enterprise/government system not expected to offer commercial service until early 2028.
Current status and scale
•  Starlink: ~11,000+ satellites in low Earth orbit (~550 km altitude), with ongoing rapid deployment (including new higher-capacity V3 satellites). It has roughly 12 million global subscribers and more than 500,000 users in Canada. Coverage reaches most of Canada, including remote and northern areas.
•  Telesat Lightspeed: 0 operational production satellites so far. The planned constellation is 225 satellites (recently expanded from ~156 due to a Canadian military contract). First pathfinder/production launches are targeted for December 2026 on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets, with global commercial service expected around Q1 2028. Orbits are higher (~1,000–1,300 km).
Target markets and service model
•  Starlink primarily serves residential/consumer users (plus mobile/RV “Roam,” aviation, maritime, and some enterprise). It is a direct-to-consumer best-effort broadband service. In Canada, residential plans typically run about $75–$150 CAD/month (tiered up to ~400 Mbps priority) with unlimited data and no long-term contracts; hardware is often available as a low-cost or free rental in many areas. Real-world speeds commonly fall in the 100–300+ Mbps range with ~20–40 ms latency.
•  Telesat Lightspeed is designed as a business-to-business (B2B) wholesale and enterprise system for telecom providers, governments, defence, aviation, and maritime users—not direct residential consumers. It emphasises guaranteed service-level agreements (SLAs), Carrier Ethernet (Layer 2) connectivity, optical inter-satellite links for routing control and data sovereignty, and military Ka-band spectrum. It aims to focus capacity where needed in real time and support high-latitude/Arctic operations. No public consumer pricing exists because it is not aimed at households.
Key practical differences
•  Availability and performance today: Starlink is usable now across Canada for homes, cottages, RVs, and remote sites. Telesat cannot replace it for residential users for years; even once live, it is expected to reach most end-users through local telecom partners rather than direct dish sales like Starlink.
•  Sovereignty and Canadian ties: Telesat is Ottawa-based, with substantial Canadian government funding (loans, equity, and a ~$2.3 billion Arctic military communications contract) and satellites built by MDA Space in Montreal. It markets features for secure, sovereign routing. However, a US investment firm owns a significant stake (~35%), and it depends on SpaceX for most launches. Starlink is fully US/SpaceX-controlled.
•  Capacity and economics: Starlink’s far larger constellation and vertical integration (own launches, manufacturing, and rapid iteration) give it a major scale advantage and lower per-bit costs. Telesat’s smaller, higher-orbit design prioritises enterprise-grade reliability, SLAs, and specialised military use over mass consumer volume.
In short, for anyone needing satellite internet in Canada right now (or the next couple of years), Starlink is the practical option. Telesat Lightspeed is positioned as a future sovereign/enterprise alternative, particularly valuable for government and defence needs in the Arctic and elsewhere, but it will not be a direct near-term substitute for Starlink’s consumer service.

text:
@drewmassman I wouldn't be so quick to declare that a Mars colony will never happen.

Throughout Elon Musk's (@elonmusk) career, people have questioned whether his ambitions were realistic. Some of his goals were considered nearly impossible, yet look at what his companies have accomplished.

🚀 Reusable rockets: SpaceX successfully landed a Falcon 9 booster in 2015 and reused one in 2017. Today, rocket reuse is routine for SpaceX.

🚀 Private spacecraft reaching the ISS: In 2012, SpaceX became the first commercial company to send a spacecraft to the International Space Station.

🚀 Private companies launching astronauts: In 2020, SpaceX's Crew Dragon carried NASA astronauts into orbit, restoring America's ability to launch astronauts from American soil.

🚀 Falcon Heavy: Successfully launched in 2018, with its two side boosters landing simultaneously.

🚗 High-performance electric cars: Tesla's Roadster entered production in 2008, demonstrating that electric vehicles could offer impressive performance.

🚗 Mass-producing electric vehicles: Tesla delivered approximately 1.64 million vehicles in 2025.

🛰️ Satellite internet: Starlink grew into a global internet service, reporting approximately 10.3 million subscribers by March 2026.

Now, does any of this prove that humans will successfully colonize Mars? Of course not.

Radiation, toxic soil, extreme temperatures, the lack of a breathable atmosphere, and the challenges of producing food, water, and energy are enormous obstacles.

But here's something I've learned from watching technological progress throughout my lifetime: There's a big difference between something being impossible and something being beyond our current capabilities.

Think about how much technology has advanced in just the past 50 years. Now imagine what another 50 or 100 years of advancements in robotics, artificial intelligence, materials science, medicine, and space exploration might accomplish.

Elon (@elonmusk) has certainly made predictions that haven't worked out on his original timelines. Some of his ideas may never succeed. But his companies have repeatedly demonstrated that ambitious engineering goals can become reality, even when success seems unlikely.

Personally, I'd rather encourage people to attempt what seems impossible than tell them they shouldn't bother trying.

I'd also be interested in hearing which obstacle Elon (@elonmusk) considers the greatest challenge to establishing a permanent human settlement on Mars.

What does everyone else think? Will humanity eventually establish a permanent settlement on Mars, or are there obstacles that technology simply cannot overcome?

text:
UNC Football: Bill Belichick Previews Syracuse, Reflects on Duke Victory and Discusses Team Development
Key Takeaways from Bill Belichick's Press Conference
🍊 Syracuse is better than its record suggests: Belichick praised Syracuse head coach Fran Brown and his coaching staff, emphasizing that the Orange have been competitive in every game and are only a few plays away from having a significantly better record.
🛡️ Syracuse presents a challenging defense: Belichick highlighted the Orange's disruptive defensive line, athletic linebackers and versatile secondary. Syracuse uses multiple defensive looks and pressure packages designed to confuse opponents and create turnovers.
🏈 Four capable quarterbacks create an unusual challenge: Belichick said he could not recall coaching against a team with four quarterbacks who were all legitimate contributors. Syracuse has demonstrated the ability to move the football effectively regardless of which quarterback plays.
⚡ Syracuse possesses an explosive offense: The Orange can generate yardage through rushing, short passes, deep throws and play-action plays. Belichick praised offensive coordinator Jeff Nixon for successfully managing the team's changing personnel.
💪 Syracuse's offensive line is exceptionally large: Belichick described the Orange's offensive line as potentially one of the biggest in college football, with several players weighing approximately 350 pounds. Its size and experience present significant challenges for UNC's defensive front.
🎯 Syracuse's receiving weapons demand attention: Belichick identified Hatcher as a primary receiving target, praised tight end Dante's speed and explosiveness, and highlighted freshman receiver Russell following his breakout performance against Louisville.
🔄 Special teams could influence the outcome: Syracuse has two dangerous return specialists, giving the Orange opportunities to generate explosive plays and favorable field position.
🌟 Greg Smith's development earns praise: Belichick commended the former high school quarterback for improving his speed, instincts, anticipation, tackling and defensive understanding. Smith's versatility allows him to cover receivers, defend tight ends and contribute near the line of scrimmage.
🧠 Communication is essential in UNC's secondary: Belichick emphasized that safeties must coordinate defensive assignments, communicate coverage adjustments and ensure teammates understand their responsibilities. Smith's ability to handle multiple safety positions has increased his value.
📈 Freshman defensive back Kent Do continues improving: Belichick praised Do's physicality, tackling ability and growing understanding of UNC's defensive system. Although Do has benefited from additional playing opportunities because of injuries, Belichick said he still has considerable room for development.
🏋️ Consistency and discipline remain UNC's biggest priorities: Belichick said the Tar Heels are improving through daily work on fundamentals, preparation, communication and toughness. The next challenge is executing consistently throughout all 60 minutes.
🔁 Injuries create opportunities for younger players: Belichick stressed the importance of the next-man-up mentality. Injuries have allowed reserves to demonstrate their abilities, while competition from younger players pushes established starters to maintain their performance.
🏆 UNC's victory over Duke was an emotional milestone: Belichick acknowledged that reclaiming the Victory Bell made it more difficult than usual to move immediately to the next opponent. However, players and coaches recognized the importance of shifting their attention to Syracuse.
🔔 Victory Bell tradition was a new experience for Belichick: The coach enjoyed participating in UNC's celebration, including taking the bell to the campus bell tower, painting it and ringing it. He emphasized that the tradition predates his arrival and was especially meaningful for the players and seniors.
📅 UNC must quickly refocus on Syracuse: Belichick compared weekly preparation to emptying the tank during a game and refilling it throughout the following week. Physical recovery, film study, communication and practice execution are essential to maintaining momentum.
🩺 Injury evaluations will continue throughout the week: Belichick declined to provide definitive availability updates before players returned to practice. He explained that medical evaluations, rehabilitation and practice participation determine whether injured players can contribute, with some decisions potentially extending to game day.
🚍 Road victories build experience, but location is secondary: Asked about UNC's success away from home, including wins in Ireland and Durham, Belichick emphasized that preparation, execution, effort and attitude matter more than the stadium or environment.
⏱️ Situational football determines close ACC games: Belichick emphasized that winning often depends on execution during critical moments, including two-minute drives, four-minute situations, goal-line stands, field goals and special-teams plays.
🏟️ Belichick downplayed questions about playoff expansion: Asked about a possible 14-team College Football Playoff, Belichick said he has no decision-making authority over the format and declined to offer a substantive opinion.
🧱 Center mobility provides additional offensive options: Belichick explained how having a center capable of pulling and blocking on the perimeter creates better blocking angles. He emphasized the center's responsibility for identifying defensive alignments and coordinating offensive-line assignments.
🤕 No player is completely healthy midway through the season: Belichick acknowledged that injuries, soreness and illnesses are unavoidable after months of practices and games. He praised players who invest additional time in treatment, rehabilitation and strength training to remain competitive.
🏅 Belichick isn't concerned with labels for UNC's victories: Asked about the description of recent wins as "double chicken," Belichick said he was unfamiliar with the expression. His priority remains straightforward: score more points than the opponent.
🔥 UNC's challenge is sustaining momentum: Following consecutive victories, including the emotional rivalry win over Duke, Belichick wants the Tar Heels to maintain their preparation, discipline and competitive intensity rather than become distracted by recent success.
