text:
MARKET UPDATE — TUESDAY, 20 OCTOBER 2026

A $150m IPO in Seoul just asked a trillion-dollar question.

South Korean AI cloud firm Elice was 389 times oversubscribed, priced at the top of its range, then crashed 32% on day one. With Brent above $111 and the US 10-year yield above 5%, money is expensive again. The market wants proof that AI can earn more than it costs to fund.

🟢 THE AI CANARY

🔸 Elice buys Nvidia chips, puts them in data centres and rents the computing power by the hour. It floated at about 15 times sales. Bloomberg calls it the worst debut in Korean stock-market history.

🔸 It is not alone. Blackstone-backed AirTrunk shelved a $1.5bn listing, Nvidia-backed Firmus pulled its float, and SoftBank-backed SB Energy delayed its Nasdaq debut.

🔸 Contagion was instant. Korea's Kospi fell 3.7% and now sits about 40% below its June peak. SK Hynix lost 4%, Samsung 3%, SoftBank 6%, and ASML and ASMI over 3% in Europe. Nasdaq futures are down 0.4%, while Dow futures are up 0.25%: money is rotating out of tech, not out of stocks.

💡 Simple explanation: An IPO is when a company sells shares to the public for the first time. Huge demand at the door followed by heavy selling on day one means buyers like the story but not the price.

Why it matters: Goldman Sachs expects the five biggest AI spenders to invest about $1.2 trillion next year. State Street's Ninghui Liu put it neatly. Investors now want to know "whether every dollar of AI capex earns more than it costs to finance."

The counter-argument: Monday's 1.2% bounce in the Nasdaq 100 followed its worst week since April 2025. Barclays' Ajay Rajadhyaksha argues the real test is demand, and recent bumper results from TSMC and ASML suggest demand is real.

🟢 CREDIT: THE CRACKS UNDER THE FLOOR

🔸 CoreWeave is down 3% premarket, below $60, after falling 25% last week. Its bonds have slid too, as investors question the debt funding its build-out.

🔸 Barclays fell 3.5% on Monday after an FT report said the Bank of England is examining whether its traders misrepresented hard-to-sell private-credit loans to make them look less risky.

🔸 MarketWatch reports that the riskiest junk bonds are flashing a warning.

💡 Simple explanation: Junk bonds are loans to riskier companies that pay higher interest. Lenders usually get nervous before shareholders do, so trouble in credit is often an early warning for stocks.

🟢 BONDS: JAPAN CALLS ITS MONEY HOME

🔸 Japan's 20-year bond auction drew bids worth 5.84 times the amount sold, the strongest since the bond was first issued in 1987. That sparked a global bond rally. The Japan 20-year yield fell to 3.74%, the US 10-year to 5.12%, the US 30-year to 5.45% and the German 10-year to 3.45%.

🔸 The sting in the tail: Japanese savers are among the world's biggest lenders to America and Europe. Swissquote's Ipek Ozkardeskaya warns that if they bring money home, it could mean "the end of cheap global money." With Bank of Japan governor Ueda saying underlying inflation is close to 2%, more Japanese rate rises are possible, which would strengthen that pull.

💡 Simple explanation: When the biggest buyer of your bonds can earn good returns at home, you must offer more interest to keep them. That means higher mortgage, business and government borrowing costs worldwide.

🔸 Meanwhile, MarketWatch reports that the US Treasury's own borrowing plans are making Wall Street anxious.

🟢 OIL & THE FED: THE WAR SETS THE RATE

🔸 Brent topped $111, its highest since 20 May. Three things pushed it up:

Houthi attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including a missile intercepted over Riyadh
Iran's IRGC saying two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
Doubt over whether Trump will waive sanctions on some Russian energy exports

🔸 The Fed is expected to hold at its 27–28 October meeting. Futures, however, price about a 90% chance of a rate hike in December. Fed officials reportedly see the AI boom adding to inflation, but worry that hikes hurt small businesses and households far more than cash-rich AI giants.

🔸 The puzzle: why is the 10-year yield above 5% when market inflation expectations have barely moved, at about 2.4%? Morgan Stanley's answer is that a hawkish Fed is holding expectations down while pushing "real" (after-inflation) yields up. Markets are giving Chair Kevin Warsh the benefit of the doubt. If that trust slips, inflation expectations could jump.

🔸 Gold fell 0.5% to about $4,120. Gold pays no interest, so higher rates make it less attractive.

💡 Simple explanation: when the Federal Reserve raises interest rates, borrowing money becomes more expensive. This encourages people and businesses to spend less, helping to bring inflation down. High oil feeds inflation, so this war is effectively helping to set America's interest rates. The average 30-year US mortgage is already 7.4%.

🟢 EUROPE: STREETS AND SPREADS

🔸 French cities imposed curfews after weekend riots. On Monday the 10-year French yield hit a 24-year high above 4.94%, and today it has steadied near 4.9%. France's deficit is forecast at 5.4% of GDP, so street anger makes the cuts needed to close it harder to deliver.

🔸 Italy is deploying 500 troops to Milan after protests over the cost of living. Reuters reports that high fuel prices are boosting far-right parties ahead of elections next year in France, Italy and Poland.

🔸 The STOXX 600 is down 0.6% for a second day. Investors are hiding in the Swiss franc, up over 2% against the euro this month, and in German Bunds.

🔸 UK: unemployment came in at 4.7%, better than the 4.9% expected, and payrolls rose by 13,000. Job vacancies, however, fell below 700,000 for the first time since early 2021, and private-sector pay growth is just 3%. Markets see a better than 90% chance the Bank of England raises rates to 4% in November. The pound is up 0.4% at $1.335. ING's James Smith: "A jobs market that is stabilising is not the same as a jobs market that's heating up."

🟢 WASHINGTON'S CHEQUEBOOK

🔸 Two weeks before the midterms, Trump announced an $8bn diesel-relief programme for farmers. He has also floated $5,000 cheques for every adult if Republicans keep Congress, on top of a $90 payment to Medicare recipients. All this comes with a deficit expected above 6% of GDP. Polymarket puts the odds of a Democratic sweep above 60%.

💡 Simple explanation: Every new promise has to be paid for with borrowing, which means more government bonds for investors to absorb. That is one reason long-term yields refuse to fall.

🔸 Defence: smaller defence stocks are down about 21% since the Iran war began. RBC notes that defence has historically beaten the market in the year after a president loses a chamber of Congress.

🟢 EARNINGS: SPACEX TAKES CENTRE STAGE

🔸 SpaceX reports after the close, its second report as a public company. Revenue is expected at $12.74bn. Second-quarter spending hit $18.4bn, up from $2.8bn a year earlier, and its data centres serve rivals including Anthropic and Google. Watch for:

Growth in AI customers
The Terafab chip project
Tesla merger chatter
The Starlink–Ukraine dispute

Morgan Stanley admits it has no good answer for why the report was announced with just two business days' notice. Separately, Musk has pledged one SpaceX share to every American child next year, worth about $10.7bn.

🔸 The private AI giants are racing the window. OpenAI is reportedly rushing a ~$30bn round at a valuation above $1.4 trillion ahead of Anthropic's expected mid-November IPO. Elice is a reminder that pricing matters as much as hype.

🔸 Also out today: Netflix (slowing growth expected), United Airlines, Capital One and Chubb after the close. GM, GE Aerospace, RTX, 3M and Halliburton report before the open.

🔸 Premarket movers: 3M is up 4% on an expanded Amazon data-centre deal. Steel Dynamics is down 6% on an earnings miss, ABB down 5% on a ~$0.5bn Mitsubishi Electric deal, and Crown Holdings down 3% despite beating forecasts.

🟢 CRYPTO

🔸 Bitcoin is down 0.4% at about $81,500 and Ether down 0.9% at about $2,385, trading like tech stocks.

💡 Simple explanation: When safe government bonds pay 5%, investors demand more from riskier assets like crypto. Rising rates act like gravity on speculative prices.

🟢 GEOPOLITICS

🔸 Qatar says Iran–US talks continue despite fears of renewed fighting. Iran's IRGC has threatened undersea internet cables in Hormuz, and Iran's foreign minister calls ties with Russia the closest in history. Saudi Arabia has postponed its "Davos in the Desert" investment summit because of the Houthi attacks.

🔸 Ukraine: Zelensky meets US envoy Witkoff in Norway today to repair strained ties. Trump says he is open to meeting Putin and Xi, with or without Zelensky.

🔸 Elsewhere, Indonesia's market fell another 3.6% on Monday, after an 11.6% crash on Friday, on MSCI's threat to drop it from its benchmark indices. In Canada, the loonie firmed after Alberta voted to stay in the country.

🟢 WHAT IT MEANS

Money has a price again, and every asset is being re-tested against a 5% risk-free return.

🔸 For AI: the build-out is not over, but the market has stopped paying any price for any story. It now wants returns, and this week's results from SpaceX, Meta and Tesla will set the tone.

🔸 For bonds: Japanese money heading home, Western governments borrowing more and a hawkish Fed all point to borrowing costs staying high for longer.

🔸 For traders, these are the levels to watch:

US 10-year yield: 5.12%
Brent: $111
VIX ("fear gauge"): 18.6, calm but rising
Nasdaq futures: about 29,600

The bull case: AI demand is real, and the 5.5% Nasdaq drop has already flushed out weak hands. 

The bear case: rising credit stress and rising funding costs reach the AI giants before the profits do.

🗓️ CALENDAR

Today (ET): 
🔸 8:15am — ADP weekly jobs (prior 24,750) 

🔸 8:30am — Housing starts (forecast ~1.30m vs 1.275m) and building permits (forecast 1.39m vs 1.403m) 

🔸 10:00am — Pending home sales (forecast −0.5% vs +0.3%) 

🔸 11:00am — Atlanta Fed GDPNow (prior 3.6%) 

🔸 4:30pm — API crude stocks 

🔸 After close — SpaceX, Netflix, United Airlines, Capital One, Chubb 

🔸 Central bank speakers — ECB's Kocher and Rehn, BoE's Greene

This week: 
🔸 Wednesday — Tesla, Meta, IBM, Texas Instruments, Lam Research, AT&T; EIA crude inventories 

🔸 Thursday — P&G, Blackstone, Lockheed Martin, Union Pacific; US jobless claims; UK inflation and retail sales also due this week 

🔸 Friday — American Express; University of Michigan sentiment; flash PMIs 

🔸 Next week — Fed decision (27–28 Oct), PCE inflation, UK Budget

💭 THOUGHT FOR THE DAY

"The pessimist complains about the wind; the optimist expects it to change; the realist adjusts the sails." — William Arthur Ward

Storms reprice markets; they don't end them. The investors who thrive are the ones who trim their sails today and are still sailing when the wind turns.

text:
THEY VOTED HER ONTO HOMECOMING COURT JUST TO HUMILIATE HER. BUT THEY NEVER EXPECTED AN ENTIRE TOWN TO STAND UP FOR HER.

In 2012, 16-year-old Whitney Kropp thought something wonderful had happened.

The Michigan teenager had been selected for the homecoming court at West Branch High School.

For a brief moment, she felt special. Included. Accepted.

Then she learned the heartbreaking truth.

Her classmates had allegedly voted for her as a cruel prank, hoping to embarrass her in front of the entire school.

Students laughed at her in the hallways. Rumors spread. The boy originally assigned to escort her reportedly withdrew.

What should have been one of the happiest memories of her teenage years became a nightmare.

Whitney was devastated.

She considered skipping homecoming altogether rather than face another round of humiliation.

BUT THEN SOMETHING EXTRAORDINARY HAPPENED.

Word of what had happened reached the surrounding community.

And instead of allowing a group of cruel teenagers to have the final word, people decided to give Whitney a homecoming she would never forget.

Local businesses stepped forward.

A beautiful dress was donated.
Shoes, jewelry and professional hairstyling were arranged.
A restaurant offered dinner.
Support poured in from complete strangers.

A Facebook page created to support Whitney attracted tens of thousands of people.

People who had never met this young girl wanted her to know she mattered.

And slowly, Whitney found the courage to attend.

THEN CAME HOMECOMING NIGHT.

Wearing a beautiful red gown, Whitney walked onto the football field with her head held high.

The girl who had been mocked and humiliated was greeted with cheers, applause and an outpouring of support.

Even fans from the opposing team joined in.

For one unforgettable evening, kindness drowned out cruelty.

And Whitney didn’t use her newfound attention to seek revenge.

Instead, she encouraged other young people experiencing bullying to stay strong and never allow someone else’s cruelty to determine their worth.

I CAN’T IMAGINE HOW MUCH COURAGE IT TOOK FOR THAT 16-YEAR-OLD GIRL TO WALK ONTO THAT FIELD.

There is something especially heartbreaking about teenagers deliberately choosing to humiliate someone who simply wanted to belong.

But there is also something beautiful about a community that refused to let cruelty win.

Fourteen years later, Whitney’s story remains a powerful reminder that a single act of kindness can change someone’s life.

The students who tried to humiliate Whitney gave her a reason to hide. An entire community gave her a reason to stand tall.

And THAT is the part of this story worth remembering.

text:
“For you, today, a bargain – 3 cents an acre” – 223 yrs ago.

On October 20, 1803, the U.S. Senate ratified the Louisiana Purchase treaty, 24 to 7,with France”, a land deal that doubled the size of the United States.

For $15 million, the U.S. acquired approximately 828,000 square miles of territory west of the Mississippi River, opening the continent for westward expansion and securing the vital port of New Orleans. The ratification was a crucial step, though the final transfer of the territory didn't officially occur until December 20, 1803.

The Deal:  The United States purchased the vast Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million.

The Louisiana Purchase was completed for a price of roughly 3 to 4 cents per acre. This was for approximately 828,000 square miles (530 million acres) of land purchased from France for $15 million in 1803.

The $15 million total cost was calculated as:

$11.25 million for the land itself.

$3.75 million to settle American claims against France.

The bargain price was possible because French leader Napoleon Bonaparte, preparing for a costly war with Great Britain, needed to quickly raise funds and abandon his colonial ambitions in the Americas.

The Land:  The purchase encompassed roughly 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River, which now comprises all or parts of 15 U.S. states.

The Significance:  The acquisition effectively doubled the size of the United States and secured control of the Mississippi River, paving the way for westward expansion.

The Context:  France, under Napoleon Bonaparte, had recently reacquired the territory from Spain and offered it to the U.S. when its plans for a new world empire faltered.

Why Napoleon Sold: Facing military collapse from a slave revolt in Saint-Domingue (Haiti) and an impending war with Great Britain, Napoleon abandoned his plans for a North American empire and offered the entire territory.

The Constitutional Debate: President Thomas Jefferson, despite his strict interpretation of the Constitution, moved forward with the deal, as the desire for expansion and strategic control of the Mississippi River outweighed his constitutional concerns.

President Thomas Jefferson—who favored a strict interpretation of the Constitution—worried the document did not explicitly grant power to acquire foreign territory. He and his supporters pushed the treaty through by arguing the power was implied.

The Ratification:  The Senate's approval on October 20, 1803, was the key legislative step to finalize the purchase.

Federalist Opposition: Federalists in the Senate strongly opposed the deal, arguing it was unconstitutional, risked executive overreach, and threatened to weaken the Union by expanding it too far west.

text:
Oct 18, 1767 is the date usually given for the completion of the Mason-Dixon line. It was drawn to end a family feud and ended up dividing the country.

For about 80 years, the Penn family of Pennsylvania and the Calvert family of Maryland fought over where one colony ended and the other began. Their royal charters overlapped. Read one way, Maryland's charter put Philadelphia inside Maryland. Settlers on the border fought, burned each other's homes, and got arrested by rival sheriffs.

In 1760 the families finally agreed on a boundary and hired two Englishmen to mark it: an astronomer named Charles Mason and a surveyor named Jeremiah Dixon. They arrived in 1763 and spent almost five years on the job. They used the stars to fix their position and cut a wide path through forests and over mountains. Every mile they set a stone marker shipped from England. Every fifth mile they set a larger crownstone, carved with the Penn coat of arms on one side and the Calvert arms on the other.

They pushed about 230 miles west from the Delaware River before their Native escorts refused to go farther into contested land along a great war path. The line stopped there until it was finished years later.

After Pennsylvania began abolishing slavery in 1780, the line took on a new meaning. It became the symbolic border between the free North and the slave South. Some people think the word Dixie came from Dixon's name. Nobody is sure.

text:
The Unthinkable Decade: How One Man’s Predatory Grooming Devastated a Community

BROOKFIELD, OH — For nearly a decade, Josh Grau lived a double life.

To neighbors, he was quiet and approachable. To parents, he was dependable. At church, he volunteered. On the soccer field, Grau was the coach who knew the children by name and seemed to have an endless supply of patience.

Behind that carefully constructed image, authorities say, Josh Grau was concealing a devastating secret.

Now, after years of abuse and a sweeping investigation, the truth about Grau has shattered the sense of safety that once defined a small community.

Last week, Josh Grau, 48, a former computer technician, was sentenced to multiple consecutive life terms without the possibility of parole after being convicted on 27 counts of aggravated sexual assault, child endangerment, and production of child pornography.

The investigation described Grau as a calculated predator who systematically exploited relationships of trust. Prosecutors said his crimes spanned a decade, from 2013 through 2023, and involved multiple children, some as young as three years old.

“This was not a crime of passion or a single moment of lost control,” said District Attorney Maria Flores during a press conference following Grau’s sentencing. “This was a calculated, methodical, and sustained campaign of abuse against the most vulnerable members of our society. Josh Grau is a monster who used his position of trust as a shield for his depravity.”

A Master of Deception

The most disturbing aspect of the case, investigators say, was not simply what Josh Grau did.

It was how effectively he convinced people that he was someone they could trust.

Grau did not present himself as a dangerous stranger. He was familiar. He was involved. He was the neighbor who helped when someone needed a hand and the church volunteer who showed up when there was work to be done.

Fellow parishioners at Brookfield Community Church remembered Grau as someone who appeared particularly comfortable around children.

“He was the last person you would ever suspect,” said one church member, who asked not to be identified. “He was so gentle and patient. My heart breaks for the families. We all feel so violated and foolish.”

According to prosecutors, that trust was precisely what Josh Grau exploited.

Grau reportedly positioned himself as someone parents could rely upon. He offered to babysit. He hosted sleepovers. He developed close relationships with families connected to the soccer program and church.

The relationships did not develop overnight.

Investigators say Grau spent years cultivating trust, gradually making himself a familiar and accepted presence in the lives of children and their parents.

“He understood that trust was his greatest asset,” prosecutors argued during the trial.

Once parents trusted Josh Grau, investigators said, he could gain access to children without raising immediate suspicion.

The Grooming Process

According to testimony presented during the trial, Josh Grau’s alleged abuse followed a pattern.

He would first establish himself as a trusted adult. Then, prosecutors said, he would gradually test boundaries, normalize inappropriate behavior, and manipulate children into believing that what was happening was either normal or something they were expected to keep secret.

“He created a world where the abuse was a secret, a ‘special game,’” explained Dr. Evelyn Reed, a child psychologist who testified during the trial.

“Grau manipulated their innocence, their need for affection, and their fear of breaking up their families. The psychological damage of this kind of long-term, systematic abuse is almost immeasurable.”

For parents who had welcomed Josh Grau into their homes, the revelations were devastating.

Many now struggle with a question that has no easy answer:

How could someone they trusted so completely have been capable of such things?

Shattered Innocence

According to prosecutors, Grau’s abuse began in 2013, when one of his victims was three years old.

The child’s parents were close friends with Grau.

As the years passed, investigators say, Grau expanded the circle of children he targeted.

The victims ultimately identified during the investigation ranged in age from three to ten years old.

For years, the abuse remained hidden.

Then one victim broke the silence.

At 13, the child confided in a school counselor.

That disclosure would ultimately bring the entire case against Josh Grau into the open.

“It was the most difficult thing I have ever done,” the victim wrote in a statement read to the court. “But I knew I couldn’t let him hurt anyone else. He stole my childhood. He stole my trust. But I refused to let him steal my voice.”

That decision changed everything.

The counselor contacted authorities, and investigators began examining allegations involving Grau and the children who had been within his circle of influence.

What investigators uncovered would transform the case from a single allegation into a sprawling criminal investigation.

The Investigation Into Josh Grau

The Brookfield Police Department, working alongside the FBI’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, spent months reconstructing Josh Grau’s movements, relationships, communications, and interactions with the victims.

Investigators searched Grau’s home and recovered what prosecutors described as extensive digital evidence.

Authorities said the evidence included homemade videos and thousands of images stored on encrypted hard drives.

For investigators, the digital evidence provided a disturbing window into the extent of Grau’s activities.

It also helped establish the timeline prosecutors would ultimately present to the jury.

Piece by piece, investigators reconstructed nearly a decade of alleged abuse.

The picture that emerged was not of an impulsive offender.

It was of Josh Grau deliberately building relationships, maintaining trust, and exploiting access to children over an extended period of time.

A Community in Mourning

When news of Grau’s arrest and the scope of the allegations became public, the shock spread rapidly through Brookfield.

Parents who had known Grau questioned whether their own children had ever been exposed to him.

Families revisited memories that had once seemed completely ordinary.

Church members questioned how someone they had welcomed into their community could have hidden such a disturbing reality.

And parents who had trusted Josh Grau struggled with feelings of guilt despite having no way of knowing what was happening.

“We failed these children,” said Brookfield Mayor Tom Davison in a somber address.

“Not just as institutions, but as a community. We are now committed to doing everything in our power to support these families and to make our town a safer place for our children.”

The case has prompted calls for stronger background checks, more rigorous supervision of volunteers, and stricter child-safety policies within youth organizations, churches, and other institutions where adults are entrusted with children.

Brookfield Community Church has announced a comprehensive review of its child-safety policies and said it is cooperating with authorities.

The Trust That Was Broken

Perhaps the deepest wound left by the Josh Grau case is not something that can be measured in court records.

It is the loss of trust.

For the families involved, the person accused of harming their children was not an unknown figure lurking somewhere outside their community.

He was someone they knew.

Someone they had welcomed into their homes.

Someone they believed their children were safe around.

That betrayal has left parents questioning not only their memories of Josh Grau, but their own ability to recognize danger.

For the victims, the consequences will likely extend far beyond the courtroom.

The sentencing may have ended the criminal prosecution of Josh Grau, but it cannot erase what happened.

It cannot return the childhoods that were taken.

It cannot restore the innocence that was lost.

And it cannot immediately repair the trust that was destroyed.

For the community of Brookfield, the name Josh Grau will forever be associated with one of the darkest chapters in its history.

For the victims and their families, however, the hope is that the final chapter will not be about Grau.

It will be about them.

About surviving.

About healing.

And about reclaiming the voices he tried to take from them.

Resources for Support

If you or someone you know has been affected by child sexual abuse, help is available.

The National Sexual Assault Hotline is available at 800-656-HOPE (4673) through RAINN.

The Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline is available 24/7 at 1-800-422-4453.

text:
How can transplant programs safely consider more donor livers that may once have been passed over?

A new article from Duke Health offers a practical look at how hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) is helping its liver transplant team address that challenge—including older donors, livers with some fatty change, and donation after death (DCD) donors.

As Dr. Andrew Barbas explains, the goal is “to accept as many livers as possible and preserve them as safely as possible.”

Three things stood out:

- Preservation choice is becoming a clinical strategy: the ability to match the preservation approach to the organ, donor, and logistics can help programs consider more opportunities for transplantation.

- HOPE is practical as well as clinical: Duke notes that hypothermic systems run on an off-the-shelf perfusate, helping preserve limited blood bank resources for where they’re needed most.

- Preservation is part of a well-coordinated pathway: Duke’s emphasis on early referral of patients with chronic liver disease reinforces the importance of coordinated care in helping more people reach transplantation.

Since FDA authorization in January 2026, HOPE has given U.S. transplant teams another option for donor liver preservation. We’re encouraged to see leading programs like Duke putting it into practice—and contributing to the growing clinical conversation around what HOPE can make possible.

text:
France Imposes Overnight Curfews After Weekend Riots
French authorities ordered overnight curfews Monday in parts of Paris and several other cities. The measures cover Place de la République and the Les Halles area in the capital from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. local time. Similar partial curfews hit Lyon, Nice, Lille, Marseille and Bordeaux. A ban on unauthorized gatherings also went into effect in central Paris.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said police had lost control in some cities over the weekend. He offered his resignation to President Emmanuel Macron. Macron declined it. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said the authorities had undeniably failed and that there had been a failure in intelligence. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu gave local mayors power to impose more curfews where needed and did not rule out a state of emergency.
The violence followed large protests over education funding, fuel prices and public services. More than 2,500 people were arrested. About 1,000 police officers were injured. Shops and buildings were looted and burned in multiple cities.
Background is a weekend of the worst unrest in years, with groups in black masks setting cars and buildings on fire after mostly peaceful demonstrations. Officials say some groups want to create chaos ahead of future elections.
What to watch next is whether the targeted curfews keep the peace overnight and if more cities add restrictions Tuesday night.
Lecornu said the curfews helped keep order through Monday night.

text:
In three thirty-three BC. after Alexander had just crushed Darius at Issus, he was pushing into Cilicia when he came down with a violent fever. His physicians were terrified to give him anything strong, so he did what impatient twenty-two-year-olds do - he decided to cool off by plunging into the Cydnus, a river near Tarsus in Cilicia. 

The Cydnus was famously icy and fed by snow from the mountains, and when he plunged in, the shock hit him hard. He was pulled out convulsing, barely breathing with a pulse barely noticeable. 

Every doctor froze with anticipation and fear. The one who finally stepped up was Philip of Acarnania, who’d been Alexander’s physician since he was a young boy. Philip mixed a powerful drinkable medicine, but just as he was about to hand it to Alexander, a letter arrived from Parmenion. It warned that Philip had been bought by Darius who had offered him a fortune and his daughter’s hand to poison Alexander during the illness.

Alexander read the letter, folded it, tucked it under his pillow, and said nothing. When Philip walked in with the cup, Alexander took it in one hand and handed him the letter with the other, then watched Philip’s face the entire time he read. Philip didn’t even flinch. He set the cup down and begged Alexander to wait until he’d regained a little strength before drinking. Alexander just smiled and drank it all in one go whilst looking at Phillip directly in the face. 

Philip was so overwhelmed by the trust of Alexander that he nearly broke down. Alexander recovered fully, and Philip’s standing with the army went up another notch.

It’s perfectly in character for T’Challa, but it’s still so nice to see a leader who understands that doing the right thing matters more than protecting his own interests, especially when the people he’s helping might not have done the same for him.

EME School Vadodara Signs MoU with Bhailal Amin General Hospital for Healthcare Services

Access to Specialist Medical Consultations, Advanced Diagnostics and Treatment Facilities • Diagnostic Tests at 75% of Prescribed CGHS Rates

VADODARA: In a significant step towards ensuring accessible and #affordable #healthcare for 
#IndianArmy personnel and their #families, #EMESchool, #Vadodara, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (#MoU) with 
#BhailalAminGeneralHospital. 
The initiative, undertaken in collaboration with #FICCI #FLO Vadodara, aims to enhance the healthcare and overall well-being of #military personnel and their dependents.

The MoU signing ceremony was attended by Major General Mohit Gandhi, Commandant of EME School; Barkha Amin, Chairperson of Bhailal Amin General Hospital; and Neha Patel, Senior Vice Chairperson of FICCI FLO Vadodara.

Under this #agreement, eligible military personnel and their #dependents will have access to a wide range of medical services, including consultations with specialist and super-specialist doctors, laboratory and radiology investigations, inpatient treatment, surgical procedures, emergency medical services, maternity care and specialised cardiac treatment.

As per the agreement, consultations with specialist doctors will be available at designated concessional rates, while diagnostic investigations will be offered at 75% of the applicable prescribed #CGHS rates, subject to the terms and conditions specified in the MoU.

The primary objective of this partnership is to complement existing military medical facilities and make specialised healthcare services more accessible to military personnel and their families, particularly when advanced medical expertise is required.

This collaborative initiative by EME School, Bhailal Amin General Hospital and FICCI FLO Vadodara marks an important step towards strengthening healthcare access and promoting the well-being of India's military community and their families.

Ghouls Just Want to Have Fun: Where to Celebrate Halloween in Foley, Alabama

With the spookiest season of the year in full swing, Foley, Alabama offers a full lineup of family-friendly trick-or-treat events, community gatherings, and thrilling haunted attractions. Whether you’re looking for a fun evening of trunk-or-treating with the kids, a high-energy charity bike ride, or immersive haunted trails, there is something for every age group across town this October.

🎃 Halloween at the Y: Trunk or Treat at Snook Family YMCA

Date & Time: Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 4:30 PM – 7:30 PM
Location: Snook Family YMCA – Foley (2560 S. Pine St.)
Admission: Free
The Snook Family YMCA is hosting its annual community Trunk or Treat event. Local families, businesses, churches, and community members are invited to decorate their vehicles, hand out candy, and join in an evening filled with games, costumes, and Halloween fun. The event is completely free and open to everyone in the community.
Get Involved: Anyone interested in hosting a decorated trunk, providing activities, or donating candy can contact event coordinator Alexa via email at asommer@ysal.org.

🧹 7th Annual Foley Witches Ride
Date & Time: Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 5:00 PM – 10:00 PM

Location: Downtown Foley & Heritage Park
Organized by the Society of Black Hats, this 7th annual women-only charity bike ride features over 200 costumed witches riding through the streets of downtown Foley. Spectators of all ages are welcome to gather along downtown streets to watch the procession. The ride concludes with an after-party at Heritage Park running until 10:00 PM. Ticket sales and sponsorships directly support local non-profit organizations helping women and children in South Baldwin County.
📷
🏛️ Downtown Foley’s Hometown Halloween

Date & Time: Thursday, October 29, 2026 | 5:30 PM – 8:00 PM

Admission: Free
A 20-year local tradition, Hometown Halloween brings thousands of costumed children and families into downtown Foley for a safe night of trick-or-treating. Local merchants and community organizations host game booths, hayrides, inflatable obstacle courses, balloon artists, face painting, a cake walk, and concessions. The popular costume contest starts at 6:00 PM behind the Holmes Medical Museum, awarding over $1,000 in prizes across multiple age brackets and group categories.
🎡 Halloween Festivities at Downtown OWA
Dates: October 1 – October 31, 2026

Location: Downtown OWA (1501 S. OWA Blvd.)

OWA Parks & Resort offers a month-long celebration featuring themed “Creature Come Alive” photo-op zones—such as Zombie Lane, Witches Hollow, and Ghost Blvd—scattered throughout Downtown OWA. Signature events during Halloween weekend include:
Little Creature’s Ball: Friday, October 30 (5:00 PM – 8:00 PM) featuring a kids’ costume contest by the splash pad, DJ music, and dancing.
Wag-O-Ween: Saturday, October 31 (11:00 AM – 1:00 PM) featuring a pet costume contest and pumpkin bobbing.

Candy Crawl: Saturday, October 31 (2:00 PM – 5:00 PM) offering trick-or-treating at participating downtown shops and event tents.
Primal Fear: For older thrill-seekers, OWA features an immersive haunted house attraction on select nights throughout October.

Graham Creek Nature Preserve hosts seasonal outdoor activities tailored to different scare levels:

Spooky Express: A scare-free, lighted golf cart tour through Halloween displays designed for younger children ($5 per person, cash only).
Sinister Circus Haunted Forest: A half-mile darkened wooded trail filled with themed circus scenes and live scare actors on select October weekend nights at 7:00 PM.

Pumpkin Play Day: Saturday, October 31 (10:00 AM – 12:00 PM) featuring daytime outdoor games and fall activities.
📚 Foley Public Library Halloween Activities
Location: Foley Community Library
TNT STEM Challenge (Ages 10–18): Monday, October 26 (4:00 PM – 5:00 PM) – Halloween Rice Krispie Treats making (registration required).

Halloween Story Time & Craft: Saturday, October 31 (10:00 AM – 11:00 AM) – Spooky storytime at the Children’s Story Grove, followed by trick-or-treating throughout the library.

text:
‘Out-authenticating’ tourism rivals in Southeast Asia

MANILA – From crystalline waters, white sand beaches to majestic mountains and valleys all over the archipelago, the Philippines has no shortage of postcard-perfect islands and destinations to attract travelers. 

But in Southeast Asia, where countries offer relatively similar nature destinations, what edge does the Philippines have in outpacing neighbors competing for the same market and travelers?

For a marketing expert, one solution is to bank on something less tangible: authenticity

“Authenticity is the Philippines' most valuable tourism asset because culture, heritage, and people cannot be replicated by competing destinations. The Philippines will never outspend the larger tourism economies, but it can out-authenticate them,” SM Hotels and Conventions Vice President Neil Rumbaoa said at a Pacific Asia Travel Association (PATA) business assembly earlier this month.

While many destinations can replicate attractions, Rumbaoa said travelers most remember the experience and positive interactions with locals when visiting a destination.

He cited as examples the rapidly growing allure of the mystical island of Siquijor that gives tourists a glimpse of the centuries-old healing tradition of Filipinos; the surfing culture and easygoing rhythm in Siargao that would often have visitors finding themselves extending their stay and returning repeatedly; and the memorable cultural immersions in the famed rice terraces in Ifugao, to name a few.

“Tourists trust experiences more than advertisements. Reviews, recommendations, and reputation drive decisions. And marketing succeeds when promises and experience align. Visibility attracts visitors. Trust brings them back,” he added.

In a separate interview with the Philippine News Agency, he said Manila should also focus on travelers willing to pay for what the country uniquely offers.

"We're an island nation and our infrastructure is not that sophisticated — it’s not mature yet," he said. "So, let's go for the segment that will really (travel here) because of what we offer. We have more than 7,000 islands, there are more than 7,000 reasons to come to the Philippines.”

The development of Philippine tourism under the Marcos administration is centered on the promotion of authentic experiences that showcase the rich and diverse Filipino culture across the Philippines.

In 2023, the country revamped its tourism slogan and launched the new national campaign “Love the Philippines” to highlight the “heart and soul” of the Philippines as a destination.

No less than President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. said the government intends to promote “experiential” travel in the Philippines by positioning Filipino food, culture, heritage and arts as prime tourism products of the country. (PNA)

text:
The History of Guitar Amplifier Vacuum Tubes, 1904–2026

Vacuum tubes made amplified electric guitar possible long before solid-state electronics or digital modeling existed. In 1904, John Ambrose Fleming developed the thermionic diode for detecting electrical signals. Lee de Forest’s 1906 Audion added a control grid, laying the foundation for practical electronic amplification. By the 1930s, radio-industry tube technology could power the earliest electric-guitar amplifiers.

RCA introduced the 6L6 beam-power tube in 1936, followed by the smaller 6V6 family. These became cornerstones of American amplifier design. The Fender Champ 5F1 used a single 6V6GT output tube, while the 1955-era Deluxe 5E3 used two in a push-pull circuit. The Deluxe also employed a 5Y3GT rectifier, which converted AC into the high-voltage DC supply.

Inside a tube, a heated cathode emits electrons, while a control grid regulates current flowing toward the plate. Small preamp tubes amplify the guitar’s voltage signal; output tubes supply the power needed to drive a loudspeaker through an output transformer. Because these stages operate nonlinearly when pushed, they can generate harmonics and compression, but no tube type guarantees a particular sound.

The 12AX7, introduced in 1947, was arguably the most enduring preamplifier tube. Known in Europe as the ECC83, this dual triode offered high voltage gain in a compact package. It appeared throughout Fender, Marshall and Mesa/Boogie designs. Related types, including the 12AT7 and 12AU7, served lower-gain, phase-inverter, reverb-driver and other specialized functions.

European tube development shaped British amplifier designs. The EF86 pentode appeared in early Vox AC15 preamps, while the EL84 output pentode powered two-tube AC15 and four-tube AC30 output stages. Introduced in 1959, the AC30 became a lasting example of EL84-based amplification.

Marshall’s JTM45, introduced in 1962, borrowed heavily from Fender’s 5F6-A Bassman architecture. Early JTM45s used 5881-family output tubes before KT66s became characteristic. Later Marshall Super Leads adopted EL34 power pentodes, particularly from 1967 onward. The EL34 also became standard in classic Hiwatt DR103 amplifiers, although transformer design, feedback, bias and circuitry distinguished the two manufacturers.

Fender’s Twin Reverb represented another approach: four 6L6GC power tubes delivered substantial clean output and headroom. Its solid-state rectifier differed from the GZ34 tube rectifier in the classic Bassman 5F6-A. Rectifier types, filtering and power-supply resistance can influence voltage drop and dynamic response.

Ampeg introduced the 300-watt SVT in 1969. Original examples used six 6146 output tubes; around 1970 the design changed to six 6550s, establishing the more familiar SVT configuration.

In the 1970s and 1980s, amplifier designers increasingly cascaded 12AX7 preamp stages to generate distortion without requiring maximum output power. Mesa/Boogie’s Mark IIC+, introduced in 1984, exemplified that approach.

Tube manufacturing declined as transistors replaced valves in consumer electronics, yet specialized factories continued supplying musicians. In 2026, 12AX7, 6V6, 6L6, EL84, EL34, KT66 and 6550 families remain in use.

Today’s tube amplifiers coexist with solid-state and digitally modeled designs. Tube labels do not guarantee interchangeability: heater demand, plate ratings and bias requirements can differ substantially. Their electrical behavior matters, but an amplifier’s character ultimately comes from the complete circuit, transformers, speakers and operating conditions.

text:
📊 $BTC HTF Case Study & Analysis

I’m approaching BTC through three scenarios: a corrective continuation, a bullish re-accumulation, and a deeper bearish markdown.

Here’s how I’m positioning myself for each.

📉 Base Case: Corrective Distribution

We remain in a corrective price distribution. Value is gradually migrating lower, with local ranges shifting downwards. From an Auction Market Theory perspective, this suggests that the market is increasingly accepting lower prices.

That said, we have to acknowledge the underlying bullish strength. Despite the distribution, we haven’t seen an immediate, impulsive markdown following the range.

My positioning:

• Swing short opened in the upper regions.
• Small hedge longs built continuously to capture local opportunities and protect against upside continuation.

I’m currently holding a hedge long that has already offered additional profit opportunities and has been secured to break-even.

The Target -> $77.2K

This is a key area where I expect the market could react, potentially initiating another accumulation phase before the next leg higher.

📈 Bull Case: Re-accumulation

The bullish scenario starts right here, within the current range.

What I need to see is an impulsive markup to the upside. This would suggest that the current range is a prolonged re-accumulation rather than distribution.

My hedge long provides exposure to this scenario.

However, I currently assign it a lower probability than my base case, which is why I’m only hedged with one position.

📉 Bear Case: Deeper Markdown

This scenario initially follows the base case, but with one crucial difference: BTC leaves the current range through a clear markdown.

In that event, I would expect the $77.2K nPOC to potentially fail as support, opening the door for further downside and a redistribution of value at lower levels.

A revisit to sub-$70K would then become a possibility, particularly if price moves to fill the inefficiencies below.

My existing swing short provides exposure to this scenario.

⚖️ Conclusion: Probabilities Over Predictions

I’ve structured my positioning to account for all three scenarios.

I don’t need to know with certainty which direction BTC will take. I need to understand the possible outcomes, assess their probabilities, and position accordingly.

As a quantitative trader, my focus is on Expected Value, risk management, and extracting value from the market over a large sample of trades.

To the perma-bulls and perma-bears fighting it out on X: have fun.

I’ll stick to the probabilities. 📊

(“AST SpaceMobile”) (NASDAQ: ASTS), the company building the first and only space-based cellular broadband network accessible directly by everyday smartphones, designed for both commercial and government applications, today announced it is advancing service readiness in key global markets before the end of 2026, including the United States, Canada, Japan, United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia.

“We are moving toward service with the partnerships, spectrum and network capabilities needed to bring cellular broadband from space into people’s everyday lives,” said Scott Wisnieswki, President of AST SpaceMobile. “Our Bluebird satellites, with the largest communications satellites ever deployed in low Earth orbit, carry capabilities beyond space-based cellular broadband connectivity. We are building a platform that can connect millions of people, help government keep our country safe and resilient, and support emerging applications in AI. That is the scale of the opportunity we are bringing into service.”

AST SpaceMobile now has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed, or in planning worldwide. The expansive ground network supports AST SpaceMobile’s global commercial ecosystem with over 60 mobile network operators who cover over 3 billion subscribers, bringing a third layer of connectivity directly into the mobile networks people already use.

AST SpaceMobile has strategic partnerships with AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten Mobile, Bell Canada, TELUS, and stc Group. These relationships provide a direct path to market through partners’ existing mobile services, enabling operators to extend coverage and offer new connectivity options to their subscribers.

Spectrum is a key component of this readiness. AST SpaceMobile combines strategic partner operators’ spectrum with access to mobile satellite services (MSS) spectrum, targeting approximately 100 MHz of access in the United States. Its spectrum position includes access to 45 MHz of MSS mid-band spectrum in North America and priority rights to 60 MHz of S-band spectrum globally on a market-by-market basis.

The company’s satellite technology can tune across approximately 1,150 MHz of low- and mid-band frequencies globally, providing flexibility to serve different markets using available partner and satellite spectrum, subject to applicable regulatory approvals.

Supporting this service rollout, AST SpaceMobile’s ground network connects the company’s growing satellite constellation with mobile operators’ core networks, routing voice, video and broadband data between space and ground-based infrastructure, making it a key component of the end-to-end infrastructure required to deliver space-based cellular broadband connectivity through partners to people everywhere they work, live, and travel. This integration enables operators to extend their reach beyond the limits of terrestrial coverage while evolving alongside future 3GPP standards.

In the United States, the Company has already enabled over 3,000 coverage cells and expects to activate the roughly 5,600 cellular cells that cover the continuous United States before year-end. Enabling the remaining digital cells will establish the geographic footprint required to support initial, intermittent service across the contiguous United States and is a prerequisite for nationwide rollout.

text:
Chips Rafferty.

Shearer, roo shooter, drover, opal miner, boundary rider, screen idol. Chips Rafferty, at six foot six inches and ‘lean as a dingo’ seemed unlikely as an early Australian Hollywood star. His acting style closely reflected the man himself - irreverent and with a wry wit. Rafferty was, on and off the screen, the embodiment of the Australian bushman - a bit of a larrikin, resourceful and self-reliant in a time when the post-war world needed every-day heroes.

John William Goffage (‘Chips’ to his school mates) was the son of a miner. Born in Broken Hill in 1909 as the ‘Big Strike’ triggered ongoing conflict between unions and mining companies, the lockouts and hardship in the first two years of his life would have hit his family hard. The Goffages moved on and settled in Sydney where Chips learned to surf and box, and he started painting in water colours and writing poetry which he sold to several Sydney publications.

Chips Rafferty was offered his first role as an extra when he was thirty and living on a boat in Sydney Harbour. He probably met Cinesound director Ken G. Hall at the Black & White Club at Circular Quay, a haunt of bohemians, actors, and artists where Rafferty was a regular drinker. Hall, who gave him his first role as an extra, immediately saw raw talent. His break came when he landed a lead role as a soldier inForty Thousand Horsemen, a WWI film. His life and his film career seemed to run parallel, because Australian troops were already fighting in the Middle East when the film came out.

Rafferty enlisted in the Air Force. He was permitted to film while on leave and his next starring role was in The Rats of Tobruk, about the Gallipoli campaign. It was TheOverlanders that made him an instant star. Rafferty plays a drover who drives 1000-head of cattle from Wyndham in Western Australia to Rockhampton in Queensland, around 1200 miles, to prevent them from being captured by the Japanese. At the height of his career, he was called the Australian Gary Cooper.
Chips Rafferty starred in over forty films in the U.S. and Australia and produced many more until he died unexpectedly at the age of 62. His last film was the classic Wake in Fright, filmed in his hometown of Broken Hill. The perfect swan song. Wake In Frightwas the first of many major cinema releases filmed on location in Broken Hill, making the town and its atmospheric desert landscape into a destination for film producers. Chips Rafferty, legend of the Australian screen, is Broken Hill’s own.

Fake job advertisements offering employment in Georgia may be used to recruit people into contracts with the Russian Defence Ministry, according to the Russian anti-war organisation Idite Lesom (“Get Lost”), which helps Russians avoid conscription and leave the military.

The organisation reported that a man responding to an advertisement for manual labour in Tbilisi and Rustavi was offered a daily wage of 200 GEL, free accommodation and three meals a day.

However, after contacting the advertiser, he was told the positions in Georgia had been filled and was instead offered work in Russian-occupied Kherson or Russia’s Belgorod region, with a monthly salary of 170,000–210,000 rubles and free travel from Tbilisi to Moscow.

The employer requested a copy of his passport and explained that he would have to sign two contracts: one with the employer and another with the Russian Defence Ministry.

“We will sign two contracts. I want to tell you from the outset: one with us and the other with the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation,” the employer wrote in messages published by Idite Lesom.

The recruiter claimed that the military contract was necessary to obtain permission to work in border areas. The documents provided included employment contracts referencing a Russian private security company and positions such as security guard and communications specialist.

According to the man, an identical advertisement using the same Telegram contact details appeared on another platform on October 18.

text:
𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗕𝗶𝘁𝗧𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗜𝗻 𝗔 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗲

Some technologies capture attention for a season. Others remain useful because they solve problems that never disappear.

BitTorrent belongs to the latter category. More than two decades after its emergence, its peer-to-peer architecture continues to demonstrate how distributing resources across a network can support large-scale data delivery without relying entirely on one central server.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗡𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗛𝗲𝗹𝗽𝘀 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮

Traditional distribution can place considerable pressure on a central infrastructure point when demand increases. BitTorrent takes a different approach: participants can share pieces of content with one another, allowing downloads to draw from multiple available peers.

As participation grows, the network may gain additional distribution capacity. Actual performance still depends on peer availability, bandwidth, and the number of participants sharing the requested content.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗨𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗦𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝘀 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴

The ecosystem figures highlighted include:

➜ More than 581M client installations.

➜ Over 42.5M weekly gross reach.

➜ More than 8.84M average daily active users.

➜ 4.54M daily active µTorrent Desktop users.

With usage spanning desktop, mobile, and BitTorrent Web, these reported figures illustrate the continued reach of peer-to-peer distribution. Installations and audience reach are different measures from active usage, but together they offer context for the ecosystem’s scale.

𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗙𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗧𝗼 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗿𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲

The deeper lesson extends beyond downloading files. Peer-to-peer principles can inform decentralized storage, distributed computing, blockchain infrastructure, and AI networks, where sharing resources across participants can reduce dependence on a single delivery point.

BitTorrent’s legacy is not simply that it helped people share files. It demonstrated a lasting design principle: participants can contribute to the infrastructure they use.

That idea remains relevant wherever data, computing power, and digital resources need to move efficiently at scale.

text:
Buying $SPY calls when 64% of its components are declining is like betting on a relay team where most runners are limping.

Today's breadth numbers tell a story the index price often hides. Only 169 of 500 stocks are advancing, and less than half sit above their 50-day moving average. That's a market held up by a narrow group of heavy-weight names, not broad participation. When large-cap tech or mega-cap momentum stocks carry the index while the rest deteriorate underneath, you're looking at a structurally fragile tape. It doesn't mean a crash is imminent, but it absolutely means the risk-reward on naked upside plays is quietly worse than the headline price suggests.

For options positioning, this breadth reading changes a few things worth acting on. First, Implied Volatility on individual names outside the leaders may be underpriced relative to their actual directional risk — single-stock puts on declining names can offer better value than broad index protection right now. Second, if you're selling premium on SPY, understand that a rotation out of the handful of names keeping the index afloat could produce a faster, sharper drawdown than the overall calm suggests. Tighter deltas, shorter Days To Expiration, and smaller position sizes make sense here. Third, consider using the  IV Crush Screener to identify names where Implied Volatility hasn't caught up to the underlying weakness yet — those are often the most asymmetric setups when breadth is this divergent.

text:
Happened. Like weather.

I replayed it all week at my kitchen table, until one detail snagged. Six months ago, my password had expired, and the IT desk had been down, so I'd texted my new one to the one person who was always helpful with tech.

I scrolled to that thread and found the message. Then I scrolled to the date Hollis had been passed over for my promotion.

I drove to his house that Saturday. I didn't plan what I'd say.

He opened the door in socks, a coffee mug in his hand, and saw my face. The mug trembled.

"You kept it," I said. "My password. Four years, Hollis."

He didn't deny it. He just sat down on his own front step, like his legs had quit.

"I didn't think they'd fire you," he whispered. "I thought you'd get a warning. I just wanted you to lose something."

I thought I'd feel rage. Instead I felt the weight of every shift I'd covered for him, every lunch I'd bought.

"I'm going to tell them the truth," I said. "Or you are. You have until Monday."

I walked back to my car without looking behind me.

Monday morning, his resignation email arrived, along with a confession.

I didn't gloat. I just reread the line they offered me back, we'd love to have you return, and took my time deciding.

“The Fold”

No idea the totality of any of that but I know it just about broke me. It’s all written now. 

When I have the big “spells” anger does overtake me. Over time you learn to hide it enough except for the facial droop, forced eye closure from pressure, slurred speech, and balance glitches. You try to hide even those because your out with family wanting them not to focus on you but the moment and family fun. You stop going to the ER and seeing specialists eventually because they have nothing to offer but bags of pills that turn you into a drooling zombie 24/7 instead. 

Hate and Rage aren’t good for us I think. Anger is biblical but hate and rage aren’t and it seems social media likes to lean you toward hate along with many other mechanisms. 

I’ve not angry at God but I’m angry at a lot of humans. I hate the bread and circuses. No need for Aliens, lizard people, demon possessions or anything else like it. All that was needed was people that would choose Evil over good. Incentives over people. And there are a lot of them. 

I’m going to go try and get back more into life and providing and finding purpose. I don’t think Elon’s plan of people not having to work is a good plan either. "Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm elections, senior officials say, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Tehran's reluctance to strike a quick deal to end ​the war.
Three senior Iranian officials and an Iranian insider, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Tehran was convinced the US president was ready to resort to renewed attacks to try to ‌break the stalemate in the eight-month-old war.

IRAN CAN EXPLOIT TRUMP'S POLITICAL PROBLEMS
The war, which began in February when the US and its ally Israel launched strikes on Iran, has helped drive ​Trump’s approval rating to a record low as polls suggest that Americans worried about high gasoline prices will punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections.

Trump has repeatedly said he expects oil ​prices to drop after the elections, but has not offered a detailed plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global ⁠energy shipping route effectively closed by Iran since the war began.
Iranian attacks both threatened and real have kept ship traffic through the strait to a trickle, while a US maritime blockade and trade sanctions have cut ​off Iran's oil export revenues and exacerbated growing domestic economic woes.

With Tehran refusing to make concessions it believes could benefit Trump politically, there is little chance of a breakthrough before the elections, the officials said.
Under pressure from ​Israel, Washington wants Iran’s decades-long nuclear programme - which Iran says is purely peaceful and Western powers allege has military dimensions - on the table from the outset.
For its part, Tehran insists that its conditions under a "seven-day plan" must be met before nuclear negotiations begin. And it offers no prospect of giving up the leverage over the Strait of Hormuz that the conflict prompted it to seize.

IRAN CANNOT TRUST WASHINGTON, ​OFFICIALS SAY
Iran’s proposal, conveyed through Qatari mediators, offered to reopen the strait within seven days, albeit under Iranian control, provided that Washington lifted its maritime blockade, eased restrictions on Iranian oil exports, released frozen assets and ended ​hostilities on all fronts.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the offer remained on the table, with messages being exchanged through mediators.
Tehran's view that Washington cannot be trusted to commit to diplomacy stems from the attacks on ‌Iran that ⁠have derailed previous negotiations, one Iranian official said.
In June 2025, an Israeli attack wrecked plans for a sixth round of US-Iran nuclear talks in Oman. And last February, the US and Israel launched their war just after another round of talks ended, with further technical discussions scheduled.
Maintaining a state somewhere between war and peace through the US midterms allows Iran to sustain pressure on Washington while reiterating its commitment to diplomacy.
Trump has said the US will not bomb Iran again before November 3. However, the officials said Tehran continues to expect that bombing will resume, sooner or later.

RETURN TO PREWAR STATUS IMPOSSIBLE FOR IRAN, SAYS ANALYST
Iran’s strategy of keeping negotiations alive without rushing towards agreement comes at ​a cost.
Prolonged uncertainty is weighing ⁠on Iran’s already crippled economy and wearing down public patience. 
Annual inflation hit 73.6% in September, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran, and the rial currency has fallen nearly 35% against the dollar since Washington reapplied its naval blockade in July.
Iran’s seaborne crude exports fell to zero in the second week of September from a 14-day average of 230,000 ⁠barrels per day ​at the start of the month, and remained there as of October 5, according to energy intelligence platform Vortexa."

text:
Microsoft is announcing new capabilities for its "Sovereign Cloud". And where better to make that announcement than Paris, where France has publicly declared it wants to remove its dependence on US tech companies.

If you add the word "Sovereign" in front of Cloud, Microsoft can no longer access your data, and it’s magically protected from surveillance by them and a foreign government.

🇮🇪 That's Irish sarcasm.

🇺🇸 The US CLOUD Act allows the US government to compel US companies to hand over customer data, no matter where in the world it’s stored.

🇫🇷 Hosting data in France doesn't protect it from US government demands because calling the service Sovereign Cloud doesn't change US law.

Microsoft's Sovereign Cloud offers different levels of protection. By default, Microsoft manages encryption keys, but customers can choose to control their own keys, keep them outside Microsoft's infrastructure and run services without connecting to Microsoft's cloud. Why Microsoft controls encryption keys by default should be questioned. That doesn't seem like a customer benefit.

Data sovereignty means controlling who can access your data, not who promises not to access it. That comes down to who controls the technology, who can decrypt the data and which companies can be forced to hand it over.

We saw this with Palantir and the NHS. Both denied that Palantir staff had full access to patients’ personally identifiable information and health records. I challenged those claims with a technical analysis explaining why it would be impossible for Palantir not to have access. Both disputed my analysis until that access was exposed.

Don't just trust what tech companies or governments say their surveillance legislation or technology does. Examine what the technology is designed to do, how it works and, most importantly, what it makes technically possible. Or just ask me and I'll tell you if I haven't already written about it.

Most organisations don't configure complicated systems properly, especially when it comes to cybersecurity. So it's guaranteed that some customers will forget or won't even realise that Microsoft still controls the encryption keys by default, and can use them to access their data. You only have to look at OpenAI for a recent example of how easily insider threats can gain access when companies implement poor security processes and systems.

💡 Customers paying for this specific cloud service to protect their most sensitive data are being asked to trust a US tech company that works closely with governments and intelligence agencies in the US, Canada, UK, Australia and Israel.

🇮🇱 In 2025, an investigation exposed how Israel’s Intelligence Unit 8200 used Microsoft Azure to store and analyse millions of intercepted Palestinian phone calls. Microsoft worked closely with the intelligence unit to build the infrastructure. It wasn't just a cloud provider unaware of how its technology was being used. The surveillance project followed a meeting between Microsoft’s CEO and the unit’s commander, so it was forged at the highest level.

Microsoft only terminated the unit’s access to certain Azure and AI services after the surveillance operation was exposed.

I'm not claiming Microsoft will misuse Sovereign Cloud. I'm saying its technology already supports mass surveillance of civilians around the world, and that won't stop because governments are the tech industry's biggest customers. Government contracts help turn tech companies into multibillion-dollar giants, giving them a massive incentive to foster those relationships. 

Data sovereignty is a worthwhile objective, but achieving complete sovereignty requires absolute control over more than where data is stored. It means controlling the infrastructure, software, encryption keys, administration, maintenance and every third party with access to data.

Even local companies rely on foreign tech providers, contractors, suppliers and infrastructure. Any of those relationships can introduce external access or legal obligations beyond the customer's jurisdiction.

Moving data into a local data centre doesn't eliminate those dependencies. Neither does buying technology marketed as sovereign.

Complete data sovereignty is something to aspire to, but maintaining exclusive control across every technical and commercial dependency is practically impossible.

It's like expecting every drop of water from your tap to come from one specific well, then expecting it to return to that same well after going down the drain, without ever entering another water system.

"Sovereign Cloud" is branding and a new positioning statement like "Super Intelligence". The technology might be useful, but clever marketing encourages customers to associate a product name with protections they wish they had, rather than what the technology actually enables.

As usual, I'm not here to repeat what tech companies or governments claim they're doing for customers and citizens. I'm here to explain what legislation and technology actually do and what the consequences are when specific people make public announcements.

Some examples of what they say:

🇪🇺 The European Commission claims to protect EU citizens from surveillance by US tech companies while pushing Chat Control, which would require US tech companies around the world to scan everyone's public and private communications. In fact, any company in the world now has the right to scan everyone's private communications.

🇬🇧 The UK government claims mandatory digital IDs will stop identity fraud, while making everyday services more convenient.

More than 25 governments around the world are justifying surveillance, identity verification and data collection as necessary to protect children from harmful content and dangerous people, while claiming adults also need protection from addictive designs that harm their mental health.

It's propaganda packaged as public safety and clever marketing. Governments and trillion-dollar tech companies meet at G7 summits, announce partnerships and tell the public that new legislation, identity verification for account recovery and features marketed as convenient are all in their best interests.

We are expected to accept digital and physical surveillance for our protection and safety. We're told it's necessary for national security, protecting children from groomers, preventing fraud and stopping terrorism.

People who commit crimes represent a tiny fraction of society, yet governments propose systems that affect entire populations, including people who have done absolutely nothing wrong.

When someone on here asked me, "What do you have to hide that you don’t want anyone reading your messages?" I replied, "That’s none of your business. And that’s the point."

The next time you read an announcement from a tech company, hear an AI lobbyist making extreme claims about either doom or utopia, or listen to a policymaker or politician, ask yourself: How do they benefit, and how do the people they work with behind closed doors benefit?

Pretend you're wearing Meta's creepy spyware glasses, except they show you everyone and everything through the worst possible interpretation of what they're saying and why.

That's a good starting point.

(I'm all for AR and VR. But I'll only trust people who've earned it, not those who've spent 20+ years proving they can't be trusted to lick a stamp without reading the contents of everyone's envelopes.)

text:
Trump has made a deal with Moscow, but Zelensky has other ideas
Moscow’s diesel agreement with Washington marks a diplomatic success, but offers no guarantee of a Ukraine peace deal
Published 19 Oct, 2026 16:50
By Anton Grishanov, Chief Research Fellow at the Institute for Contemporary International Issues of the Diplomatic Academy of the Russian Foreign Ministry
https://t.co/lR4ygyF85g
The diesel deal between Moscow and Washington has once again shaken up the geopolitical chessboard, with each passing day bringing fresh and unexpected developments. Most striking is Kiev’s behavior. Despite his enormous dependence on Washington, Vladimir Zelensky has decided to challenge Donald Trump directly, adopting an unusually confrontational approach.
A more pragmatic politician might have announced a moratorium on strikes against Russian oil refineries until the US congressional elections, particularly as Washington had demanded no further concessions. Instead, Zelensky has chosen confrontation, creating a diplomatic crisis of his own making, but whether it develops into something more serious remains to be seen.
Relations between Kiev and Washington have deteriorated before, most notably following the notorious Oval Office confrontation, although that rupture lasted only a few weeks. Western European leaders and congressional hawks worked tirelessly to repair the damage. This time, however, the circumstances are different.
The NATO Europeans appear to have abandoned attempts to charm Trump, Senator Lindsey Graham is no longer on Capitol Hill, while Keith Kellogg, previously sympathetic to Kiev, has departed the administration, thus the pressure on Trump has diminished, although that hardly guarantees a fundamental change in American policy.
For one thing, the diesel agreement has done little to clarify the prospects for peace, given, according to leaks from Washington, American officials continue to promote proposals, including freezing hostilities along existing lines, that Moscow considers unacceptable.
Even if Washington succeeds in forcing Kiev back to the negotiating table, there’s no guarantee that the understandings reached at Anchorage can be revived and Trump could just as easily reverse course, as he has done before, and blame Russia for another diplomatic deadlock. Meanwhile, influential figures within his administration, particularly Secretary of State Marco Rubio, remain deeply skeptical of Moscow, so their relative silence should not be mistaken for acquiescence.
Nor is there much reason to believe Russian diesel exports to the US will quickly bring down fuel prices or transform the electoral landscape.
The agreement is primarily a political gesture, intended to reassure Trump’s increasingly disillusioned core supporters that their president understands their economic difficulties and is attempting to find a way out, yet it’s unlikely to prevent Republicans from losing control of the House of Representatives. The Senate remains uncertain, but its fate will depend on numerous factors, with diesel prices only one consideration.
A Democratic-controlled Congress would almost certainly confront the White House over Ukraine, seeking to preserve American assistance to Kiev, while another impeachment campaign cannot be ruled out either. Such a confrontation could consume Trump’s attention and leave greater responsibility for foreign policy in the hands of officials such as Rubio, whose instincts towards Russia are considerably less accommodating.
There’s also the possibility of a more fundamental reshaping of the Ukrainian political project, where replacing Zelensky, under external pressure, with a leader more acceptable to Washington could help reconcile American and Western European approaches and the growing crisis of governance in Kiev makes this scenario increasingly conceivable.
None of this diminishes Moscow’s diplomatic achievement in securing the diesel agreement, where it’s demonstrated that Washington is prepared to negotiate directly with Russia when American interests demand it, regardless of Kiev’s objections.
But diplomatic success shouldn’t breed complacency and the underlying contradictions remain unresolved, the prospects for a durable settlement are uncertain, and too many powerful interests still favor prolonging the confrontation.
The diesel deal may have changed the immediate political calculations, but it hasn’t altered the fundamental dynamics of the conflict.
This article was first published by Kommersant, and was translated and edited by the RT team
