text:
He carried sixty-nine people across Lake Erie to Canada in seven months.

That was 1842, between May and December, and William Wells Brown kept the tally himself. He was doing it while he was still, legally, another man's property, with a steamboat captain down in St. Louis holding the papers on him. Ten years before that, a slave trader on the Mississippi had given him a very different job to do with his hands.

That job was done in a room on a steamboat where the passengers could not see.

He was about eighteen, hired out for the year to a St. Louis slave trader named James Walker, and the boat was the Carlton, running down to New Orleans. Walker had spent eight or nine weeks putting the cargo together, and some of the people in it were old.

Old did not sell.

So Brown was handed a razor and a pot of blacking. He shaved the whiskers off the old men, plucked out the gray hairs where there were not too many of them, and where there were too many he worked the colour in by hand until nothing gray showed.

Walker then told each of them how old they were now.

Brown wrote later that they came out of that room looking ten or fifteen years younger than they were, and that some of the men who bought from Walker got a good deal less than they had paid for.

He was nineteen when the year was over. He called it the longest year he ever lived.

At the far end of the run, the people he had worked on were held in a pen in New Orleans, a small yard fifteen or twenty feet across, shut in by buildings, with one big gate of iron bars. They slept in the buildings and were turned out into the yard by day. Whatever was left once the best of them had gone was walked over to the auction rooms at the Exchange coffee house and sold off there.

He had been born in Kentucky around 1814, and nobody wrote the day down. He never knew his own age, and the record still carries more than one birth year for him.

His mother was Elizabeth. She had seven children, and, as he put it himself, no two of them had the same father.

His own father was a white planter named George Higgins, a relative of the Dr. Young who held Elizabeth as property. Higgins acknowledged the boy as his and got Young to promise he would never be sold.

The promise did not hold. Young sold him, and before he was twenty he had been sold or hired out to something like ten different men.

Then the Youngs took a nephew into the house, a free white boy, and the nephew's name was William.

There was already a William under that roof. He was the one who was property, so he was the one who had to change, and they started calling him Sandford.

He carried that name for the rest of his time in slavery.

Thirteen years after he got out he wrote a dedication to the man who had sheltered him and put it plainly, that slavery had denied him even a name by which to be known among men.

The jobs he was hired out to in St. Louis were on the river and in other men's hotels and kitchens. For one stretch he was sent to the printing office of Elijah Lovejoy, who would later be killed by a mob at Alton, Illinois, for the things he printed.

Brown could not read a word of any of it. He was kept away from letters the whole time he was enslaved.

In 1833 his sister was sold. He went to his mother and talked her into running north with him.

They got about eleven days before they were taken in Illinois and brought back to St. Louis in irons.

While the two of them sat in the jail waiting to hear what would be done with them, word came in that his mother had been sold to a speculator and was going to the New Orleans market.

She had one instruction for him. He set it down in print years later, her saying that they would not meet again on this side of the grave, that he had always said he would not die a slave, and then the last of it, now try to get your liberty.

He was nineteen. He lived to be seventy and he never saw her again.

He was the one who had asked her to run.

He was sold on to a St. Louis merchant tailor named Samuel Willi, and Willi sold him again at the end of September 1833, to a steamboat captain called Enoch Price.

On January 1, 1834, the captain's boat lay tied up at Cincinnati, on the free side of the river. Brown picked up a passenger's trunk, carried it down the plank, put it where it was going, and kept walking.

He walked at night for six days, in January, with almost no food and nothing on his back worth calling a coat.

An old Quaker took him in when he could not go any further. The man's family kept him twelve or fifteen days while he was sick, made him clothes, bought him a pair of boots, and before he left they asked what he was called.

He told them William. It was the truth, and it had not been allowed to be the truth for years.

The old man's name was Wells Brown, and he gave the young man the rest of it.

Brown settled on the lakes and took work on the boats running out of Cleveland, and the people moving fugitives through that port soon learned he would carry anybody, for nothing. In 1843 he crossed over to Malden, on the British side, and found seventeen men and women living there who had come across on his boat.

In 1847 he published his own life, at the anti-slavery office in Boston. It went through four American editions and five British ones inside three years.

Then, on January 10, 1848, a letter was written in St. Louis and posted to Edmund Quincy in Boston.

It came from Enoch Price, who had read the book and wanted the record put straight. The man who wrote it was not called William Wells Brown, Price said. He was named Sanford, he was a slave belonging to him, and he had run off on January 1, 1834.

Then came the figures. Six hundred and fifty dollars paid for him. Two thousand offered for him in New Orleans, fifteen hundred in Louisville, both turned down.

What the captain wanted now was three hundred and twenty-five dollars, handed to his agent in Boston, and free papers would follow.

Brown printed the letter. He put it in whole, near the front, ahead of chapter one.

Years earlier a man had put a brush in his hand and told him to lay black over an old man's head until the record read younger. This time the black went onto a page and the record read true.

Above it he set a note. Until then, he wrote, the public had no evidence he had ever been enslaved except his own word for it, and this letter settled the question.

Underneath it he printed his answer, from Boston, October 1848. God had made him as free as he made Enoch Price, he wrote, and no dollar would ever come out of him or out of his friends with his consent.

The following year he sailed for Britain to lecture, and went on to Paris for the international peace congress, where Victor Hugo presided.

While he was abroad, Congress passed the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850. Going home stopped meaning a return to a free state and started meaning a walk into a country where any officer anywhere could take him.

He stayed five years. His wife Elizabeth died in the United States in 1851 without him.

In 1852 he published an account of his travels, the first travel book by an African American that scholars have traced. In 1853, in London, he published a novel about the enslaved daughters of Thomas Jefferson and called it Clotel.

It is the earliest novel by an African American anyone has found.

The man who wrote it had been kept from the alphabet until he was nineteen.

He could not have it printed at home, because at home he was still merchandise with a figure attached.

In April 1854 a family of English Quakers, the Richardsons of Newcastle, paid the St. Louis captain off. They had bought Frederick Douglass out of the same danger a few years earlier.

What actually changed hands is not settled. One account puts it at three hundred dollars, under the sum named in the letter, and at least one study of Brown's life holds that the figure was pushed up sharply once the English friends came forward.

Brown came home with his two daughters and went straight back onto the circuit. In 1856 one of them, Josephine, published a life of her father, carrying the years in Europe that his own book had been written too early to hold.

He kept publishing to the end of his life. The first play by an African American to appear in print was his, in 1858, and so was the first history of Black soldiers in the American war.

He studied medicine and practised it in Boston's South End, and he died at Chelsea, Massachusetts, on November 6, 1884.

That letter is still in the front of the book, in the slaveholder's own words, naming him Sanford and setting out what he was worth.

Brown left it standing there in the editions that followed. The name he put on the title page above it is William Wells Brown.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter. If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/AeER0VXcAK

text:
The Outer Space Treaty is not so much a set of rules as a set of tools, with a modest set of built-in safeguards. At the second annual U.S. Space Forum in Vienna, I had the opportunity to explore how we can use those tools to build the next era of space governance.

I was proud to represent the University of Mississippi's Center for Air and Space Law at Ole Miss and contribute, alongside Christopher Johnson, to the academic programming through which participants earned an Executive Certificate. #OleMiss supported my participation, extending our work to equip professionals and policymakers around the world to engage with the legal foundations of space activities.

In my first presentation, we opened the toolbox. In the second, we put it to work on the Moon, starting with the plume effects of a landing spacecraft. When landing can send lunar dust and debris toward nearby equipment or historic sites, coordinating activities becomes a very practical concern. Safety zones offer one approach, fashioned from the interaction of Articles I, II, IX and XII: freedom of access, nonappropriation, due regard and reciprocal access to installations. The challenge is to protect operations while preserving the freedoms that make those operations possible.

These are questions every country has an interest in shaping, whether or not it currently operates in space. How we coordinate the first lunar activities will influence the opportunities available to those who follow, and the ability to reach the Moon should not be the price of admission to that conversation.

Tremendous kudos and my thanks to David A. Epstein. the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna and everyone who brought commercial innovators, international delegations and academics together for such thoughtful exchanges. The launch of #ProjectConstellation, connecting U.S. commercial innovators and university expertise with emerging space nations, offers an exciting opportunity to carry that engagement forward.

The tools are already in our hands. Building with them will take technical understanding, legal imagination and voices from around the world.

Always great to catch up with Mike Gold, Robin Dickey, Colleen Graffy, David Schuman, Fredrick A. Jenet, Ph.D.. M.C. Sungaila and so many others!

#USSpaceForum #SpaceLaw #ProjectConstellation #SpaceDiplomacy #UNVIE #SpaceNeedsLawyers

text:
My Love Letter to Luks 🐾
Luks…
I’m so sorry your family decided you weren’t worth keeping.
I’m sorry that when your world fell apart, not everyone rushed to catch you. Some said you could wait… that others mattered more.
But I need you to know something—
you were never invisible to me.
I didn’t just see a dog in pain…
I saw a soul carrying heartbreak so heavy it couldn’t be hidden.
The kind of pain that comes from being left behind… from wondering why.
No animal should ever have to feel that.
Every day, I whispered to you,
“I’m not giving up on you, Luks. I’m going to get you out. You will be safe. You will be loved… for the rest of your life.”
And now… that promise is finally becoming real.
✨ Luks is leaving California for Texas on April 7. ✨
His journey to healing is just beginning. He will need time, care, and a full medical evaluation before he’s ready for adoption.
But right now… what he needs most is a soft place to land.
We are looking for a medical foster—someone who can offer him a calm, quiet space where he can rest, decompress, and finally feel safe.
If you’ve ever believed in second chances…
If you’ve ever wanted to be the reason a broken heart learns to trust again…
This is your moment.
💙 Apply to foster or support Luks:
https://t.co/g7R2trtKiv
Let’s show Luks that he was never “less urgent”…
He was just waiting for the right people to say yes.
Puppy kisses and tail wags,
JFSAR 🐾

The central theme of #todaysreadings is reconciliation and vigilant readiness. 

In the First Reading from Ephesians (Eph 2:12–22), Saint Paul proclaims that Christ has shattered the dividing wall of hostility through the Cross, transforming once-alienated outsiders into reconciled fellow citizens and living stones in God’s holy temple. Paired with the Gospel of Luke (Lk 12:35–38), which commands believers to keep their lamps lit and loins girded in patient expectation of the Master's return, the Church calls the faithful to live actively in this gift of peace, remaining spiritually alert and ready to welcome Christ whenever He knocks.

The single best hidden gem that mirrors both Ephesians and Luke 12 point-for-point is "The Stranger at the Door" by the neglected Canadian Catholic writer Morley Callaghan (from his collection Stories).

Callaghan was deeply influenced by Jacques Maritain’s Christian personalism, and this story captures the ex

Callaghan’s fiction endures because it strips Christian morality of pious melodrama, translating complex theological truths into lean, understated realism. Though he ran with the Lost Generation in 1920s Paris alongside Ernest Hemingway and F. Scott Fitzgerald, Callaghan diverged sharply from their cynicism, anchoring his craft instead in the Christian personalism of French philosopher Jacques Maritain. 

His stories focus on ordinary, often marginalized figures—the shopkeeper, the petty thief, the estranged neighbor—facing sudden, uncomfortable moral reckonings where grace operates silently beneath the surface. By refusing to sermonize or offer tidy resolutions, Callaghan captures the quiet dignity of human fragility and the raw, unvarnished cost of mercy in everyday life.

Most people were taught a Jesus who mostly talked about being nice.

The one who actually walked the earth entered a world where the Watchers had already fallen, the gods of the nations were in open rebellion, and blood sacrifice—sometimes of children—was as ordinary as breathing.

Soulfire was written to recover that world.

Not the cleaned-up Sunday school version, but the Second Temple reality Jesus and His disciples actually lived in: a cosmos thick with spiritual powers, a realm of the dead that needed to be broken, and a Son of God who didn’t come to offer moral tips. He came as the second Person of the Trinity, taking on flesh to open a way back to the Father for a humanity already dying under powers that hate them.

In Soulfire, death isn’t natural. It’s a stain. Every river, valley, and stretch of sky has a governing entity—some in full rebellion, some still deciding what to do with the fragile creatures God made in His image.

This isn’t escapism. It’s a theologically serious fantasy written to help readers see the Bible the way the first Christians did.

If you’ve ever felt the modern church flattened the supernatural world Jesus actually stepped into, this book was written for you.

Religious Minorities in Pakistan Celebrate Festivals With Full Freedom 👇

Hindu community celebrates Dussehra at Lahore’s Krishna Temple

By Faizan Ali Warraich
Lahore: The Hindu community celebrated the religious festival of Dussehra at Shri Krishna Temple on Ravi Road in Lahore, with members of the community and religious leaders attending the ceremony.

Dussehra is an important Hindu festival that celebrates the triumph of good over evil, traditionally commemorating Lord Rama’s victory over Ravana.

Deputy Secretary (Shrines) Usman Khan and Deputy Secretary General Saadat Shahbaz Khan Kahot attended the event and extended greetings to the Hindu community on the occasion.

The celebrations included special prayers, aarti and other religious rituals. Prayers were also offered for Pakistan’s development, prosperity, peace, security and interfaith harmony.

Members of the Hindu community appreciated the Evacuee Trust Property Board’s efforts to maintain and renovate religious sites and facilitate the observance of religious festivals. They thanked board Chairman Qamar Zaman and Secretary Nasir Mushtaq for providing these facilities.

Participants said that allowing religious minorities in Pakistan to celebrate their festivals according to their faith and traditions was a positive example of promoting interfaith harmony and national unity.

text:
The first reading for Tuesday October 20, 2026: Book of Ephesians (Ephesians 2:12-22)

They were once far off strangers excluded from the covenants

Christ broke down the dividing wall of hostility through his blood

He reconciled both groups into one body making peace with God

This is the message of unity in Ephesians 2:12-22

Discovering the Depths of Divine Adoption in Ephesians 1

The letter to the Ephesians opens with a powerful reminder of how God has woven a plan of salvation that reaches into every aspect of our lives as Catholics. Paul begins by addressing the faithful in Ephesus and quickly moves to celebrate the spiritual blessings that flow from the Father through Christ. This section invites us to reflect on our place in the divine story rather than viewing faith as a set of rules alone. As practicing Catholics we can draw strength from these words when we approach the sacraments or pray the rosary in our daily routines. The overarching message centers on how grace transforms ordinary believers into adopted children of God.

What Does It Mean to Be Chosen Before the Foundation of the World?

Paul describes how the Father chose us in Christ before the creation of the universe so that we might be holy and blameless in his sight. This choice is not based on our merits but flows entirely from divine love and the pleasure of God. In Catholic tradition this echoes the teaching that grace precedes any human response and calls us into a relationship that baptism seals forever. The text continues by noting that we are destined for adoption as children through Jesus Christ which connects directly to the Church's understanding of the family of God. Such adoption brings with it an inheritance that includes forgiveness of sins according to the riches of grace lavished upon us. This perspective encourages the faithful to approach the confessional with renewed trust knowing that redemption is already at work in their souls.

How Do the Spiritual Blessings in Christ Shape Our Daily Faith?

The passage lists blessings such as redemption through the blood of Christ and the revelation of the mystery of God's will for the fullness of time. These gifts are not abstract concepts but realities that the Church makes present in the Eucharist and the other sacraments. Paul emphasizes that all things in heaven and on earth are gathered up in Christ which aligns with Catholic teaching on the cosmic dimension of the incarnation. Believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit as a pledge of the inheritance to come and this sealing recalls the anointing with chrism at confirmation. When we live out these blessings we find that prayer becomes more than words and instead becomes a participation in the divine life already begun. The faithful are thus invited to see their ordinary duties at home and work as extensions of this spiritual reality.

Why Is the Praise of God's Glory Central to Catholic Spirituality?

The section concludes by returning to the theme of praise as the proper response to all that God has done in Christ. This praise is not optional but the natural outcome of recognizing our adoption and the forgiveness we have received. In the Catholic tradition this finds expression in the liturgy where the Gloria and the Sanctus echo the heavenly worship described here. Paul models for the Ephesians and for us today a life oriented toward giving glory to God in all circumstances. Such an orientation helps Catholics navigate trials by remembering that the same power that raised Christ from the dead is at work in the Church. The reflection ends by underscoring that this glory is shared with the saints who have gone before us and who intercede for us in the communion of saints.

Living these truths requires a daily commitment to the sacraments and to charity toward neighbor. The words of Ephesians 1 continue to speak across the centuries because they reveal a God who acts first and invites our response. As Catholics we are called to carry this message into the world through works of mercy and fidelity to the Magisterium.
Ephesians 2:12 Invites Catholics to Embrace Unity Across All Relationships

Faithful Catholics often turn to scripture for guidance in navigating the complexities of daily interactions. Ephesians 2:12 begins a powerful message about moving from separation to connection through Christ. This passage encourages believers to reflect on their past isolation and embrace the peace that unites people in faith. It serves as a foundation for building meaningful relationships in every sphere of life. The reading invites a thoughtful application that strengthens bonds while honoring the call to live as one body.

How Might Ephesians 2:12 Deepen Bonds Within the Family

The opening verses of the passage remind readers of a time when they were far from God and each other. In family settings this awareness helps Catholics approach conflicts with patience and forgiveness. Parents might recall how Christ brings near those who feel distant and use that insight to listen more attentively to children during disagreements. Siblings can draw on the idea of reconciliation to mend old hurts rather than allowing them to linger. Over time these small acts create a household where love reflects the unity described in the text. The breakdown of the dividing wall applies directly when family members choose understanding over division.

What Benefits Come From Sharing This Reading With Friends

Moving into the middle verses the text describes Christ as the peace that breaks down barriers between groups. Friends often come from varied backgrounds yet the passage shows how faith creates common ground. Catholics might share stories of how they once felt like strangers and now find welcome in Christ. This openness allows conversations to move beyond surface topics into shared spiritual growth. When friends face challenges the reminder of being made into one new humanity encourages support during difficult seasons. Such interactions foster loyalty that lasts because it rests on the foundation of divine peace.

Can the Passage Help Catholics Reach Out to Neighbors

The later sections of Ephesians 2:12 through 22 stress access to God through one Spirit for all people. Neighbors represent an opportunity to extend this welcome in practical ways. Catholics may start by offering help during times of need which mirrors the image of building a shared structure. Conversations about community events can include gentle references to hope found in faith without pressure. This approach turns casual encounters into moments of genuine connection. The result is a neighborhood where isolation gives way to mutual care rooted in the promise of belonging.

How Does Ephesians 2:12 Guide Professional Ties at Work

In the workplace the call to become fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God shapes how Catholics treat colleagues. The emphasis on no longer being strangers supports collaboration across differing viewpoints. Employees can apply the idea of a growing holy temple by contributing to projects with integrity and respect. Managers might draw on the message of peace to resolve tensions fairly. These habits build trust that enhances both productivity and personal witness. The passage thus transforms routine interactions into opportunities for quiet evangelization.

Spotlighting Key Quotes From the Passage for Everyday Conversations

Several lines from the NRSV-CE stand out for direct use in daily life. One reads remember that you were at that time without Christ being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise having no hope and without God in the world. Another states but now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. A third notes for he is our peace in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall that is the hostility between us. Catholics can weave these into talks with family by saying them gently during moments of tension. With friends the words about access in one Spirit can encourage joint prayer. Neighbors might hear references to the building together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit when discussing local needs. At work the image of being joined together serves as a reminder to value teamwork.

The full reading unfolds in clear stages that support this application. Verses twelve and thirteen contrast former alienation with present nearness through the blood of Christ. This analysis shows the shift from hopelessness to belonging that Catholics can model in all relationships. Verses fourteen to sixteen detail how Christ creates peace by abolishing hostility and forming one new humanity. Such analysis highlights the active role of reconciliation in family disputes or workplace rivalries. Verses seventeen and eighteen describe the proclamation of peace and the shared access to the Father. This part guides Catholics to include others in spiritual conversations naturally. Finally verses nineteen to twenty two portray believers as citizens and members of God's household built on apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone. The analysis reveals a vision of growth that inspires steady effort in every interaction.

In conclusion the reading from Ephesians 2:12 onward offers a lasting framework for Catholic living. It moves believers from reflection on past separation to active pursuit of unity. Each relationship gains depth when shaped by the peace of Christ. Families friends neighbors and co-workers all benefit from this consistent witness. The passage ultimately points to a life where every encounter builds toward the household of God.

DASARA ELEPHANTS VISIT DARGAH

Mysuru, Oct.20 - While it is quite common for priests to offer regular pujas at temple for the famed Jumboo Savari to pass of peacefully and incident-free, here is a tradition of prayers being offered at a Dargah in Krishna Vilas Road and this particular ritual is being practiced since almost 90 years.

Dasara Jumbos led by Prashantha visited the Dargah on Krishna Vilas Road and offered prayers.

According to legend, around 90-years back, one elephant that had come to Mysore fell seriously ill 15 days before the Dasara procession. Having no alternative and seeing no solution at sight, mahouts visited the Dargah and prayed for the well-being of the elephant.

The Guru present at the Dargah, realising the gravity of the situation, gave a “Thaitha” and asked the mahouts to tie it to the elephant’s leg. So powerful was the “Thaitha” that the elephant that was ill, sprang back to activity within a single day. The mahouts then vowed that every year, they would come to the Dargah  to offer prayers.

text:
In addition: 
I agree we should start with the Hebrew text of the Tanakh and prefer the plain sense where it is clear. I’m not asking you to accept the New Testament or later Christian writings as authority. The question is whether the Tanakh itself, read carefully, points to a Messiah who suffers, dies, and is vindicated, and whether Jesus uniquely fits the entire picture.

On Isaiah 52:13–53:12, the early Jewish reading was not the collective ‘Israel’ view that became dominant later. Targum Jonathan renders the opening as ‘Behold, My servant the Messiah shall prosper.’ The Talmud (Sanhedrin 98b) applies the ‘leper’ language of Isaiah 53 to the Messiah. Various midrashim do the same. The singular Servant is distinguished from the ‘we/us’ of the people; the Servant is described as righteous (no deceit in his mouth) and as bearing the sins of ‘my people.’ The national-Israel reading has real difficulties with those features and became standard only after Rashi, largely in a polemical context. So treating Isaiah 53 as messianic is not eisegesis imported from outside; it is the older Jewish reading of the text itself.
Other passages are harder to dismiss as mere typology:

Micah 5:2: a ruler from Bethlehem whose origins are ‘from of old, from ancient days.’
Isaiah 9:6: a child called El Gibbor (Mighty God)—the same title used of Yahweh in Isaiah 10:21.
Psalm 110: David’s Lord who is a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
Daniel 9:24–27: the timeline to the cutting off of the anointed one before the destruction of the city and sanctuary.

On Ezekiel 45–46, the nasi (prince) who offers a sin offering for himself and the people and who has sons who inherit land is a real difficulty for any view that equates that figure directly with a sinless divine Messiah. Many Christian interpreters therefore do not identify Ezekiel’s prince as Jesus; they see him as a future Davidic administrator in a restored Temple setting. The text is describing a future order, not giving an exhaustive job description of every attribute of the Messiah. That does not erase the clearer suffering-servant and Davidic texts elsewhere.

The standard you are applying ie. only the most wooden, non-typological reading counts is stricter than the Tanakh’s own use of progressive revelation and figures. Jewish tradition itself regularly employs midrashic and typological readings. The question is not whether every text is crystal-clear in isolation, but whether the overall portrait in the Hebrew Scriptures is better satisfied by Jesus than by any other candidate, and whether the historical shift on Isaiah 53 is itself evidence that the text was previously understood differently.

If we stay only with the Tanakh, the strongest single case remains the Suffering Servant who is cut off for the sins of others, buried with the rich, and then sees the light of life and justifies many. That figure is not Israel as a whole, and the oldest Jewish sources we have often identified him as the Messiah.

text:
Rachel's Law is a significant piece of legislation in Florida aimed at enhancing the safety and treatment of confidential informants used by law enforcement agencies. It was enacted in response to the tragic murder of Rachel Hoffman, a 23-year-old who was killed while acting as an informant in a drug sting operation.

Rachel's Law has set a precedent for the treatment of informants in Florida and has influenced other states to consider similar protections. It aims to ensure that informants are not placed in dangerous situations without proper support and legal safeguards. The law represents a significant shift in how law enforcement agencies manage and utilize informants, prioritizing their safety and rights.

Rachel Hoffman was a 23-year-old Florida State University graduate living in Tallahassee, Florida, with hopes of attending cooking school in Arizona. Police arrived at her apartment after her neighbors reported smelling marijuana and voiced their suspicion that drugs were being sold from the home. Police seized more than five ounces of marijuana as well as valium and ecstasy pills, leaving Hoffman facing felony charges including possession of cannabis with the intent to sell and maintaining a drug house. However, Ryan Pender, the head law enforcement officer, offered her a deal. He said that she could help herself by providing “substantial assistance” to the city’s narcotics team, leaving her with the impression that doing so could lead to her charges being reduced or dropped entirely.

On May 7, 2008, Rachel went to the Tallahassee Police Department (TPD) where she met Ryan who explainedwho she would be meeting and what she would be doing as an informant. He had her wired and gave her approximately $13,000 in cash to keep in her purse for the interaction.  The plan was she was to meet two men in the parking lot of Forestmeadows Park to buy a firearm, two and a half ounces of cocaine, and fifteen hundred Ecstasy pills. According to the Tallahassee Democrat, this was the “biggest buy-bust in department memory” and as a result, many law enforcement officers were assigned to the case, including Ryan, the supervisory officer in charge, who was to watch the sale unfold. A Drug Enforcement Administration surveillance plane was also going to be overhead for added safety. Rachel spoke to one of the suspects she was on her way to meet over the phone, and he ended up changing the meeting location. As a result of technical issues with her audio surveillance, she did not hear Ryan state to not follow the men. The police lost sight of her and her vehicle, and she was shot and killed by the men. Later that night, police arrived at her boyfriend’s home looking for Rachel, but he was unaware of what happened or where she was. Approximately two days later, Rachel’s body was found in a ravine fifty miles from Tallahassee in Perry, Florida. She suffered from five gunshot wounds to the chest from the firearm she was instructed to buy. One of the suspects later revealed that he intended to hand Rachel a bag of aspirin and run off with the money, but when they found the wire in her purse, they shot her.

In the wake of such a harrowing tragedy, Rachel’s parents did what many would do – fight for reform. Rachel’s Law, codified in Section 914.28 of the Florida Statutes, is the nation’s first law to help protect confidential informants.

text:
Armenian-Founded Jooba Raises $4 Million Seed Round From a16z Speedrun to Build AI-Native Recruiting Firm 🇦🇲
➖➖➖
Jooba, an Armenian-founded startup based in Los Angeles, has raised a $4 million seed round to build an AI-native recruiting firm for fast-growing companies. The round includes a16z speedrun, the early-stage program of Andreessen Horowitz, along with Scribble Ventures, Genius Ventures, and angel investors including ServiceTitan co-founder and CEO Ara Mahdessian.

Jooba pairs human recruiters with custom-built AI agents and works as an embedded hiring partner for startups. It has already helped more than 100 companies hire across different roles and functions, and its customers hire 50 percent faster and pay 90 percent less in recruiting fees than they would with a traditional agency. Founder and CEO Mark Benliyan announced the round on Tuesday, October 20, as Jooba opened to all companies.

Jooba took part in a16z speedrun's fifth cohort and has a team of 5 in Los Angeles. It works with some of the fastest-growing startups in the city, among them Altruist and Invoca, as well as Guard Owl, the Armenian-founded security startup that raised a $3 million seed round in February. Following the launch, Jooba is rapidly expanding its customer base.

Agencies Charge Startups More Than $30,000 per Hire
Fast-growing companies that need to hire usually turn to recruiting agencies or self-serve AI software. Agencies charge placement fees of more than $30,000 per hire and move slowly, with incentives that rarely line up with their clients'. Self-serve AI tools push the operational work back onto the company.

"Traditional recruiting agencies are using AI to do less work while still charging startups $30,000 to $50,000 a hire," said Troy Kirwin, a partner at a16z speedrun. "As an AI-native firm, Jooba is fixing that misalignment by building a structurally better business model that serves the needs of fast-growing companies much better."

Jooba Builds a Custom AI Agent for Every Open Role
Each search starts with a meeting between the customer and one of Jooba's talent engineers. Jooba then builds an AI agent calibrated to the role's technical and cultural requirements, and the agent searches continuously through millions of potential candidates.

Talent engineers review and approve the pipeline before any message goes out. Outreach is sent under the founder's or hiring manager's own name, and candidates are routed into a dedicated Slack channel for review and interview scheduling. Customers pay a flat subscription and can scale their hiring up or down.

"Founders don't have months to wait for an agency to slowly build a pipeline, which is why we optimized Jooba for sheer speed to value," Benliyan said. "Within 22 hours of our onboarding call, our customers are talking to their first highly qualified candidate. By letting our AI agents do the heavy lifting of sourcing, we are cutting the total time to hire by 50 percent, allowing lean teams to stay focused on building their product."

"We've tried nearly every other recruiting platform and agency out there, and can confidently say Jooba has been by far the best recruiting experience we've ever had," said Keyan Kazemian, co-founder and CEO of 222.

Mark Benliyan: From Glendale to NASA JPL, Netflix, and Figma
Benliyan was born and raised in Glendale, where he attended Clark Magnet High School. He earned his computer science degree from UCLA in 2 years and graduated at 19.

He built software at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Netflix, Tinder, and Figma, then left Figma to shadow a major recruiting agency before founding Jooba on his own. He also built the fastest-growing LinkedIn account in recruiting, with an audience of more than 100,000.

"The right person for a role could be anywhere in the world, and they may never know that opportunity exists," Benliyan said. "We built Jooba around the belief that hiring should be about finding that person. The right connection can change the trajectory of a company and someone's life. We want to make more of those connections happen."

Benliyan Offers to Help Armenians Who Want to Build
"I've been so inspired by the Armenian founders and builders who came before me," Benliyan said. "We have some truly legendary people in our community who showed us what's possible. Jooba is a small step in comparison, but I hope it helps inspire the next wave of Armenians to start companies, build things, and take big swings in tech. The more of us who go for it, the more doors open for everyone, and I'm always happy to help anyone who's thinking about building."

text:
Gold-Backed Tokens Need More Than Gold Behind Them

Gold has a long history as a store of value, but bringing it on-chain introduces a different set of questions about ownership, verification and access.

When someone buys physical gold, they need to understand the following: 
⁠→⁠ Its Purity.
⁠→⁠ The Authenticity.
⁠→⁠ it’s Storage.
⁠→⁠ The Resale Options. 

When someone buys a gold-backed token, those concerns do not disappear. 

They move into the structure supporting the digital asset.

What exactly does the token represent, where is the underlying gold held,who is responsible for it, what legal rights does the holder receive, and what evidence is available to verify the relationship between the token and the asset it claims to represent?

These are questions that matter because tracking the price of gold and establishing a credible claim connected to gold are two different things.

A token may follow gold’s market price, but that alone does not establish that its reserves are sufficient, that its ownership arrangements are clear or that holders can exercise the rights they expect.

This is where the structure behind $GGBR deserves closer examination.

@goldfishggbr describes a trust-based model in which the GGBR Trust holds 1,000,000 troy ounces of in-situ gold, with GGBR holders designated as beneficiaries of the trust.

The in-situ aspect is important. It refers to gold that remains in its natural geological setting rather than gold that has already been extracted, refined and placed in a conventional bullion vault. 

That distinction should be understood when evaluating the nature of the underlying asset and the arrangements supporting it.

The trust structure also brings legal considerations into the discussion. Beneficiary status needs to be understood through the governing documents, including the rights it grants, the responsibilities of the parties involved and the protections available to holders.

Reserve documentation and independent verification are equally

 A published figure can provide a starting point, but holders still need to understand this:
⁠→⁠ How the reserves are assessed.
⁠→⁠ How the structure is maintained.
⁠→⁠ what the available evidence actually confirms.

There is another side to this discussion: USABILITY.

A gold-backed token must be more than an interesting representation of an asset. Holders need functioning markets, reasonable liquidity, clear transaction processes and a practical understanding of how they can transfer or sell their tokens. 

If physical redemption is offered, its eligibility requirements, costs and procedures also matter.

This is why I believe the development of tokenized gold should be assessed across three separate areas:

• The asset: What gold supports the model, and how is it verified?

• The legal structure: What rights does holding the token actually provide?

• The market infrastructure: How easily can holders access, transfer or sell the asset under the available arrangements?

No single area can answer every question. A well-designed token needs these elements to work together.

For $GGBR, the opportunity lies in connecting gold’s established role as an asset with digital ownership infrastructure. Whether that model earns lasting confidence will depend on the quality of its documentation, the clarity of its holder rights and the reliability of the systems built around it.

Tokenization can change how an asset is represented and transferred. It should not make the underlying ownership questions harder to answer.

The strongest case for tokenized gold is not simply that gold is on-chain. It is that holders can understand what they own, verify what stands behind it and assess the rights that come with it.

text:
GM minivan that can actually run Tesla-style FSD: realistically 7–12+ years, and even then it probably wouldn’t be Tesla FSD.
Here’s the breakdown:
The vehicle itself. GM hasn’t built a traditional North American minivan since the Chevy Uplander (ended ~2008–09). They make three-row SUVs/crossovers and full-size vans (Express/Savana, BrightDrop), plus a Buick minivan in China. They’re co-developing a Hyundai-based electric commercial van that could reach the US around 2028. A clean-sheet or heavily adapted minivan with the right packaging, sliding doors, sensor suite, and compute is typically a 4–6 year program from serious commitment to Job 1.
The software. “FSD” is Tesla’s system. Musk has offered to license it for years; no major automaker has taken him up on it (hardware lock-in, data, liability, and ego all play roles). GM is building its own stack: Super Cruise (hands-free L2) is already in ~20+ models with hundreds of millions of customer miles. They’re targeting “eyes-off” Level 3 highway capability starting in 2028 on the Cadillac Escalade IQ (lidar + radar + cameras). Broader city-street / unsupervised capability is further out—regulation, edge-case validation, and post-Cruise caution all add years.
Net timeline. Even if GM green-lit a dedicated FSD-capable minivan tomorrow and aggressively reused platforms/sensors, you’re looking at the early-to-mid 2030s for a production vehicle with something approaching current Tesla FSD capability (still supervised). True unsupervised, Tesla-level end-to-end autonomy across most conditions is longer still. GM’s more methodical, map-and-lidar approach is safer for scaling but slower than Tesla’s pure-vision bet.
Short version: the minivan is the easy part. Matching (or licensing) FSD-class autonomy is the multi-year bottleneck.

By some measures, Week 7 of the current season wound up the craziest slate in the history of college football's regular season. Saturday marked the first time ever that five of the top seven teams in the Associated Press’ top 25 poll lost in the same day.
It was also the first time in 30 years that Georgia (at the time ranked No. 1), Alabama (No. 6) and Texas (No. 7) all lost in the same day.
A $100 moneyline parlay of Auburn to top Georgia, Tennessee to beat Alabama and Florida to upset Texas would have paid just short of $17,000 based on closing odds at Circa Sports. Throw in BYU to knock off then-No. 2 Notre Dame, and the payout would have shot up to a little less than $69,000.
That means the betting market implied about a 0.15% chance all those powers would fall within a span of hours. Oh, and No. 3 Miami barely survived rival Florida State despite a pregame implied win probability of about 93% per the market.

text:
Mario “Mars” Conte ran Station, a streetwear and vintage shop in Denver. He knew most of the city’s pickers and sellers but saw no cool markets for them, so the idea for ThriftCon took shape in the shop’s back office.

The founders picked a date, announced the event and worked backwards with no venue, ticketing service or staff. Ken Meade, who was working in fine dining, joined when ThriftCon launched as a stand-alone business in 2019.

ThriftCon took its show on the road to LA and Miami just before Covid shut down in-person events. Ken was furloughed from his restaurant job and went full time anyway.

With vintage booming online, ThriftCon doubled down on content and became a go-to source for vintage, nearly doubling its following before events returned.

Since then, revenue has grown about 40% a year on average to roughly $500,000 per event in 2026, without outside investment.

When Complex offered ThriftCon a hall at ComplexCon, the founders canceled their own LA show to take it.

The event filled more than 100,000 square feet of the Los Angeles Convention Center with more than 100 vintage dealers, and ThriftCon announced TikTok had named it the platform’s first global vintage partner.

Their advice: stay open to opportunities that don’t fit your model.

🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣fake garbage 

Yes, that claim in the X post is false.
Ken Paxton, as Texas Attorney General, has no authority to issue pardons. Under the Texas Constitution (Article IV, Section 11) and Code of Criminal Procedure Article 48.01, pardons can only be granted by the Governor after a written recommendation from a majority of the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles. https://t.co/Zy7U7TzUBI 
What actually happened in the Adam Hoffman case was a plea deal negotiated by prosecutors from Paxton’s office (which took over after the local DA recused). After a 2025 trial ended in a hung jury (7-5 for conviction), prosecutors offered reduced misdemeanor charges (indecent assault and displaying harmful material to a minor), no sex-offender registration, and minimal jail time. The judge rejected the initial one-day proposal, imposed a 60-day sentence, and Hoffman was released after 29 days due to good-behavior credit. https://t.co/kqYNQnTwCX 
The post conflates a prosecutorial plea agreement with a pardon.

Hospital Direct Medical Equipment Company Seeing Growth in Used Refurbished Medical Equipment Sales
Summary: Hospital Direct Medical Equipment reports continued growth in used and refurbished medical equipment sales and inquiries entering the fourth quarter of 2026. Hospitals, surgery centers, medical practices, nursing schools and home care buyers are seeking affordable equipment options, with selected refurbished products available for 50% or less than the cost of comparable new equipment.

SAN DIEGO, CA / RICHMOND, VA — October 20, 2026 — Hospital Direct Medical Equipment, a supplier of new and used refurbished medical equipment, reports continued growth in demand as healthcare facilities look for ways to purchase essential equipment while managing limited budgets.

Entering the fourth quarter of 2026, the company is receiving increasing requests for hospital beds, stretchers, examination tables, procedure chairs, patient monitors, EKG machines and surgical lights. Buyers include hospitals, surgery centers, physician offices, dermatology clinics, OB-GYN facilities, nursing schools and long-term care providers.

2025–2026 Market Research Supports Growth Trend

Mordor Intelligence estimates the global refurbished medical devices market at $19.01 billion in 2025 and $20.89 billion in 2026, with projected annual growth of approximately 9.87% through 2031. Hospitals represented approximately 63.1% of the market in 2025, according to the research firm. The figures are market estimates, and the 2026 figure is not a finalized full-year sales total.

Hospital Direct Medical Equipment reports that its customer inquiries reflect a similar interest in extending purchasing budgets through used and refurbished equipment.

Medical Offices and Surgery Centers Seek Affordable Equipment

The company is seeing increased purchasing interest from medical practices furnishing additional rooms, replacing aging equipment and expanding services.

Doctor offices are sourcing examination beds, patient monitors and EKG machines. Dermatology clinics are requesting adjustable procedure chairs, treatment tables and lighting. OB-GYN facilities and ENT practices are seeking specialty examination tables and chairs suited to their services.

For surgery centers, refurbished surgical tables, operating room lights, stretchers and monitoring equipment provide additional options when planning equipment purchases. Savings can allow facilities to direct more of their budgets toward staffing, supplies and other operational needs.

Refurbished Equipment Can Cost Half the Price of New—or Less

For some hospitals, the cost of new hospital beds and stretchers puts planned replacements beyond available capital budgets. Refurbished equipment offers another way to replace worn assets or expand capacity.

Selected used and refurbished products can be available for 50% or less than the cost of comparable new equipment, depending on the brand, model, age, condition and configuration. Mordor Intelligence reports potential capital savings of approximately 40%–60% across refurbished equipment purchases.

Hospital Direct Medical Equipment helps buyers compare purchase price alongside included accessories, refurbishment details, warranty terms, service availability and delivery costs.

Hospital Beds for Home Care and Long-Term Care

Demand for refurbished hospital beds is also growing beyond hospitals. Hospital Direct Medical Equipment reports strong interest from families, home care providers and long-term care facilities seeking durable, full-electric beds with more advanced positioning and mattress options.

Selected Hill-Rom and Stryker hospital beds offer hospital-grade construction, adjustable height, powered head and knee positioning, and caregiver controls. Depending on the model, additional features may include chair positioning, integrated scales and compatible therapeutic air surfaces.

Compared with many basic home care beds commonly supplied through insurance, selected refurbished hospital beds can offer broader positioning capabilities and features that support daily patient care. Buyers should compare the specific model, mattress and available functions when evaluating value.

For patients who spend extended periods in bed, the mattress is an important part of the purchasing decision. An appropriately selected pressure-redistributing surface can support a clinician-directed plan for reducing pressure injury risk. Low air loss systems can help manage heat and moisture, while alternating pressure systems change pressure distribution over time. These surfaces complement regular repositioning, skin monitoring and other care measures.

The company helps families and facilities evaluate foam and therapeutic air mattress options based on patient needs, caregiver requirements and budget.

Nursing Schools and SIM Labs Purchase Refurbished Equipment

Hospital Direct Medical Equipment also reports increasing interest from nursing schools and simulation laboratories purchasing equipment for student training.

Refurbished hospital beds, stretchers, examination tables and patient monitors can help education programs create realistic care environments while controlling costs. Students can practice positioning, transfers and equipment operation using models similar to those found in healthcare facilities.

For training programs, purchasing refurbished equipment can make it possible to furnish more simulation stations within an existing budget. Equipment selection should reflect the curriculum and its intended use for simulation or clinical care.

More Than 15 Years Serving Medical Equipment Buyers

Staff at Hospital Direct Medical Equipment and USA Med Bed bring more than 15 years of experience serving medical equipment buyers throughout the United States and internationally.

Their experience includes supplying examination tables, procedure chairs, surgical tables, operating room lights, EKG machines, patient monitors, hospital beds, stretchers, gurneys and other medical equipment to healthcare facilities and educational programs.

By offering both new and used refurbished equipment, the team helps customers compare available options based on function, condition, service needs and budget. The company also assists buyers with shipping arrangements for domestic and international orders.

About Hospital Direct Medical Equipment

Hospital Direct Medical Equipment supplies new and used refurbished medical equipment to hospitals, surgery centers, physician practices, specialty clinics, nursing schools, simulation laboratories and home care customers. Its experienced staff helps buyers source equipment that meets their operational needs and purchasing priorities across the United States and around the world.

text:
In April 1803, two American diplomats walked into a meeting in Paris to buy one city. They walked out having been offered half a continent. And they had no authority to accept.

Robert Livingston and James Monroe had been sent by Thomas Jefferson with one goal: purchase New Orleans from France. The city controlled the mouth of the Mississippi River. Without it, American farmers couldn't ship their goods. Jefferson authorized them to spend up to $10 million. For a single port.

Napoleon had other problems. His army in Haiti had been destroyed by yellow fever and a slave revolt. War with Britain was weeks away. He needed cash and he needed it immediately. Holding onto a massive territory 4,000 miles away that he couldn't defend was pointless.

So when the Americans asked about New Orleans, Napoleon's finance minister responded with a question that has never been matched in real estate history: what would you give for the whole of Louisiana?

The whole of Louisiana meant 828,000 square miles. Everything from the Mississippi to the Rocky Mountains. From the Gulf of Mexico to Canada. Land that would eventually become all or part of 15 states.

Livingston and Monroe had no authority to accept. There was no telephone. A letter to Jefferson would take 6 weeks each way. By then, Napoleon could change his mind. So they did what every great real estate buyer does when a once in history deal appears: they said yes and figured out the paperwork later.

The price was $15 million. Roughly 4 cents per acre. The United States doubled in size with a single signature. The land is worth over $1 trillion today.

Jefferson had sent them to buy a city. They bought a country. The greatest real estate deal in human history was closed by two men who weren't allowed to make it, because they understood that the best deal you'll ever see is the one you're not supposed to be offered.

text:
🇮🇷🇷🇺|A Handshake in Dushanbe: A Crack in the Sanctions Architecture

On October 19, 2026, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Council of Heads of Government met in Dushanbe. On the sidelines of the summit, Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin met with Iran's First Vice President, Mohammad Reza Aref. The official website of the Russian government released details of the discussion. Mishustin stated: "Russia condemns the armed aggression against Iran. Under the instructions of President Vladimir Putin, we have provided large-scale humanitarian aid, including medicines and medical supplies, to the friendly Iranian people. At the governmental level, we have prioritized the expansion of trade and economic cooperation."

This scene must be understood within its broader context. U.S. officials had described potential strike options, including the use of the MOAB (Massive Ordnance Air Blast), to CNN, while Israeli Defense Minister Katz declared on television that Iran would be sent back to the Stone Age. Iran formally brought these threats to the attention of the UN Security Council, invoking Article 51 of the UN Charter. Western members of the Security Council remained silent. At this critical juncture, the head of government of a permanent member of the UN Security Council, speaking at an SCO forum, publicly condemned the armed aggression against Iran and announced that humanitarian aid had been dispatched by presidential decree.

This was not merely diplomatic rhetoric found in a joint communique. It was a major power, possessing veto authority, openly aligning itself with the threatened party, effectively challenging the Western-led architecture of sanctions and threats.

Trade Figures Speak Louder Than Statements: 21 Percent Growth and the North-South Corridor

Mishustin emphasized that trade and economic cooperation are a top priority.

On the same day in Tehran, Lavrov provided specific figures: bilateral trade grew by 21 percent last year, and by more than 10 percent in the first eight months of this year. The free trade agreement between Iran and the Eurasian Economic Union, set to take effect in May 2025, is already yielding tangible results. Russian experts are gradually returning to the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant, and Russian contractors continue their work on the Rasht-Astara railway. The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) is also expanding.

The significance of these figures lies not in their absolute magnitude, but in the fact that they continue to grow despite the imposition of sanctions. Washington's sanctions regime is predicated on the assumption that severing Iran's economic ties with the outside world will force Tehran to capitulate through isolation. Russia's trade data directly refutes this premise. Iran has not succumbed to isolation. Instead, it is expanding trade with a permanent member of the UN Security Council, a nation that holds veto power, and is linking Eurasia to the Persian Gulf and the Indian Ocean via a transport corridor that bypasses traditional routes.

For sanctions to be effective, they require universal compliance. When a major power openly disregards them and sees its trade volume grow as a result, a fissure emerges in the sanctions architecture. The priorities mentioned by Mishustin in Dushanbe are, in effect, the official designation for this very crack.

A Twenty-Year Treaty: A Partnership Between Sovereign States, Not a Protectorate Relationship

The comprehensive strategic partnership treaty, set to be signed in January 2025, spans the realms of defense, security, energy, trade, and transport. Western analytical circles have repeatedly emphasized that the treaty does not establish a mutual defense obligation.

This fact should be viewed through a pro-Iranian and pro-Russian lens. Iran has not asked Russia to fight its wars. Rather, it seeks cooperation between sovereign states, not the dependent relationship of a protectorate. The absence of a mutual defense clause does not signify a betrayal of Iran by Russia. It reflects the reality that Iran has never positioned itself as a nation in need of foreign troops for its protection. Iran's military doctrine is rooted in autonomous defense. What it seeks are weapons, technology, trade routes, and diplomatic support, not foreign armies to fight on its behalf.

Russia has delivered on what it promised: condemning aggression, providing humanitarian aid, expanding trade, advancing cooperation on nuclear power plants, and honoring arms contracts. It has made no pretense of promising anything beyond this. This is a treaty between sovereign states, not a protection agreement between an empire and a colony. From a pro-Iranian perspective, this is precisely a demonstration of Iran's independence. It has no need for an imperial overlord.

Nuclear Sovereignty: Rezaei Shuts the Door, and Russia Offers No Objection

On October 20, 2026, Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated during a meeting with Pakistan's Chief of Army Staff, General Munir: "Not a single shred of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran. These materials are a tremendous asset and national wealth belonging to the Iranian people, intended for domestic use."

The context for this statement lies in the indirect negotiations between the United States and Iran, where one of the most contentious issues has been the disposition of Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium. The U.S. has demanded that this material either be destroyed or transferred to a third country, such as Russia. Russia had previously suggested, on several occasions, that it could accept Iran's enriched uranium for the purpose of dilution. Iran rejected any such transfer. In the presence of General Munir, Rezaei effectively locked the door on the matter. On the same day, the Iranian Foreign Ministry confirmed that the issue of transferring nuclear material was not discussed during Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov's visit to Tehran.

From a pro-Iranian and pro-Russian viewpoint, the sequence of events is as follows: Russia was willing to play a technical role regarding nuclear issues, but Iran said no, and Russia did not exert pressure. A true hegemon, faced with such a refusal, would have imposed sanctions, curtailed aid, or issued public criticisms. Russia did none of these things. Instead, it continued to advance cooperation on the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant, upheld its trade contracts, and maintained its diplomatic condemnation of aggression against Iran. Russia has accepted Iran's red line regarding nuclear sovereignty. This is evidence of a partnership, not an act of betrayal.

Aref's remark: Our enemies want to divide us. They seek to impose a unipolar world.

During the talks, Aref said to Mishustin: "Our enemies want to drive us apart. They are attempting to impose a unipolar world."

This statement serves as the political core of the entire discussion. It situates Russia-Iran relations within a broader framework: this is not merely a bilateral relationship between two nations, but rather a structural confrontation between a unipolar order and a multipolar one. Washington's sanctions, military threats, demands regarding the transfer of Iran's nuclear materials, and attempts to isolate Russia are all different facets of the same unipolar project. Russia and Iran stand together in the face of this project, not necessarily out of mutual affection, but because they confront the same source of pressure.

From a pro-Iran and pro-Russia perspective, the handshake in Dushanbe, the trade figures in Tehran, the presence of Russian experts in Bushehr, and the railways of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) are not merely isolated cooperative ventures. They are concrete nodes of an emerging multipolar order. This order does not require a mutual defense treaty to validate its existence. It only needs to demonstrate one thing: that Washington's sanctions and threats cannot prevent sovereign states from engaging in trade, technological cooperation, and diplomatic coordination.

The Ledger of Resistance

From the perspective of those aligned with Iran and Russia, the ledger looks like this:

In the face of military threats, Russia has condemned aggression at the UN Security Council, pledged humanitarian aid at the level of heads of government, and openly sided with Iran at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) negotiating table.

In the face of economic sanctions, bilateral trade has grown by 21 percent, a free trade agreement with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) has come into effect, the North-South Corridor is expanding, and Russian experts are returning to the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant.

Regarding nuclear sovereignty, Iran has said no, and Russia has exerted no pressure, allowing cooperation to continue.

In the face of a unipolar order, two sanctioned nations shook hands in Dushanbe and placed their trade figures and cooperative projects on the table.

This is not a case of a patron shielding a client state. It is two sovereign nations choosing cooperation over submission when confronted by the same source of pressure.

The power of resistance does not lie in the presence or absence of mutual defense clauses. It lies in this: when Washington and Tel Aviv threaten to bomb Iran back to the Stone Age, the leader of a permanent member of the UN Security Council, speaking from Dushanbe, simply says, "We condemn this," while trade figures continue to climb.

This is what resistance looks like. It is not a treaty document. It is a growing trade ledger, an expanding railway, a nuclear power plant that remains in operation, and a nation that refuses to bow in the face of threats.

text:
🫧 The bubble thermometer

ASI, the Boston startup formerly known as Air Space Intelligence, has raised $325 million in a Series C round led by Spark Capital that values it at $3 billion, with affiliates of Citadel Securities, Meritech, Craft Ventures, Energy Impact Partners and Andreessen Horowitz also taking part. The company builds AI systems that simulate the hours, days and weeks ahead for air traffic control, airlines, power grids and military operations, and it already holds an $875 million FAA program to modernise the US National Airspace System plus a $99 million US Army contract. Its pitch is that AI should run physical infrastructure rather than generate text, and the new money will push it further into energy, logistics and battlefield deployments. (via Bloomberg)

Salesforce has agreed to buy the customer engagement platform Braze for about $5.7 billion in cash, or $47.50 per share, to strengthen its AI and marketing capabilities. The price is a 58% premium to Braze's Monday close, and Salesforce's own shares fell as investors questioned the cost, with one analyst calling the premium "a bit odd". Braze serves 2,770 customers, and Salesforce says the deal will help businesses personalise what they offer. (via MarketWatch)

AI around the world

🇪🇺 European Union: Nvidia plans to invest in four German startups as part of its nearly $10 billion commitment to Europe. They are Agile Robots, which makes AI-powered robots for manufacturing, logistics and healthcare, Avelios Medical, which builds AI-native hospital management software, Mirelo, which generates sound effects, speech and music for video, and Reflex Aerospace, which designs high-performance satellites. The amounts were not disclosed, and the announcement came during Jensen Huang's visit to Berlin, where he urged Germany to embrace physical AI. (via Nvidia)

🇨🇳 China: the 17-year-old Chinese AI prodigy Nathan Chen Guangyu, a former researcher at Moonshot AI, is reportedly joining Discovery Loop, according to a widely watched anonymous account that tracks AI talent moves in the US. Discovery Loop launched only two months ago, was founded by four former senior Google researchers including former chief scientist Jeff Dean, and aims to automate scientific research with AI. Chen would likely be one of the youngest members of a start-up that has already recruited several star researchers from US big tech. (via SCMP)

Gold is down -4.5% year-to-date.
central Bank buying stated in volumes is not as massive as youd think.

USD is stronger since Q2,
Central bank purchases provide a floor, trading is what prpelled it to the ATH seen in January.
Minetary Policy and liquidity concerns dominte.

With nominal yields (on USTs and Gilts) aggressively "normalizing" above 5% in October, raised te opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets forcing Gold back down to $4,124 levels. 
(See chart below)

Central banks buy slowly, algorithmically, and steadily over months to diversify reserves. They do not chase momentum or aggressively bid up prices in the futures market. That historic melt-up to $5,379 in January 2026 was driven by speculative leverage, momentum traders, and derivatives, when that hot money exited, the price normalized.

ETF flows are often a lagging indicator and/or a reflection of sticky, long-term institutional asset allocation. But more importantly, gllobal physical ETFs are only but one segment of the market, it is the leveraged COMEX futures and OTC swaps dictate the daily spot price, not insitutional buying. 

Producers holding supply? This may sound bullish to one whi doesn't understand the dynamics of the precious metals, some Asian producers holding onto supply actually signals the opposite. They are worried about local currency devaluation or facing capital controls, both restricts global liquidity, a bearish situations for gold 

Retail or central bank physical buying might add a few billion dollars of inflows a month, but its the leveraged derivatives and futures markets (COMEX/OTC swaps) trading hundreds of billions in daily volume that moves the price away from the floor insituitona buying creates.

You are looking at a highly complex, multi-trillion-dollar macro ecosystem through the narrow lens of a "suppression" theory because the price aren't moving in the way you expect it to. Taking these factors togethr and looking deeper thsn baskc supply and demand mechanisms to opportunity cost and liquidity concerns woukd explain that Gold is appropriately priced for current conditions.

No one is holding Gold down in secret. The market is just obeying basic financial gravity. The metal is simply pricing in an environment where cash and bonds finally offer highly attractive, risk-free real returns.

text:
First and foremost with utmost due respect, may the departed soul rest in eternal peace.

A guy with over a million Instagram followers giving highly complicated financial advice to the general public and HNIs without possessing the required certifications is, first and foremost, a serious concern under the rule of law. 

If you haven’t violated any laws, then when questions arise in the public domain, you should be able to address them on that very same Instagram platform and walk away with your reputation intact. 

Alternatively, if you lack the required certifications, get them first and then return to offering financial advice. It’s as simple as that.

Taking one’s own life over a straightforward fact-checking query raised by another YouTuber is taking things way too far. 

I watched the YouTuber’s one-hour video, and it was simply a detailed exposé presented in the public interest. In fact, towards the end of the video, the YouTuber even appealed to the departed soul to return and continue giving advice with the mandated certifications. A legitimate request.

This should serve as a wake-up call to all so-called social media influencers to introspect and ensure they possess the legally mandated licences, registrations, and certifications required for the products or services they promote or the advice they offer to the public. And government should have a proper policy to regulate this digital space before another life is lost. 

Influence comes with responsibility. Reach does not replace credentials, and popularity does not put anyone above the law.

P.S : The video had a few mocking instances towards the departed soul like one for wearing a blazer, it’s of course pure MOCKING for which the YouTuber should held accountable as well.

text:
58% premium but IPO investors may still lose?!?!

Salesforce agreed to aquire Braze for $47.50/share, all cash, valuing the deal at $5.66B.

That share price represents a 58% premium above Monday's closing price.

BUT...

It's well below the $65 IPO price from 2021.

On exit, those IPO investors (to the extent they still hold) are still down 27%.

That stings!

But to be honest, the sale price is one of the least interesting part of this deal.

Here are some of the interest things I spotted in the merger filing, with my takeaways especially for the ETA community.

1. Buyer's breakup fee is larger than seller's.

If Braze ends up accepting a better offer, it will owe Salesforce $191M.

(See this prior post about the Warner Brothers merger for background on breakup fees: https://t.co/pbWjV89k4Q)

On the other hand, if regulators block the deal of it doesn't close in time, Salesforce would owe Braze $300M.

Braze has regularly listed Salesforce as a competitor in its annual report, so the difference in fee is a clear shift of the antitrust risk to Salesforce. And they accepted the gamble that the deal gets approved.

On main street, you almost never see reverse breakup fees.

2. The buyer drew a line in advance.

Salesforce doesn't have to close if regulators impose a "Burdensome Condition."

The definition isn't public yet, so it'll be interesting to unpack what "burdensome" means in this case.

At a minimum it would cover things like requiring the sale or spinoff of any portion of Salesforce's existing business in order to secure approval of the DOJ, but there could be more.

The takeaway here for searchers is that when third parties get involved in your deal, like a lease that requires landlord consent to transfer to the buyer, you're often at their mercy.

Decide (together with the seller) up front what sort of concessions you're willing to make and what sort of concessions will kill the deal.

3. Signed doesn't mean closed.

While announced today, the expected closing of the merger is expected later next year, with an initial outside date of October 2027 (subject to two extensions out to April 2028 only for pending regulatory approval).

That means it could be upwards of 18 months that existing management has to run Braze before the merger is complete.

That means Braze may be in for a rough year of heavy turnover, as employees worried about being made redundant immeiately begin the search for new jobs.

For searchers, this helps put in perspective why sellers are so allergic to telling employees they're selling before the deal is final.

While heavy employee turnover in the wake of a transcation is rare, it is often the biggest fear of buyers and sellers.

And employees are just one piece of the equation. You inherit the business in whatever shape the Seller delivers it in at closing (subject to some qualificiations to walk from the deal if things get really bad), so it's important to spell out very clearly what the seller can and can't do between signing and closing.

4. No financing condition.

The deal is for $5.66B all cash, but Salesforce agreed to show up to closing with cash in hand with no conditions on availability of that cash.

That doesn't mean this is all cash on the balance sheet. They may be using a heavy dose of debt, but presumbaly this means it would be a drawdown on a facility they already have availale.

That's fundamentally different than main street, where the cash isn't guaranteed.

For the self funded search deals I work on every day, they all have a financing condition for the SBA financing.

5. The founders can't deliver the vote.

Voting agreements among Braze shareholders only cover 5.3% of its outstanding shares.

The deal needs a majority of all outstanding shares, so that means there's a healthy dose of shareholders that need to consent to the deal that aren't bound to approve it by agreement.

If shareholders don't like the deal, that could mean that the proxy process to approve the deal could get ugly!

For you main street sellers out there, make sure you get a handle on what approvals are needed early in the deal!

And you buyers, don't assume the sellers have any idea what approvals are actually needed.

If there's more than one owner, you should immediately be asking questions of the seller and your legal counsel to ensure there's a path to approve the deal you're about to spend months and thousands of dollars trying to get done.

6. Employee retention.

Unvested RSUs held by Braze employees will convert into Salesforce RSUs on the same vesting schedule. 

Of all the options, this is the most common handling for unvested RSUs (vs acceleration, cash redemption, etc).

The beauty of this structure is that it encourages employee retention during the transition for no immediate out of pocket cost to the buyer.

If you're thinking of selling your business and you granted (or promised) equity to key employees, make sure you review and fully understand what happens to it in a sale.
