🇺🇸🇷🇺 WHY DOES TRUMP LOVE PUTIN? ZELENSKY MAY HAVE FINALLY FOUND THE ANSWER.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky believes he understands why Donald Trump has such an extraordinary admiration for Vladimir Putin. According to Washington Post columnist Max Boot, the explanation may be much simpler than secret conspiracies or hidden intelligence operations: Trump admires enormous wealth, unlimited power, and men who possess both.

For years, people have speculated about a sinister connection between Trump and Putin. Yet Boot argues that convincing evidence of a secret arrangement would likely have emerged during the four years Democrats controlled the White House and had access to classified intelligence. Zelensky offered a different explanation in an interview with the Financial Times: Trump simply admires autocrats and the ultrawealthy. "He openly and loudly says that he loves and respects such people," Zelensky observed.

Trump may see Putin not merely as a dictator who has ruled Russia for decades, but as a fellow billionaire. Estimates of Putin's alleged hidden fortune range from $40 billion to an astonishing $250 billion, although these figures remain impossible to independently verify. To Trump, who constantly measures success through money, influence, and personal dominance, Putin represents something deeply attractive: a man who has accumulated extraordinary wealth while exercising virtually unchecked political power.

And this admiration raises uncomfortable questions about Trump's own presidency. Critics, ethics experts, and independent journalists have repeatedly accused him of using public office to benefit his family and private business interests. Several areas have attracted particular scrutiny.

First, cryptocurrency. Trump's dramatic transformation from cryptocurrency skeptic to enthusiastic supporter coincided with the emergence of family-linked ventures, including World Liberty Financial. Critics question whether financial interests connected to the president create opportunities for wealthy investors and foreign actors to purchase political influence.

Second, foreign business deals. Although Trump's sons formally manage the family business, the Trump Organization continues pursuing international licensing agreements, real estate developments, and golf projects. Ethics watchdogs argue that these arrangements create serious conflicts of interest when foreign governments and investors have business relationships with the president's family.

Third, financial markets. Democratic lawmakers and financial analysts have raised concerns about suspicious trading activity surrounding major presidential announcements, particularly decisions involving tariffs and economic policy. They have called for investigations into whether politically connected investors benefited from advance knowledge. Suspicion, however, is not proof of insider trading.

Fourth, legal protection. Critics accuse the administration of weakening independent oversight and using executive authority to protect political and financial interests. Decisions involving federal investigations, regulatory enforcement, and the Justice Department have intensified concerns about whether presidential power is being used to shield allies and business associates from accountability.

This brings us back to Putin. The Russian dictator has built a political system in which enormous wealth, personal loyalty, state institutions, and political survival are closely intertwined. Independent opposition has been crushed, critical journalists have faced persecution, and powerful businessmen understand that their fortunes depend on loyalty to the Kremlin.

Perhaps this is precisely what Trump admires. Putin does not face meaningful electoral competition, independent institutional checks, or the kind of public accountability that democratic leaders must endure. He can remain in power for decades while surrounding himself with extraordinary luxury and unquestioning loyalty.

🔐 END-OF-DAY MARKET REPORT — OCTOBER 20, 2026
━━━
🌐 TOP NEWS OF THE DAY
Brent crude is trading around $110, near its highest levels since May. Attacks on tankers and energy facilities around the Strait of Hormuz have resumed. Iran's First Vice President said there was "no other option left" but to take control of the strait. Meanwhile, Gulf crude oil exports have recovered to approximately 80% of pre-war levels.
Wall Street rebounded on Monday: the Nasdaq rose 1.1% to 26,430, the S&P 500 gained 0.4%, and the Dow slipped 0.1%. The semiconductor index closed up 2.5% after an eight-day losing streak, recovering part of the previous week's 11.5% sell-off driven by concerns over AI financing.

Treasury yields are rising: the U.S. 10-year yield stands at 5.14%, while the 2-year yield is at 4.77%. The Fed is expected to leave rates unchanged on October 28, but CME FedWatch is pricing in approximately an 89% probability of a rate hike in December. September U.S. inflation came in at 3.7%, above expectations of 3.6%.

AI borrowing is in focus: S&P Global warned that major cloud companies carry more AI-related debt than they have disclosed. CoreWeave fell to a 52-week low despite Goldman Sachs maintaining a "Buy" rating; the yield on its 2032 bond is around 14.9%.

GM reported better-than-expected third-quarter results, with earnings per share of $3.70 and revenue of $50.02 billion, and approved a $20 billion buyback program. However, after narrowing its full-year profit forecast, the stock fell approximately 5% in premarket trading.

The CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate. As a result, the SEC is moving forward with its own "Regulation Crypto Assets" proposal. The 60-day public comment period ended today, with approximately 140 comments submitted. The proposal includes a safe harbor under which qualifying tokens would not be considered investment contracts, as well as exemptions for smaller issuances.

Total crypto market capitalization stands at around $2.7 trillion, Bitcoin dominance is 60.3%, and the Fear & Greed Index is in neutral territory, ranging between 49 and 55 depending on the source.

━━━
₿ BITCOIN

bitcoin:native  fluctuated within the $81,300–$81,800 range during the day, trading around $81,400 after declining approximately 1.3%–1.6% over the past 24 hours. Its range over the past week was $79,676–$84,070. The $82,000 level has turned from support into resistance. A recovery will not be considered meaningful until BTC breaks above $82,600 and $83,450, while losing the $84,000 area continues to reflect a weak trend. On the downside, $80,000–$79,700 is the first major support zone. A break below it would bring $77,500–$78,000 and subsequently $76,000 into focus. On the daily Ichimoku chart, the price is below both the Tenkan line (approximately $81,970) and the Kijun line (approximately $83,460), indicating a pressured technical structure.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $526.6 million in net inflows on Monday. IBIT alone accounted for $665 million, marking the largest daily inflow since October 2025. The combined outflows over the previous two weeks, however, totaled approximately $910 million. According to Glassnode, although selling pressure is easing, spot and ETF demand remains too weak to sustain a lasting rally. The futures market continues to drive selling pressure. Funding rates in derivatives markets are slightly positive, and leverage is not excessive.
BTC remains highly correlated with the S&P 500. Risk appetite driven by interest rates and oil prices continues to be a decisive factor.

━━━
🔷 ETHEREUM & ALTCOINS

ethereum:native  is trading around $2,380, down 1.6%–2% on the day and approximately 6% over the week. Its monthly loss has reached 8.6%. Support stands at $2,313–$2,357, with resistance at $2,405 and then $2,535, the weekly high. ETH ETFs have also experienced outflows in recent weeks.

BNB is flat at $727 (+0.3%), SOL is at $104 (-1.4%), ripple:native  at $1.29 (-1.3%), DOGE at $0.079 (-0.8%), and ADA at $0.216 (-2.1%). Market breadth is weak: 65 of the 88 tracked assets declined.

Notable movers: NEAR fell 6.5% to $4.73. HYPE declined 1.8% to $78 but remains up approximately 200% year over year. ZEC fell 3.3% to $1,126. In the privacy sector, Monero rose 3.5% to $615, while Worldcoin posted the day's strongest major move, gaining 8.6%. World Liberty Financial was among the biggest decliners, falling 5.4%.
━━━
📋 KEY CRYPTOCURRENCY NEWS

BlackRock filed for the "iShares Bitcoin Managed Protect ETF," which tracks IBIT and offers downside protection. Details such as the protection level and return cap have not yet been disclosed.

Strive purchased $335 million worth of Bitcoin using $369 million raised from investors.

Solana treasury company SkyAI sold its entire SOL holdings and launched a $201 million share buyback program.

The CFTC rejected CME's legal position in the dispute over perpetual futures trading. The decision could have significant implications for the regulatory framework governing perpetual futures markets in the United States.
Tether responded to an investigation by a senator, arguing that its own efforts have reduced Iran-linked transaction volumes.

Mesh partnered with Visa to enable users to spend crypto and stablecoin balances without requiring separate cards. Mastercard, meanwhile, announced a tool designed to screen stablecoin payments for fraud and sanctions risks.

━━━
🔓 TOKEN UNLOCKS

AERO (Aerodrome) — October 22, approximately 02:58 Turkey time (estimated timing for the transition between weekly emission periods). Estimated value: $3.54 million, equivalent to approximately 4.4 million AERO, or around 0.30% of the circulating supply. Recipients: liquidity providers and vote-escrow token holders (protocol emissions). Selling pressure: 🟢. The Aerodrome–Velodrome merger and token conversion begin on October 21. The conversion period, combined with emissions, could create short-term volatility.

SCR (Scroll) — Around October 22; time unspecified. Estimated value: $1.72 million, equivalent to approximately 86 million SCR at a price of about $0.02. Tokenomist shows a ratio of approximately 20%, but the calculation methodology could not be verified. Recipient profile: ecosystem and growth fund. Selling pressure: 🟡. The token's low price results in a large token quantity, while the dollar impact remains limited. The date and amount are based on Tokenomist data and may not be final.

━━━
🔭 OUTLOOK AND UPCOMING EVENTS

In the short term, the key drivers for BTC are coming from outside the crypto market. If oil prices sustain levels above $110 and Treasury yields continue rising, they will limit the upside potential of risk assets. Monday's surge in ETF inflows did not translate into a corresponding price increase, suggesting that buyers are present but lack sufficient strength to overcome the selling wall above $82,000 on their own. As long as the $79,700–$80,000 range holds, range-bound trading between $80,000 and $82,600 remains the main scenario. A daily close below this range would bring a test of $77,500 into focus.

Tonight at 23:30 Turkey time, SpaceX will release its first earnings report following its IPO, providing an additional signal for sentiment toward AI and technology stocks. The October 27–28 FOMC meeting is the key threshold of the week. Even if rates remain unchanged, stronger signals pointing toward a December rate hike could cause ETH and altcoins to react more sharply than BTC.
With the SEC's public comment period now closed, the final rule proposal and the CFTC's decision on perpetual futures will shape the regulatory agenda in the absence of congressional action. The first trading days following the Aerodrome–Velodrome merger should also be monitored closely across the DeFi sector.

I made a nifty chart for Christians this election cycle.

Below are some important social topics and how the Bible overwhelmingly aligns with Republican/Conservative views.

Abortion: Conservatives support pro-life policies that protect the unborn from conception, aligning with Scripture’s clear teaching that God forms and knows people in the womb (Ps 139:13-16; Jer 1:5) and that shedding innocent blood is among the things He hates (Prov 6:16-17; Exod 20:13). This includes eliminating abortion procedures, supporting alternatives like adoption, encouraging celibacy until marriage, and defending the vulnerable who cannot speak for themselves (Prov 31:8-9). Liberals promote expansive abortion access, including late-term and taxpayer-funded procedures through groups like Planned Parenthood, which treats the unborn as disposable rather than sacred image-bearers (Gen 1:27). Such a position prioritizes personal autonomy over divine sovereignty in the creation of life and fails to uphold justice for the innocent. Science clearly shows us that a human being's life begins at conception, and the Bible tells us that intentional killing of an innocent human being is immoral. The development or location of a human being does not dictate their worth. Human beings do not magically acquire God's image randomly in fetal development. We have it the moment we were conceived.

Law & Order: Conservatives emphasize strong policing, swift justice, and deterrence, consistent with the biblical mandate that governing authorities are God’s servants who bear the sword to punish evil and maintain order (Rom 13:1-4; 1 Pet 2:13-14). This reflects principles of retribution and protection of the righteous (Exod 21:23-25; Prov 14:34). Liberals often favor reduced enforcement, no-cash bail, and lighter sentencing that can embolden lawlessness, contrary to the warning that delayed punishment encourages evil (Eccl 8:11) and the call to purge evil from the community (Deut 19:18-20). While compassion for the imprisoned is biblical (Matt 25:36), unchecked leniency undermines the government’s God-given role.

Homosexuality/Gay Marriage: Conservatives uphold marriage as the union of one man and one woman for companionship and procreation, matching the creation pattern Jesus affirmed (Gen 2:24; Matt 19:4-6). Homosexual practice is described as contrary to nature and sinful (Rom 1:26-27; Lev 18:22), yet the gospel offers hope of transformation (1 Cor 6:9-11). Liberals promote same-sex marriage, pride celebrations, and institutional affirmation of the behavior, which conflicts with the call to repent and turn from sexual immorality (1 Thess 4:3-5) and the command to honor the marriage bed (Heb 13:4). Affirming sin is not love; Scripture calls for both grace and truth.

Transgenderism: Conservatives affirm biological sex as fixed by God’s design (Gen 1:27; Matt 19:4) and oppose medical transitions for minors or the redefinition of sex in sports and law, protecting bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19-20) and rejecting cross-dressing or body mutilation (Deut 22:5; Lev 19:28). Identity is found in Christ, not self-perception (Rom 12:2). Liberals endorse gender-affirming care, puberty blockers, surgeries, and self-identification that overrides biology, treating gender as a social construct rather than a created reality (Ps 139:13-14). This approach denies the goodness of God’s male-female design.

Immigration and Border Security: Conservatives advocate secure borders, legal pathways, and enforcement of the law, consistent with submission to governing authorities and the recognition that God set boundaries for nations (Rom 13:1-2; Acts 17:26). Hospitality to the foreigner (Lev 19:34) is balanced with order and protection of citizens (1 Tim 5:8). Liberals often support reduced enforcement, amnesty, and open-border policies that disregard national sovereignty and can strain resources or enable disorder, contrary to the need for wise governance and defined boundaries (Neh 2:17-20). Compassion does not require lawlessness.

Secularism in Public Schools: Conservatives support parental choice, school prayer, and the inclusion of biblical or creation perspectives alongside other views, aligning with the command to teach children the fear of the Lord (Deut 6:6-7; Prov 1:7; Prov 22:6). Liberals enforce strict secularism, removal of religious expression, and curricula that often promote moral relativism or exclusive evolution, which suppresses the knowledge of God (Rom 1:20-21) and limits parents’ ability to raise children in the faith (Eph 6:4). Education without God leads to a lack of knowledge (Hos 4:6).

Loving Your Neighbor (Biblical Agape Love): Conservatives understand agape as selfless, truth-telling love that seeks another’s eternal good, including gentle correction and calling people out of sin (Eph 4:15; Gal 6:1; Prov 27:6). True love warns of danger and shares the gospel so people can have eternal life (Ezek 3:18; Jas 5:20). Liberals often redefine love as affirmation of any identity or behavior, including sin, under the banner that “love wins.” This contradicts Scripture’s insistence that love rejoices in the truth (1 Cor 13:6) and that Jesus both showed mercy and said “go and sin no more” (John 8:11). Affirmation of destructive choices is not sacrificial love.

Charity: Conservatives prefer voluntary, cheerful giving through churches, private charities, and personal donations (2 Cor 9:7; Jas 1:27), which data consistently shows Republicans practice at higher rates and in larger amounts than Democrats at comparable incomes. Churches and local charities often deliver aid more efficiently and with biblical accountability. Liberals favor higher taxes to expand government welfare programs that are frequently marked by bureaucracy, fraud, waste, and funding of causes inconsistent with Scripture. While caring for the poor is commanded (Deut 15:7-11; Matt 25:35-40), forced redistribution through the state is not the biblical model of generosity.

Racism: Conservatives view all people as equal image-bearers of God, to be judged by character rather than skin color (Gen 1:27; Gal 3:28; 1 Sam 16:7). They reject racial partiality and identity politics in favor of impartial justice and individual responsibility (Rom 2:11; Acts 10:34-35). Liberals often frame race through a lens of perpetual victimization, treating minorities as needing rescue rather than capable of personal agency, and support policies such as affirmative action and racial quotas. These create partiality and reduce merit (Lev 19:15; Jas 2:1-4), contrary to the biblical call to unity in Christ without favoritism (Eph 2:14-16).

Modern Feminism: Conservatives affirm the equal dignity of men and women as image-bearers while recognizing complementary roles in marriage and the church (Gen 1:27; Gen 2:18-24; Eph 5:22-33). They value motherhood, family, and biblical sexual ethics (Prov 31; Titus 2:4-5; Heb 13:4). Modern feminism often promotes abortion, sexual liberation, the rejection of traditional family roles, and antagonism toward men, which conflicts with creation order, the call to purity (1 Thess 4:3), and sacrificial love within marriage (Eph 5:25). Equal value does not require identical roles or the denial of biological and creational differences.

Marxism/Communism: Conservatives reject forced redistribution, the abolition of private property, and state control of the economy, defending the biblical principles of private ownership, personal stewardship, and the work ethic (Exod 20:15; Exod 20:17; Matt 25:14-30; 2 Thess 3:10). Giving is to be voluntary (2 Cor 9:7; Acts 5:4). Liberals incorporate class-struggle language, envy-driven policies, and expanded government control that resemble Marxist ideas. These conflict with the prohibition against stealing and coveting, the dignity of work, and the recognition that God is the source of wealth (Deut 8:18). The state is not God.

1st Amendment (Freedom of Speech/Religion): Conservatives defend robust free speech and religious liberty, including the right to proclaim biblical truth without censorship (Acts 5:29; Acts 4:19-20). They oppose “hate speech” regulations and cancel culture that silence views on morality or sexuality. Liberals support free expression in many areas yet often favor restrictions on religious or traditional viewpoints in public institutions and private business, which can hinder the Great Commission (Matt 28:19-20) and the call to speak truth (Eph 4:25). Biblical faith requires the freedom to obey God rather than men.

2nd Amendment (Right to Bear Arms): Conservatives support the right to keep and bear arms for self-defense and as a check on tyranny, consistent with biblical examples of armed protection of family and community (Luke 22:36; Exod 22:2-3; Neh 4:17-18). Liberals favor extensive restrictions and bans that limit the ability to defend one’s household (Prov 22:3). Scripture recognizes the legitimacy of force in defense of life and the reality of a fallen world (Gen 9:6; Ps 144:1), while still calling for peace wherever possible.

Climate Change/Environmentalism: Conservatives affirm stewardship of the earth (Gen 2:15; Ps 24:1) while favoring market innovation, energy abundance, and a balanced approach that avoids treating the planet as divine or subordinating human flourishing to alarmist policies. Liberals push aggressive regulations, carbon taxes, and international accords that can harm the poor and treat environmental concerns as overriding other biblical priorities such as dominion and provision (Gen 1:28). Care for creation is good; idolizing it or ignoring human needs is not.

Gun Control: Conservatives resist broad restrictions that disarm law-abiding citizens, emphasizing personal responsibility, mental-health focus, and the right of self-defense (Exod 22:2-3; Luke 22:36). Liberals advocate universal background checks, assault-weapon bans, and red-flag laws that can infringe on rights without addressing the heart of violence (Jer 17:9). Biblical justice includes the protection of the innocent (Ps 82:4) and does not require citizens to be helpless before evil.

Universal Healthcare: Conservatives prefer private insurance, personal responsibility, and charitable care (2 Thess 3:10; Jas 1:27), avoiding massive government programs that create debt and dependency (Prov 22:7). Liberals support single-payer or heavily subsidized systems that expand state control over healthcare. While caring for the sick is biblical (Matt 25:36; Luke 10:33-35), Scripture does not mandate government-run healthcare or coercive redistribution to achieve it.

Death Penalty: Conservatives support capital punishment for murder as a matter of justice and deterrence, consistent with the principle that the one who takes a life should forfeit his own (Gen 9:6; Rom 13:4; Lev 24:17). Liberals generally oppose the death penalty, emphasizing rehabilitation or the risk of error. While mercy is biblical, the consistent testimony of Scripture is that just retribution for murder upholds the value of life (Num 35:31; Eccl 8:11).

Euthanasia/Assisted Suicide: Conservatives oppose assisted suicide and euthanasia, affirming that God determines the length of life (Ps 139:16; Heb 9:27) and that the command not to murder applies (Exod 20:13). Palliative care and the dignity of suffering are preferred (Rom 5:3-5). Liberals support legalization in various states under the banner of autonomy and compassion. Ending a life prematurely rejects the sanctity of life and the biblical call to protect the vulnerable (Prov 31:8).

Affirmative Action: Conservatives favor color-blind, merit-based standards that judge character and ability without racial partiality (Rom 2:11; 1 Sam 16:7; Deut 1:17). Liberals support race-conscious admissions, hiring, and quotas in the name of equity. Such policies show favoritism, reduce the applicant pool, and conflict with the biblical prohibition against partiality (Lev 19:15; Jas 2:1-4). Equal opportunity does not require engineered outcomes.

School Choice/Vouchers: Conservatives support parental choice through vouchers and education savings accounts so families can select schools aligned with their values, fulfilling the duty to train children (Prov 22:6; Eph 6:4; Deut 6:7). Liberals typically defend the public-school monopoly and oppose funding that follows the student. Restricting options limits parents’ ability to provide a biblically informed education (2 Tim 3:15).

Taxation (Wealth Redistribution): Conservatives favor lower, flatter taxes and voluntary generosity, recognizing private property and the biblical work ethic (2 Cor 9:7; Exod 20:15; Deut 8:18). Liberals support progressive taxation and expanded redistribution through government. While taxes for legitimate public functions are legitimate, heavy redistribution driven by envy or class rhetoric conflicts with the prohibition against coveting and stealing (Exod 20:17; Prov 10:4).

Military Interventionism: Conservatives support a strong national defense and just-war principles to protect citizens and allies (Rom 13:4; Eccl 3:8), while recognizing the cost of unnecessary conflict. Liberals often favor restraint or humanitarian interventions selectively. Scripture calls for peacemaking (Matt 5:9) yet also for authorities to restrain evil (Ps 82:3-4). Prudence, not isolationism or endless war, is the biblical balance.

Free Trade vs. Protectionism: Conservatives prioritize national interest, job protection, and fair trade that does not undermine citizens (1 Tim 5:8; Phil 2:4), while still recognizing the benefits of legitimate commerce. Liberals more readily embrace unrestricted free trade. Scripture values both diligence and provision for one’s own household (Prov 27:23; Gen 3:19) and does not require open borders for goods at the expense of domestic order.

Evolution vs. Creationism in Education: Conservatives support teaching the scientific evidence for design alongside evolutionary theory and affirm God as Creator (Gen 1:1; John 1:3; Exod 20:11). Liberals typically insist on exclusive naturalistic evolution in public schools. Suppressing the possibility of a Creator conflicts with the clear testimony of creation (Rom 1:20; Ps 111:2) and the duty to teach truth.

Prayer in Schools: Conservatives favor allowing voluntary student-led or community prayer and religious expression in schools (2 Chr 7:14; Matt 18:20; 1 Thess 5:17). Liberals generally oppose organized or public prayer, citing separation of church and state. While private prayer is always appropriate (Matt 6:5-6), excluding God from public education undermines the moral foundation Scripture calls parents and communities to provide (Prov 22:6).

Divorce and Remarriage: Conservatives uphold the permanence of marriage and restrict divorce to narrow biblical grounds such as sexual immorality (Matt 19:3-9; Mal 2:16; Gen 2:24). They emphasize counseling and reconciliation (1 Cor 7:10-11). Liberals support no-fault divorce and easy dissolution based on personal happiness. Scripture treats the marriage covenant as sacred and hates the breaking of it (Mal 2:16; Matt 19:6).

Pornography: Conservatives support restrictions on pornography and emphasize purity, recognizing that lust is adultery in the heart (Matt 5:28; Job 31:1; 1 Cor 6:18). Liberals treat adult pornography largely as protected speech with minimal regulation. Scripture commands believers to flee sexual immorality, keep the marriage bed undefiled (Heb 13:4), and guard their eyes and hearts (Ps 101:3; 1 Thess 4:7)

The Scorpion and the Frog

A scorpion approached a frog who waited at the riverbank.
“Carry me across,” the scorpion said, “for I cannot swim.”

The frog eyed him with weary caution.
“You are a creature of the sting. If I take you upon my back, you will strike me. We will both drown.”

The scorpion replied with smooth logic.
“If I sting you in the water, I perish as well. It would be against nature and reason.”

The frog, persuaded by this argument, allowed the scorpion to climb aboard. He swam out, strong legs pushing through the current.

Halfway across, the sharp agony of a sting pierced his back. His muscles faltered. As both began to sink beneath the river’s surface, the frog gasped:

“You promised! Why would you do this?”

The scorpion’s voice held neither anger nor triumph, only a resigned truth.
“Silly frog! You knew I was a scorpion when you offered to ferry me across the river.”

They vanished into the cold deep together.

Answer: B) Snallygaster

The Snallygaster is said to haunt Frederick County, Maryland, especially South Mountain, Braddock Heights and the Middletown Valley. Its roots go back to the German immigrants who settled the area beginning in the 1730s and told of a monster called a Schneller Geist, meaning "quick ghost." Legend describes it as half bird and half reptile, with a metallic beak lined with razor-sharp teeth and octopus-like tentacles, swooping silently out of the sky to carry off its victims. Seven-pointed stars, said to keep it away, can still be seen painted on local barns. In February and March 1909, newspapers reported a beast with "enormous wings, a long pointed bill, claws like steel hooks, and an eye in the center of its forehead" that screeched "like a locomotive whistle." The Smithsonian Institution reportedly offered a reward for its hide, and President Theodore Roosevelt reportedly considered postponing an African safari to hunt it himself. It later came out that the 1909 reports were a hoax by Middletown Valley Register editor George C. Rhoderick and reporter Ralph S. Wolfe to sell more papers. In 2021, the American Snallygaster Museum opened in Libertytown, Maryland.

How'd you do?

1SG 🫡 WOGBTC EVENING ORDER — October 20, 2026
TSE Training • TRUST HIS CARE—BECOME AVAILABLE TO CARE

1 — THE ORDER

Morning’s AWP: SURROUNDED BY HIS CARE — Psalm 34:7.

Tonight’s training: Entrust your concerns to the Lord so you can give faithful attention to the people He places before you.

“casting all your care upon Him, for He cares for you.”
— 1 Peter 5:7, NKJV

Training passage: 1 Peter 5:5–11.

Battle Line: I belong to Christ. I can entrust my burden to Him and make room to care for another.

2 — THE TRAINING

Warrior Doctrine — Dependence on God strengthens faithful service.

A. Bring the actual burden.

Peter connects casting your cares with humbling yourself under God’s mighty hand. Humility includes admitting your limits: you cannot oversee every circumstance, prevent every hardship, or determine another person’s response.

Name the concern plainly in prayer. You can approach your Father before you feel composed or have a solution.

B. Trust the character of the One receiving it.

The foundation of this command is personal: He cares for you.

Morning’s picture of the Lord’s angel encamping around His people directs your attention toward God’s protective care. Tonight, practice depending on that care. His faithfulness gives you reason to bring Him the concern again whenever it returns.

Continuing concern does not mean your prayer failed. Return to Him, then carry out the responsibility before you.

C. Stay watchful while you trust.

Read verses 8–9 alongside verse 7. Peter joins entrusting your cares with vigilance and steadfast faith. Prayer prepares you to pay attention, exercise discernment, and act wisely.

Verse 10 also acknowledges suffering. God’s care sustains His people through difficulty; the passage gives no timetable for every burden to disappear.

D. Give others room to speak.

A person who is hurting may need time to explain what they are carrying. Your first useful act may be patient attention.

Ask: “What would be helpful right now?”

Listen to the answer. Offer a kindness you can honestly provide. Your responsibility is to love faithfully; entrust the person and the outcome to Christ.

Training Drill — ENTRUST • ATTEND • ACT

ENTRUST: “Father, this concern is weighing on me: _____. I place it in Your care.”
ATTEND: Give the person before you time to speak without preparing your answer.
ACT: Choose one fitting response: encouragement, practical assistance, prayer with their agreement, or a dependable follow-up.

Ordinary-life example: Someone at work seems distracted. Ask how they are doing and allow an honest answer. If they share a difficulty, listen before offering advice.

Armor Fit

Belt of Truth: God’s care remains true during uncertainty.
Breastplate of Righteousness: Make honest promises and keep them.
Boots of Peace: Approach with patience.
Shield of Faith: Entrust the outcome to the Father.
Helmet of Salvation: Remember your belonging to Christ.
Sword of the Spirit: Read 1 Peter 5:7 within verses 5–11.

Supporting study — NKJV: Psalm 34:17–19; Matthew 6:25–34; Galatians 6:2, 5; 2 Corinthians 1:3–4.

Train the Trainer

Read 1 Peter 5:5–11 together. Ask:

What does this passage reveal about God?
What burden can we bring to Him?
What responsibility remains ours to carry out?

Teaching point: Trusting God with our burdens helps us become attentive and dependable in caring for others.

3 — THE EXECUTION

Commander’s Orders

Read the training passage slowly.
Name one concern and entrust it to the Father.
Identify your next faithful responsibility.
In your next suitable encounter, listen carefully and offer one practical kindness.

Tonight’s assessment:
What did I entrust? What responsibility did I fulfill? Did I listen long enough to understand what help was welcome?

Prayer of Deployment

Father, thank You that You care for me. I bring You the concerns I cannot resolve and the outcomes I cannot control. Keep me watchful, humble, and steadfast in faith.

AWP DAILY ORDER — October 20, 2026
Promise #293 • SURROUNDED BY HIS CARE

1 — THE ORDER

Today’s 365Promises summary: “My angels will surround all who fear Me.” 

“The angel of the LORD encamps all around those who fear Him,
And delivers them.”
— Psalm 34:7, NKJV 

Battle Line: I belong to Christ; I can trust His care and move toward others in love.

2 — THE TRAINING

Warrior Doctrine — Reverence for God steadies your response to fear.

Fear Him means reverence Him. Read Psalm 34:11–14: reverence takes practical shape through truthful speech, doing good, and pursuing peace. Bring your concerns honestly before God, then let His Word direct your response.

“Encamps” gives you a picture of protective presence. Your view of the situation is limited; God’s knowledge and ability extend beyond what you can see. Keep your attention on the Lord who provides that care.

Read the promise alongside the hardship. Psalm 34:17–19 acknowledges the afflictions of the righteous. Trusting God means depending on His faithfulness through trouble, without demanding that every outcome follow your preferred timetable.

Let trust make room for love. Entrust what exceeds your control to Christ. Then give the person before you your attention: listen, ask what would help, and offer the kindness within your reach.

Armor Fit

* Belt of Truth: Uncertainty does not establish abandonment.
* Breastplate of Righteousness: Speak honestly and do good.
* Boots of Peace: Approach others with patient attention.
* Shield of Faith: Entrust unseen circumstances to God.
* Helmet of Salvation: Remember whose you are.
* Sword of the Spirit: Read Psalm 34:7 in its full setting.

Supporting study — NKJV: Psalm 34:11–14; 2 Kings 6:15–17; Hebrews 1:14; John 16:33; Romans 8:35–39.

3 — THE EXECUTION

Commander’s Orders

1. Read Psalm 34:1–10, 17–19 slowly.
2. Pray: “Father, I entrust _____ to Your care.”
3. Complete one responsibility you can act on today.
4. Give one person patient attention and one practical expression of Christ’s love.

Tonight’s assessment: What did I entrust to God? What faithful action did I complete? Whom did I care for?

Prayer of Deployment

Father, thank You for Your watchful care. Through Jesus Christ, I belong to You. Teach me to reverence You, trust Your wisdom, and obey Your Word. When uncertainty presses, steady me for today’s responsibilities. Give me patient ears, truthful words, and willing hands for the people You place in my path. Lord Jesus, my Commander, lead me in Your peace and love. Amen.

TRAIN • STAND • EXECUTE 👊🛡️

Lab Report - powered by https://t.co/eqFpIa32h7

Here is the show for October 20, 2026.

https://t.co/wUOKoz7EZt

Yesterday we had some technical difficulties, so two of the companies I covered, Cambria and Four Nines, are on today's show through the magic of editing by my wonderful production team at https://t.co/eqFpIa32h7. Today I have three deep dives: Kirkland Lake Discoveries, Cambria Gold Mines and Four Nines Gold.

Kirkland Lake Discoveries reports high-grade gold at Mirado and commences an additional 25,000-metre drill program (KL South Project, 18 km south of Kirkland Lake, Ontario): Mirado West hole KLM26-039 hit 73.86 g/t gold over 1 metre, and KLM26-041 hit 36.43 g/t over 1.45 metres, along with more mineralized intersections in the Mirado North and South Zones. The boys are really rolling up their sleeves. What excites me is that there's a historical, non-compliant resource with widespread gold disseminated in permeable rock, rock like a sponge that soaks up the gold-bearing fluids, plus the vertical veins that are the source of that gold. These are orogenic gold veins: steeply dipping, narrow and high grade, the kind that made Red Lake and Goldcorp, and Fosterville in Australia, now owned by Agnico Eagle after a big takeover of Kirkland Lake Gold. Two ounces a tonne is about $8,000-a-tonne rock, and an ounce and a bit is over $4,000. Think of the disseminated gold as a layer of the cake with these high-grade veins coming up through it, and the drilling is proving that model out. Mirado West is a brand new discovery west of the North and South Zones, and it looks like the system extends at least 500 metres or more to the west. Mirado North returned 2.01 g/t over 19 metres, and Mirado South 7.36 g/t over 3.5 metres and 1.27 g/t over 11 metres. With open pits being mined at half a gram these days, that's all high grade for an open pit target. They raised $20 million and are fully funded for a minimum of 25,000 metres, about 15,000 at Mirado and 10,000 on regional targets. CEO Stefan Sklepowicz says the priority is to determine the gold-bearing structures, how far they extend, where they may connect and what controls the higher-grade concentrations. I'm a shareholder, and I'm excited about the potential for a one to three million ounce open pit scenario, but those high-grade orogenic feeder veins can be big company makers, and I'm a junkie for high grade. Executive Chairman Denis Laviolette says big deposits have big footprints, and they're growing Mirado significantly to the west, north and south. The preliminary interpreted footprint is about 1,300 by 930 metres horizontally and 550 metres vertically, versus a historical footprint of about 740 by 380 metres and 380 metres vertically. They give you the proper disclaimer: that's an exploration model, not a resource. I think the growth is in every direction, including down, where you'll find the feeder veins. Northwest of Mirado, a 1.2-kilometre trend of elevated gold grains in glacial till includes a sample with 235 grains. I'd love to see those grains. Rounded grains have travelled with the ice, like gold in a river, while angular, pristine grains are close to source, and with that many, my guess is they're close to source. They're also using hyperspectral analysis, which is almost like an x-ray of the drill core that maps the alteration. When gold-bearing fluids hit the country rock they chemically alter it, and that fingerprint helps vector the next holes. Really cool technology, and the boys are doing the science in a very impressive way. They only have a C$82 million valuation with a very large land package in the Kirkland Lake mining district, very big mining country. They trade about 237,000 shares a day, a pretty solid audience, with 148,000 so far today and flat on the day. Someone wants to buy a couple hundred thousand shares and there isn't a lot on the sell side, so I think it could close green. I've covered their https://t.co/eqFpIa32h7 Pro Sentiment on past Lab Reports, so check those out. On the Lassonde Curve: they're only about 25 to 30% into my sweet spot on the left side of the curve and haven't gone up the left side in a substantial way yet. If they do, and that's a big if, what I see in the drilling tells me they could have a wonderful long-term run up the left side, given the quality of the project and their large land package in the Kirkland Lake district.

Cambria Gold Mines intersects 98.56 g/t gold over 8.2 metres at the Silver Coin Deposit (Premier Gold Project, near Stewart, British Columbia): this fairly new company took over a failed mine and believes it can make a successful mine out of it. CEO Rob McLeod has deep roots as a geologist in Stewart and the Golden Triangle, his family has had a lot of success in the region over many decades, and he started his career underground at this project. The basic thesis is that it failed because there wasn't a strong enough understanding of the gold system, where the gold was and how to get at it, so they're doing a lot more drilling. This release reports four holes, 657 metres, including 98.56 g/t over 8.2 metres with 794 g/t over 1 metre in SC26-2714, 22.62 g/t over 4.4 metres and 3.75 g/t over 20 metres including 19.95 g/t over 1 metre in SC26-2710, and 4.55 g/t over 10.6 metres in SC26-2719. Lots of juicy numbers, but grade alone is not king. Grade plus continuity is king, and this is a perfect example: the old operator had high grade but didn't understand the continuity, and that's a recipe for failure. Rob's first sentence says a lot about his thesis: high gold grades over potentially underground bulk mineable widths make Silver Coin a priority for underground development in the spring of 2027. Underground development right around the corner is unique these days. His team has outlined a multi-phased epithermal gold system with multiple wide domains, several open for expansion, and Silver Coin brings both tonnes and grade to the hub-and-spoke complex they're building to support the Premier Mill. The northern part of Silver Coin was mined in the 1990s by Westmin and Tenajon by underground longhole stoping, and Cambria's model draws on the operating data and history from Rob's cousin, Bruce McLeod, who led that work. The southern extension is the focus of the infill drilling. Had the former operator done more infill, they'd have understood the gold distribution better and probably wouldn't have had a failed mine, especially at today's gold prices. Silver Coin plus high grade from the Premier deposit is expected to be the initial feed for their 2,500-tonne-a-day Premier Mill while Red Mountain is built. The sections show high grade within a wide distribution, and block caving costs about as much as open pit mining these days, so a bulk mining scenario could be very attractive. They're down a penny today, which surprises me given the results, but gold is down. They came out of the gate strong and have trended down since, and with 426 million shares out, maybe some old shareholders aren't that confident, but the last four months don't always tell you about the next four. They have a C$298 million valuation, very inexpensive for a restart, and the reason is that they're trying to restart a failed mine. They have a very good audience, about 610,000 shares a day, with 1.38 million today, double average, and stronger buy orders than sell orders. https://t.co/eqFpIa32h7 Pro Sentiment is mixed but opportunity focused: high-grade drill results, development updates and substantial warrant exercises have strengthened optimism, and some of the selling pressure is holders selling stock to exercise cheaper warrants, which brings money into the company. Confidence remains conditional on execution, which is reasonable: they've got to prove a failed mine can be a success. Investors question the change in the Mount Margaret strategy. That's a large porphyry in Washington State they planned to spin out and have now decided to keep and drill to enhance its value first, which makes sense to me. I'd be 100% focused on the gold project, and if they prove it out, financing the copper won't be a problem. Just my two cents. They can drill from underground, so they aren't hampered by drill-season weather like a lot of Golden Triangle projects. High-profile backers are fine, but don't base your thesis on them; they don't get it right all the time, trust me, I know several of them. The warrant overhang, dilution, the financing and restructuring, and the gold and silver stream and other liabilities are valid negatives to watch. On the Lassonde Curve: they're developing an old mine with infrastructure already there, which is different from most companies that have to build all of that, so I put them only about 10% into my sweet spot on the right side of the curve. There's plenty of blue sky if they keep proving up their thesis, and the drilling won't move the needle so much as confirm this can be a success. You can't fight the Lassonde Curve.

Four Nines Gold intersects 80.1 metres averaging 1.08 g/t gold in the expanding Lower Telegraph Corridor (Hayden Hill Gold Project, Lassen County, California): hole HH26-003 returned 80.1 metres of 1.08 g/t gold and 10 g/t silver, starting just below the pit, from the same collar as HH26-005, which hit about 58 metres of multi-stage silicified hydrothermal breccia with assays pending. I've written a lot of news releases and read 10 or 20 times more, and this one is full of geospeak. Remember, you're not trying to impress other geologists; you're telling the story to retail investors, who can also plug the release into AI and ask it to explain it like they're a high school student. So let me translate. Hayden Hill produced about 480,000 ounces of gold, with Amax mining the Lookout pit, and the question is where all that gold came from. It's a vein system below a pit. Keep it simple. HH26-001, 150 metres north, also hit broad near-surface gold, and HH26-003's deeper 8 metres of 1.10 g/t may be the down-dip extension of the 214 Vein. That's not underground mineable, but it's important. This is the first systematic exploration drilling at Hayden Hill since 1997, and the Lower Telegraph Corridor is the first of eight exploration zones, leaving seven to test. President and CEO Charles Ross says the inaugural campaign is exceeding expectations, and their objective is to show Hayden Hill hosts a much larger gold system than historical mining ever revealed. I like that. I'm a big fan of VP Exploration David Flint, a super talented geologist, who says the significance lies in the consistency of the mineralizing structures in holes about 150 metres apart, interpreted as the upper expression of a low-sulfidation epithermal gold vein system, and I agree 100%. Epithermal veins come in clusters of steeply dipping veins, and that's likely what fed the pit. There are two critical parts: the breccia unit, broken-up country rock with quartz and gold squeezed in along the path of least resistance, and below it the boiling zone, the bonanza zone, the jewelry box, which is what makes high-grade underground mines. When you cut breccia core, you send in the country rock with the quartz, which dilutes the gold, so even a tenth of a gram or a gram in the breccia is good news. It tells you to keep going deeper. That's why I care about depth, like hole HH26-011, more than strike extension. In the core photos I see multi-phase quartz, like a pot that boils, stops and boils again millions of years later, flow textures and very intense alteration, and some of it looks like it's getting close to the boiling zone. I live in Mexico, where epithermal veins have made it the most important high-grade silver district in the world for hundreds of years, and when I see gold-rich epithermal veins I get excited. Look at Sleeper and Midas in Nevada, and Hishikari in Japan, at one time the highest-grade gold mine in the world. The game changer is getting into that boiling zone, because finding it in one vein helps you find it in the others in the cluster. They only have a C$20 million valuation, very cheap for a potential gold-rich epithermal vein system. They trade only 96,000 shares a day, with 61,000 by about 11:30 Central, so they need to work on their digital marketing, news releases and corporate presentation. Bids are reasonably good and offers reasonably soft, so I think it goes sideways off this news. It came off a base around 60 cents on very high volume, which doesn't suggest strong hands, although I'm encouraged that it's bottoming on lower volume, which can signal a change in direction. https://t.co/eqFpIa32h7 Pro Sentiment is broadly optimistic but tempered by execution and trading risks, with confidence in the team and the past-producing project. In David Flint, you couldn't find a more exceptional mine finder. He's the goods. Skeptics point to share price weakness and selling as shares come free trading. The financing was pitched as being in strong hands, but the market tells you they weren't that strong. On dilution, I'm only about 70% in agreement: they can raise money, and better marketing could lower their cost of capital. As for whether the early drilling tested deeper targets, no, it hasn't, and I see that as a positive still to come, not a negative. On the Lassonde Curve: with a tiny C$20 million valuation, I put them at the very left extreme of the curve, viewed as a complete concept rather than a company proving its thesis. They've got a long way to go up the left side of the curve, and I don't think they've even started the ascent yet.

Over the past several days the Trump administration has made six moves that squeeze Ukraine or ease pressure on Russia, per reporting from the Washington Post, Reuters, Axios, Bloomberg and the FT.

🚀 Patriots: The Post reports Patriot interceptor transfers to Ukraine are still unapproved, including missiles European allies offered that need Pentagon sign-off. Hegseth hasn't finished the paperwork. Rubio denies any deliberate decision to hold them back. Ukraine's stocks are nearly gone.

🛰 Satellites: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield restrictions disrupted drone operations, including interceptors used against jet-powered Shaheds. Reuters reports the restrictions came from the White House. Trump denies ordering them, and Musk says the US government controls military Starshield.

⚠️ Warnings: Zelensky told US senators Ukraine missed American early warnings of Russian ballistic launches three times last week. Washington denies withholding anything.

🏭 Refineries: Washington has pressed Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries. Zelensky offered a 30-day pause in exchange for Patriots and backed a reciprocal halt on energy strikes. Russia has matched none of it and keeps hitting Ukrainian cities and power plants.

🚧 Sanctions: Trump eased restrictions on Russian diesel exports and waived further Russia energy penalties, citing fuel prices. His administration is also working on a way to let some sanctioned shadow-fleet tankers be sold and returned to legitimate shipping.

🗣 Rhetoric: On October 19 Trump told reporters, "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much." The same day a Russian drone hit a park in the Kharkiv region and killed six people, three of them children, according to Ukrainian authorities cited by Reuters.

Since Trump signed his October 16 order waiving sanctions under the Graham Act, daily reports from Ukrainian regional authorities have recorded at least 37 civilian deaths from Russian attacks in reporting periods spanning October 16–20. The toll includes victims killed before the order was signed. (Image on reply)

Each step has its own stated reason: weapons shortages, technical limits, fuel prices, negotiations. Taken together, Ukraine is being asked to cut its energy strikes while its interceptors wait on approvals, its drones run on constrained satellite service and its warnings arrive unreliably. Russia has shown no comparable restraint.

Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. Washington continues to demand restraint from Kyiv.

On August 13, Paul Zeitz convened the first meeting of a working group focused on structural transformation and deliberative democracy. Participants from organizations including Issue One, Democracy2076, Mediators Foundation, Hope for Democracy, People’s Bill of Rights 250, and Renew to Thrive used the session to introduce their work, map the broader ecosystem, share updates on major initiatives, and begin aligning efforts around potential legitimacy crises and windows for reform.

Zeitz, a physician and longtime political advocate who co-coordinates the Renew American Democracy platform with Danielle Reiff, framed the discussion around the RAD build pillar. This pillar emphasizes the need for structural change advanced through citizen deliberation. The informal conversation served as both an introductory gathering and preparatory work for a RAD Forum scheduled for September 17 on Constitution Day under the Renew to Thrive convenings.

Participants and Their Work

The group began with brief self-introductions. Zeitz described his background in the global AIDS movement alongside Leigh Blake and his current focus on democracy organizing. Blake, who co-leads People’s Bill of Rights 250 with Alicia Keys, noted the project’s public-facing approach and her preference for avoiding elite speak.

Vinay, Partnerships Director at Mediators Foundation, emphasized efforts to connect local civic hubs and scale national collaboration so that disparate deliberative projects reinforce one another rather than compete. Brendan Halloran, based in Washington, D.C., drew on years of international governance work, including at USAID, and recent involvement with Missouri American Democracy, Driving Together, Renew to Thrive, and Issue One.

Brian Bird of Hope for Democracy described a coalition advancing annual civic assemblies in states through initiative. The goal is to create bodies with real political power beyond ordinary legislative control. Steven Montoya of Democracy2076 outlined research on congressional reform that maps divergence and convergence between structural reformers and institutional modernizers. He also discussed lessons from constitutional change processes in nine other democracies. Stefanie Lindquist shared her model constitutional convention, which has been hosted at ASU and WashU with students from more than 80 universities. She plans to expand the model through a dedicated website.

Rosarie Tucci, Vice President for Citizen Engagement at Issue One, highlighted her work on inclusive peace processes and her belief that citizens must be centrally involved in reforms. She pointed to deliberative democracy as the practical path. John Mongan, a former State Department official and author of the More Stable Union Substack, described planning for a legitimacy crisis and the idea of a Third Continental Congress convened by governors. Walter Roberts, associated with Renew to Thrive and connected convenings, spoke of whole-systems generative change, movement alignment, and frameworks oriented toward all people and places thriving.

Mapping the Ecosystem

Tucci summarized the current landscape of structural reform coherence. She identified Danielle Allen’s Council on Common Purpose as a key venue that promotes collaboration across states, from state to federal levels, and across sectors such as electoral, judicial, congressional, and executive. She contrasted this with DFAD, a large coalition of organizations and think tanks that includes the Brennan Center and Common Cause. DFAD’s approach is closely tied to H.R. 1 and Democratic control, an orientation several participants viewed as problematic for long-term, sustainable democratic systems.

Discussion also covered the upcoming April summit that appears to succeed the American Democracy Summit. That earlier summit itself followed the Unrig the System conferences. Tucci noted Issue One’s criteria for engagement. The event should go beyond panels to advance coherent integration of reform pathways so the public is not confused by competing visions or timelines. Walter Roberts described Nanner as an association that grew out of Unrig the System. It holds an annual December gathering of structural reformers that has historically mediated tensions among ranked-choice, proportional, and other proposals. The gathering also offers open time for side convenings.

Zeitz noted multiple amendment-focused efforts. These include Democracy2076’s mapping of constitutional amendment movements, one of which involves a right-to-health proposal supported by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, and the separate People’s Bill of Rights process. The group’s goal is to weave these strands with deliberative work so parallel efforts become mutually reinforcing rather than fragmented.

Major Initiatives and Updates

Blake reported that People’s Bill of Rights 250 has support from roughly 800 organizations. Alicia Keys has conducted regular briefings, including a large women’s session with about 200 groups. The project’s mapping platform, developed with https://t.co/pvgaxgu4kR and now associated with Bridge, has attracted about 55,000 votes and roughly 1,200 ideas from the public. Common priorities include healthcare, free and fair government, equal rights for women, broader equality, treatment of immigrants, and eliminating money in politics. The effort deliberately avoids politicians, corporations, and special interests in its public posture and is fiscally sponsored by Equal Citizens Foundation under Lawrence Lessig. A campaign drawing on Stephen Kull’s survey findings, which highlight cross-partisan agreement on dozens of issues, is forthcoming, along with work involving Global Citizen and the ERA Coalition. Blake stressed the need for language simple enough for ordinary people and a sense of belonging and possibility amid widespread political disillusionment.

Danielle Reiff described the Nationwide Deliberation Campaign as a multi-stage process. It moves from grassroots deliberations and deliberative polling to state and national citizens’ assemblies. The aim is a refined set of structural reform proposals ready by the end of 2027 or early 2028 to influence the subsequent election cycle. She framed the work as preparation for meeting the moment, whether through ordinary political channels or an acute legitimacy crisis in which the federal government is widely viewed as illegitimate. In the latter case, high-level transitional mechanisms such as a national dialogue or a Third Continental Congress could channel legitimate public input. Reiff and others linked this to an options memo prepared for governors that outlines their potential role if the federal government loses legitimacy. The memo has reached Governors Safeguarding Democracy and has been shared with offices in several states.

John Mongan elaborated on the Third Continental Congress concept. He has shared related materials with the governors of Massachusetts, California, and Illinois. Massachusetts declined to engage. California and Illinois expressed interest if another state took the lead. He has also engaged D.C. think tanks, many of which are wary of institutional risk and legal exposure. Mongan stressed that the idea is not secession. It is a response to the absence of a legitimate federal authority. He drew a historical parallel to the First Continental Congress’s assertion of independent governance within the British system until disputes were resolved. He identified specific red-line scenarios, including failure to seat duly elected members in early 2027 or an occupant of the White House lacking constitutional authority in 2029. He argued that governors would need advance planning for essential functions, coordination, and foreign outreach.

Scenario Planning and Crisis Readiness

Brendan Halloran and others proposed shared scenario planning for the medium term, roughly 2027 through 2029. The idea is to map potential crises, windows of opportunity, and trajectories so the structural-reform community can align rather than compete. Tucci noted that Issue One is preparing three cross-partisan legislative packages as a possible core set of measures that could be advanced in narrower windows. Larger constitutional pathways would be reserved for wider openings. The group discussed how such planning could reduce fragmentation. It could also help organizations move beyond implicit assumptions, in which blockers prepare only for breakdown and builders prepare only for continuity. Planning would support coordinated action across outcomes that contain shades of gray.

Participants also referenced the United Democracy Alliance and related red-line work led in part by National Security Leaders of America. This is a cross-partisan group of retired military, intelligence, and diplomatic figures. These efforts focus on real-time monitoring and response around elections, particularly the midterms and 2028. The RAD-oriented group positioned itself as contributing the complementary constitutional legitimacy and day-after structural dimension. Tucci and others observed that many blocking-oriented networks prioritize immediate defense and minimum viable agreements. Relational work and later pivots toward reform form part of a longer theory of change.

Looking Ahead

The September 17 RAD Forum was presented as a co-created opportunity to advance these conversations. It could potentially support planning for the April summit and leverage connected-convening approaches. Walter Roberts floated hosting a huddle of 15 to 17 conveners focused on the trajectory of gatherings leading into the April event. Other near-term touchpoints mentioned included the PolicyLink Summit and Crooked Con on November 7 in D.C.

Closing reflections were measured but constructive. Halloran noted the value of holding both generational and more time-bound change in view. Tucci described the work as simply doing what participants can, as hard as they can, to meet the moment. Roberts observed that the quality of the emerging collaboration felt different in frequency and capacity for rapid, appropriate response. Zeitz expressed excitement about the productivity of the first dialogue and the intention to continue weaving efforts.

The meeting closed with commitments to follow up on specific items. These include sharing the Nationwide Deliberation Campaign and Vehicles for Democratic Renewal papers, circulating notes, and refining the September 17 agenda. Participants maintained the cross-partisan, citizen-centered orientation that they repeatedly identified as essential.

text:
Truth with a little twist. 

Historic 19th-century Mormon writings contain the main elements behind the claim that good Mormon men receive a planet full of virgins, even though the exact modern phrasing does not appear as a direct quotation. The relevant teachings center on exaltation to godhood, the creation of worlds, eternal procreation to populate those worlds, and plural marriage that includes specific references to “virgins.”

Doctrine and Covenants 132 is a revelation recorded on 12 July 1843 through Joseph Smith. It teaches that men who enter and keep the new and everlasting covenant of marriage, which includes plural marriage, “shall pass by the angels, and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods, because they have no end” (verses 19–20). The same revelation addresses plural marriage directly: “if any man espouse a virgin, and desire to espouse another, and the first give her consent… And if he have ten virgins given unto him by this law, he cannot commit adultery, for they belong to him… for they are given unto him to multiply and replenish the earth, according to my commandment… and for their exaltation in the eternal worlds, that they may bear the souls of men” (verses 61–63). The stated purpose is eternal increase and the continuation of the Father’s work through spirit offspring.

Brigham Young, speaking in the Journal of Discourses 11:269 on 19 August 1866, stated: “The only men who become Gods, even the Sons of God, are those who enter into polygamy. Others attain unto a glory and may even be permitted to come into the presence of the Father and the Son; but they cannot reign as kings in glory, because they had blessings offered unto them, and they refused to accept them.” Related statements from Young and other leaders in the same period connected the highest form of exaltation—reigning as kings over one’s own posterity and kingdom—with acceptance of plural marriage when it was taught as a commandment.

Orson Pratt taught extensively in the Journal of Discourses and in his periodical The Seer (1850s–1870s) that exalted beings would create worlds and people them with their own spirit children. He wrote that “the peopling of worlds, or an endless increase, even of one family, would require an endless increase of worlds” (Journal of Discourses 1:59, 1852). He also stated: “As our Father and God begat us, sons and daughters, so will we rise immortal, males and females, and beget children, and, in our turn, form and create worlds, and send forth our spirit children to inherit those worlds” (Journal of Discourses 14:242, approximately 1871). In The Seer (1853) he published the full text of Doctrine and Covenants 132 and explained that plural marriage made it possible to people far more worlds than monogamy, including calculations of multigenerational increase. Similar language appears in writings and sermons by Parley P. Pratt (Key to the Science of Theology, 1855) and Heber C. Kimball (Journal of Discourses 1:356, 1852) concerning becoming fathers of earths and filling worlds with offspring.

text:
$KR AND THE MERGER THAT WOULD NOT DIE // A Yahoo Finance analysis argues Kroger doomed the Albertsons deal by offering up its weak stores, and an $8B trial over that claim opened this week

The argument, as the analysis lays it out, is that Kroger protected its strongest stores during the Albertsons merger fight and offered regulators the weaker end of the fleet. That is now the heart of a Delaware trial. Albertsons $ACI says Kroger's divestiture plan sank the $24.6B deal, and it wants more than $8B for the damage.

* ⚖️ The trial: the bench trial in Delaware Chancery Court began October 19 and is expected to run about two weeks, with former CEOs of both companies set to testify
* 🛒 The claim: Albertsons says Kroger kept its most profitable stores ineligible and grew the divestiture package in steps from 238 stores to 579, still short of the 650 store cap in the merger agreement
* 💰 The ask: more than $8B in damages per Albertsons, up to $9.3B counting a $600M termination fee Kroger never paid and up to $6.88B in lost merger premium
* 📉 The weak store numbers: Kroger second quarter identical sales grew just 0.2% without fuel against 3.4% a year earlier, and Kroger cut its full year identical sales outlook in September while holding its profit targets
* 🗣️ The defense: Kroger calls the claims fatally flawed and says nothing more it could have done would have changed the regulatory outcome
* 📊 Tape: $KR down 0.41% to $62.79 in the regular session, against the $63.05 close on Oct 19

▬▬▬

⚠️ THE CATCH
The $8B is a litigation ask in an unsealed court filing, not a liability Kroger has booked, and Delaware rulings in cases like this typically land months after the trial ends. The merger itself has been dead since courts blocked it in December 2024. What is actually live for Kroger is a legal bill on top of a core grocery business whose own sales growth slowed well before this trial started.

▬▬▬

🧠 THE TAKEAWAY
Kroger walked away from the deal and kept the stores. Now it has to defend, under oath, how it chose which stores to offer up. Does the trial exposure actually matter for $KR here, or is the slowed identical sales line the only number that counts? 👇 NFA

text: On this day in 1803, the US Senate ratified the Louisiana Purchase, 24 to 7. President Jefferson had sent envoys to Paris to buy just New Orleans, with authority to spend up to $10 million, so American trade could keep moving down the Mississippi. Napoleon, short of cash for war in Europe, offered the whole territory instead: about 828,000 square miles for $15 million, roughly three cents an acre. The deal doubled the size of the United States overnight, even though Jefferson worried the Constitution gave him no clear power to do it. Was this the greatest land deal in history, or just Napoleon selling what he could not hold?

text:
THEY VOTED HER ONTO HOMECOMING COURT JUST TO HUMILIATE HER. BUT THEY NEVER EXPECTED AN ENTIRE TOWN TO STAND UP FOR HER.

In 2012, 16-year-old Whitney Kropp thought something wonderful had happened.

The Michigan teenager had been selected for the homecoming court at West Branch High School.

For a brief moment, she felt special. Included. Accepted.

Then she learned the heartbreaking truth.

Her classmates had allegedly voted for her as a cruel prank, hoping to embarrass her in front of the entire school.

Students laughed at her in the hallways. Rumors spread. The boy originally assigned to escort her reportedly withdrew.

What should have been one of the happiest memories of her teenage years became a nightmare.

Whitney was devastated.

She considered skipping homecoming altogether rather than face another round of humiliation.

BUT THEN SOMETHING EXTRAORDINARY HAPPENED.

Word of what had happened reached the surrounding community.

And instead of allowing a group of cruel teenagers to have the final word, people decided to give Whitney a homecoming she would never forget.

Local businesses stepped forward.

A beautiful dress was donated.
Shoes, jewelry and professional hairstyling were arranged.
A restaurant offered dinner.
Support poured in from complete strangers.

A Facebook page created to support Whitney attracted tens of thousands of people.

People who had never met this young girl wanted her to know she mattered.

And slowly, Whitney found the courage to attend.

THEN CAME HOMECOMING NIGHT.

Wearing a beautiful red gown, Whitney walked onto the football field with her head held high.

The girl who had been mocked and humiliated was greeted with cheers, applause and an outpouring of support.

Even fans from the opposing team joined in.

For one unforgettable evening, kindness drowned out cruelty.

And Whitney didn’t use her newfound attention to seek revenge.

Instead, she encouraged other young people experiencing bullying to stay strong and never allow someone else’s cruelty to determine their worth.

I CAN’T IMAGINE HOW MUCH COURAGE IT TOOK FOR THAT 16-YEAR-OLD GIRL TO WALK ONTO THAT FIELD.

There is something especially heartbreaking about teenagers deliberately choosing to humiliate someone who simply wanted to belong.

But there is also something beautiful about a community that refused to let cruelty win.

Fourteen years later, Whitney’s story remains a powerful reminder that a single act of kindness can change someone’s life.

The students who tried to humiliate Whitney gave her a reason to hide. An entire community gave her a reason to stand tall.

And THAT is the part of this story worth remembering.

BREAKING NEWS — TRUMP DOESN'T NEED TO BUY CHAGOS OR INVADE IT. HE JUST NEEDS TO DO WHAT HE'S ALREADY DOING IN GREENLAND.

By Stan Robinson Voice of Wales 

All he has to do actually is keep flying troops in, then surround it by the fleet. Look at what the 'deal' is with Greenland.

And there it is. The quiet part out loud. The real playbook.

Forget the offer. Forget the invasion. Forget the press conference where he calls it "a terrible deal" and Burnham says "Yep."

Trump has already shown us the model 1,500 miles north. Greenland.

Washington says: we're not buying it, we're not invading it. We're just... exercising. A few more P-8s into Thule. A few more troops on rotation. A few more destroyers doing "freedom of navigation" around the Denmark Strait. Then a few more. Then the fleet is there. Then the base is there. Then the question of who owns it on paper becomes academic because the only aircraft landing on the runway have American roundels.

That is the Greenland deal. No treaty. No purchase. No invasion. Just presence. Permanent, undeniable, overwhelming presence until Copenhagen realises that sovereignty is what you can defend, not what the ICJ writes in an advisory opinion 13-1 with a Russian judge and a Chinese judge concurring.

Now apply it to Diego Garcia.

BREAKING NEWS — CHAGOS VERSION:

Trump does not need to buy Diego Garcia for $1. He does not need to invade it. He just needs to keep flying troops in. Which, incidentally, he already does.

The base already hosts B-52 nuclear-capable bombers. It already hosts the B-2s that had to fly back to Missouri when Starmer refused overflight for the Iran strikes — the very refusal that turned Trump from vaguely concerned to implacably opposed. It already is, in every operational sense, an American base that Britain happens to administer.

So Step 1 is done. Troops are in.

Step 2: Surround it by the fleet. The Indian Ocean is not the English Channel. The US 7th Fleet does not need permission to loiter in international waters around a British Indian Ocean Territory that Britain is actively trying to cede to Mauritius because 116 countries, including Russia, China, North Korea and Syria, voted that it should.

Step 3: Wait for the inevitable. Burnham tells Mauritius he will do "everything possible" to ratify. Burnham tells Trump "Yep" he will review it. Streeting tells Parliament "We're not going to go ahead without the Americans." The legal uncertainty that Streeting says makes it "extremely unwise and a risk not worth taking" remains. The base remains. The Americans remain. The Mauritians remain 1,300 miles away.

And at some point, someone in the Pentagon asks: why are we paying Mauritius £101 million a year for 99 years — £34.7 billion nominal — to lease back a base we already occupy, to solve a legal problem created by an ICJ advisory opinion that America voted against?

Answer: we aren't. We just stay.

That is the Greenland model. You don't buy it. You don't invade it. You just never leave. You exercise until exercise becomes presence, presence becomes posture, posture becomes ownership. Sovereignty by airlift.

Labour calls it a surrender deal. Trump calls it a terrible deal. The fleet calls it Tuesday.

And Burnham? Burnham will still be saying "Yep."

Trump signals possible exit from Iran, warns Europe over US support
Washington: US President Donald Trump has said the United States could leave its military campaign against Iran immediately, while warning European allies that Washington could withdraw its support if they do not change course.
Speaking at a midterm election rally in Kansas, Trump claimed that Iran would not acquire a nuclear weapon and that the US had achieved its main objective. “We could leave right now,” he said, although he did not announce a timetable or plan for ending military operations.
Trump claimed that Iran’s navy, air force, radar systems and air defences had been destroyed, adding that 229 Iranian fighter jets were scattered across runways. He also alleged that Iranian authorities had killed at least 75,000 protesters over the past eight months, but offered no evidence to support the claim.
On Truth Social, Trump wrote that the US stands with Europe, but warned: “If they don’t soon find their way, we will have no choice but to leave.” He accused European countries of failing to assist Washington during the conflict with Iran, despite the heavy US spending on NATO.
Analysts noted that the warning did not, by itself, constitute a formal announcement of a US withdrawal from Europe or NATO.

text:
If I had 6 months to scale a B2B tech startup from $0 → $10K/mo using X alone...

This is the exact playbook I'd use:

1. Identify the biggest problems your product solves, then focus on the ones businesses are willing to pay to fix.

2. Turn those problems into content using this framework:

Problem → Story → Before vs. After → Solution → CTA

3. Post 4 times a week. Share customer pain points, case studies, and industry trends. Track what works and double down.

4. Track every high-intent prospect engaging with your content in a Google Sheet. Follow them and build relationships before pitching.

5. DM warm prospects with a valuable guide that helps them solve a specific problem your product addresses.

6. Move interested prospects into sales calls. Diagnose their problems, show them the solution, and present your offer.

Rinse and repeat.

Content attracts attention. Relationships build trust. Sales turn both into revenue.
