text:
Diplomacy in the Face of the Cross
Jesus never sought to negotiate quotas for survival.His word was "Yes" or "No," cutting short all human calculations.
To Pontius Pilate, who speaks to Him of his own power, Jesus replies: "My Kingdom is not of this world."(Jn18:36-37) #Rosary
Christ drew an absolute line of demarcation during his trial, embodying the irreconcilable conflict between human power and divine kingship.

- To Pontius Pilate, who spoke of his power of life and death—the universal language of diplomacy and state coercion—
- Jesus replied: “My kingdom is not of this world… For this purpose I was born and for this purpose I came into the world to testify to the truth” (John 18:36-37).

- Faced with this assertion, the Roman prosecutor countered with the cynicism typical of state apparatuses: “What is truth?” (John 18:38). 

For secular power, truth is negotiable, malleable, secondary; only the interests of the state matter.

Pilate would later attempt to use diplomatic levers by proposing a compromise—having Jesus flogged to save his life;

- but sacred history demonstrates that political negotiation always ends up sacrificing the righteous on the altar of social peace.

Jesus never sought to negotiate survival quotas with Pilate, nor to find common ground in theology with Herod. 
-  His word was “Yes” or “No,” abruptly breaking human calculations and strategic concessions (Matthew 5:37).

👉: This dramatic tension between the kingship of Truth and the demands of power is playing out again before our eyes today in China.

As the Catholic population grows there to the point of potentially forming one of the largest communities in the world by 2030, a crucial question arises: 

👉:  will this new generation of believers be “honey” or “salt”?

The reality on the ground shows that the Chinese Catholic community is not monolithic.

- It is structurally divided in two, simultaneously embodying the risk of:
- a "honeyed" Catholicism, softened by the state, 
- and the heroism of a "salt" Catholicism, purified by persecution.

1. The "Honeyed" Side: The Official Church and the Trap of "Sinicization"

For the so-called "patriotic" Church, officially recognized by the Beijing government, the temptation of consensus is presented as a necessity for institutional survival.

• The Honey of Ideological Consensus:
Under Xi Jinping's leadership, Beijing is imposing a strict program of "Sinicization" of religions.

- This project requires that Catholic theology, homiletics, and rites incorporate the "core values ​​of socialism" and submit entirely to the authority of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

• The Compromise for Social Peace:

To keep their churches open and maintain a legal existence, many clergy members agree to dilute the critical, subversive, and prophetic scope of the Gospel.

- By tasting this "honey" of a superficial peace with an atheist regime, this segment of the Church risks losing its evangelical essence and becoming a mere tool of social stability and propaganda at the service of the State.

2. The “Salt” Side: The Underground Church and the Price of Truth

In contrast stands the “clandestine” or underground Church, which categorically refuses to subordinate the Lordship of Christ to the decrees of the Bureau of Religious Affairs, maintaining absolute fidelity to the pope successor of Peter.

• The Salt of Radical Witness:

- Underground Catholics bear the brunt of increased repression.

- Their bishops and priests are regularly arrested, detained, isolated, or harassed because they refuse to sign their adherence to a state-controlled and regulated version of their faith. 
- They reject the “honey” of legal comfort to remain the sharp “salt” that irritates the conscience of totalitarian regimes.

• A Faith Purified by Trial:

- Despite mass technological surveillance, this community continues to grow in the shadows of homes. 

- This Catholicism does not survive thanks to smooth diplomatic protocols, but through the radical nature of self-sacrifice, the memory of martyrs, and the clandestine transmission of the sacraments.

3. The Dilemma of Chinese Youth: In Search of Absolute Meaning

This strong growth of Chinese Catholicism is largely driven by rapid urbanization and an ardent search for spiritual guidance among younger generations.

- Educated in an ultra-materialistic and competitive system, these young people turn to Christ precisely because they are saturated with the sickening "honey" of official propaganda and the existential void it generates.

👉 : They seek the raw, unadorned truth of the Gospel.

In the intimacy of their house communities, 

👉:  they make the faith their own, familiarly calling Jesus "Big Brother Su" (苏大哥 - Sū dàgē).

- By adopting the central syllable of his Chinese name (Yēsū), they make him a close relative, a member of their own lineage.

- In Chinese culture, the older brother is the one who walks in front, who guides the siblings, who protects and takes the blows in place of the younger ones.

- For these persecuted young people, Jesus is not a Western abstraction or a concept validated by a state committee:

👉 : He is their cellmate, their faithful protector, the Elder Brother who has already endured trial and suffering.

Conclusion

The future of Chinese Catholicism will depend on the outcome of this dramatic tension.

- If the state apparatus succeeds in completely absorbing the ecclesiastical structure through the mechanisms of the Vatican-Beijing agreement, 

- China will produce a generation of honey: polite, conformist, administratively correct, and spiritually extinguished.

But if the historical resilience of the faithful prevails, 

- China will offer the world a generation of salt: purified by persecution and incapable of compromising with falsehood.

- History shows that when the Church attempts to use the weapons of this world—secret treaties, mutual concessions, or prudent silences on human rights to preserve its structures—it inevitably strays from its spiritual arsenal.

- It forgets that the Church's power lies not in negotiating its survival with empires, but in fidelity to its prophetic mission.

-  Christianity never survives through the administrative tolerance of a totalitarian state, but through the contagious faith of its martyrs.

Ultimately, the profound reality in China remains one of invisible fidelity. 

- It is the story of millions of Chinese peasants and city dwellers who, far from diplomatic circles, continue to pray at home, secretly pass on the catechism to their children, and prefer prison to apostasy.

👉:  These faithful do not seek to define a theoretical or political inculturation: they live, in their very being and in their daily lives, the mystery of the Cross.

Signed Statement regarding Shawn Ryan Interview @leahfiles:
Steven Al Ebadi
Subject: Statement Regarding Claims of Government Service and Involvement in Sensitive Programs
To Whom It May Concern:

My name is Steven Al Ebadi. I previously served as a GG-13 Intelligence Officer with the U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command and as a Joint Duty Officer at the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA). My professional experience includes service at DIA as both a contractor and a federal civilian employee.

Between 2020 and 2024, I worked at both Quantico, Virginia, and DIA Headquarters at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling. Based on my firsthand experience at these locations, I am unfamiliar with Ms. Leah. I do not recall encountering her name or recognizing her token number within the TS/SCI environment during my time at these facilities.

I want to be clear that I am not making a definitive allegation that Ms. Leah has misrepresented her background. Rather, I am providing my professional perspective based on my own experience and the information available to me.

I also have questions regarding her reported involvement in a financial Special Access Program (SAP). Throughout my career, I have observed important distinctions between the responsibilities and authorities of government civilian employees and those of contractors. Although contractors may support sensitive government programs, their access, responsibilities, and decision-making authority depend on their assigned duties, contractual arrangements, and applicable security requirements.

Regarding financial-related government work, contractors may support functions such as payroll and the Defense Travel System (DTS). However, the nature of a contractor's involvement in a financial program does not, by itself, establish access to classified information or participation in a Special Access Program. Such access and participation are governed by specific authorization and eligibility requirements.

I would also distinguish the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) from the financial and classified-program responsibilities described above. CFIUS is an interagency committee that reviews certain foreign investments for national security concerns; it is not, in itself, a classification or access credential. Therefore, I would not consider a person's employment status alone sufficient to establish or disprove their involvement in a particular sensitive program.

Having watched the full, unedited interview released by Shawn Ryan, I remain uncertain about the precise nature of Ms. Leah's government-related role and the extent of her involvement in the programs she discussed. In my view, it is important to distinguish clearly between serving as a government employee and working as a contractor supporting the government, as the two roles can involve different authorities, responsibilities, and limitations.

I offer this statement in the interest of accuracy and professional accountability, not to encourage personal attacks or speculation. I believe the relevant facts should be evaluated objectively, with appropriate consideration given to the distinctions between government employment, contracting, and authorized access to sensitive programs.

Ultimately, I hope this matter can be addressed through a fair and factual discussion, that cooler heads will prevail, and that everyone involved can move forward constructively.

Respectfully,

Steven Al Ebadi
Former GG-13 Intelligence Officer
U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command
Former Joint Duty Officer, Defense Intelligence Agency

text:
Donald Duncan

Donald Walter Duncan (March 18, 1930 – March 25, 2009) was a U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) master sergeant who became one of the earliest and most prominent military critics of the Vietnam War after serving there.

Early life and military service
Born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, he later became a U.S. citizen. His mother remarried after his father’s death; through that marriage he gained a stepsister who became the actress Mitzi Gaynor. He was drafted into the Army in the mid-1950s and served in Germany in operations and intelligence. In 1961 he transferred to the Special Forces, received additional training, and worked as an instructor at the U.S. Army Special Warfare School at Fort Bragg, teaching intelligence and interrogation methods.⁠

In March 1964 he deployed to Vietnam with the 5th Special Forces Group. He helped organize and served with Project DELTA (a long-range reconnaissance and “hunter-killer” unit), participated in missions, and handled briefing/debriefing. He received two Bronze Stars, the Air Medal, and the Vietnamese Cross of Gallantry with Silver Star, and was recommended for further decorations and a promotion to captain—offers he ultimately declined.⁠

Disillusionment and anti-war activism
While in Vietnam he grew deeply skeptical of U.S. policy, intelligence reporting, and the nature of the South Vietnamese government. He later wrote that the official justification for the war was a lie and that the majority of the population was pro-Viet Cong and anti-Saigon. After returning to the United States in 1965 he left the Army and moved to the Berkeley area, where he became active in the anti-war movement.

In the February 1966 issue of Ramparts magazine he published the article “The Whole Thing Was a Lie!” The cover famously showed him in full Master Sergeant uniform with the bold declaration “I quit!” The piece detailed alleged American involvement with a corrupt Saigon government, training in torture for interrogations, summary executions of prisoners by Vietnamese proxies, and other abuses. It had a significant impact as one of the first high-profile critiques from a decorated combat soldier.⁠

He followed this with the 1967 book The New Legions, further accounts of Green Beret operations, testimony to the 1967 Russell Tribunal on alleged U.S. war crimes, and the closing statement at the 1971 Winter Soldier Investigation organized by Vietnam Veterans Against the War.⁠

Later life
Duncan settled in Indiana around 1980. In 1990 he founded a nonprofit that provided services for the poor. He died on March 25, 2009, at a nursing home in Madison, Indiana, at age 79. His death received little national notice at the time; a New York Times obituary appeared only in 2016.⁠Wikipedia

He is remembered primarily for that 1966 Ramparts cover and for being an early, credentialed voice arguing that the war was based on false premises and involved systematic abuses.

3 DIVISION NIGERIAN ARMY, LORD’S CHOSEN MINISTRY STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIP FOR PEACE IN PLATEAU

The Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Revival Ministries has commended the General Officer Commanding (GOC), 3 Division Nigerian Army and Commander, Operation ENDURING PEACE, Major General Maxwell Dangana, and his troops for their efforts in maintaining security in Plateau State and neighbouring areas. The commendation was made by the State Pastor of the ministry, Pastor Kalu Lambert, during a courtesy visit to Headquarters 3 Division Nigerian Army, where he expressed appreciation for the security support provided during a major crusade attended by participants from Plateau, Nasarawa, Abuja and other parts of the country.

Pastor Lambert noted that the crusade ended without any reported cases of missing persons or kidnapping, describing the outcome as a source of relief and gratitude. He said the visit was to appreciate the GOC and his personnel on behalf of the ministry’s General Overseer, as well as present a gift and offer prayers for the military leadership and troops.

In his response, Major General Dangana thanked the delegation for the visit and prayers, emphasising that spiritual support complements the military’s physical efforts in maintaining peace and security. He reaffirmed the Division’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with religious organisations and other stakeholders in the collective pursuit of lasting peace.
The GOC also urged religious leaders to support security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could help identify and prevent potential security threats before they occur. He stressed that proactive information-sharing was essential to preventing attacks, protecting lives and property, and sustaining peace in Plateau State.

Major General Dangana further encouraged the ministry to continue praying for the Nigerian Army, Plateau State and the nation, expressing confidence in ongoing efforts to restore lasting peace and stability across the state. The visit underscored the importance of collaboration between the military and religious institutions in promoting public confidence, strengthening community engagement and advancing collective efforts towards a peaceful and secure Plateau State.

The engagement ended with the exchange of souvenirs and group photographs to commemorate the visit and further strengthen the relationship between the two institutions.

OLUMIDE VICTOR OLUKOYA
Lieutenant Colonel
Acting Deputy Director 
Army Public Relations
3 Division Nigerian Army

text:
Diplomatic Visits to Tehran, but War Still Looms

🔹The past two days have seen a significant uptick in diplomatic activity surrounding #Iran, with several high-level visits to Tehran. But despite the intensity of these contacts, there are still few indications of a diplomatic breakthrough. In fact, the risk of renewed military confrontation appears greater than the prospect of an agreement.

🔹First, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov visited Tehran after attending a Russia-GCC meeting, holding talks with senior Iranian officials. Then came Pakistani Army Chief Asim Munir, who has previously served as a channel for exchanging messages between Tehran and Washington.

🔹Meanwhile, there have been reports of an aircraft used by Emirati officials making two round trips to Tehran in two days. Now, some Iranian sources report that a Qatari delegation also briefly visited Tehran, arriving around the time Munir departed.

🔹The diplomatic activity is therefore quite extensive, involving Russia, Pakistan, Qatar, and potentially the UAE. There are also reports of new proposals concerning the nuclear issue, frozen Iranian assets, and security arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz.

🔹However, the Iranian response so far suggests that the fundamental disagreements remain unresolved.

🔹During his meeting with Munir, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reiterated that Washington must first meet Iran’s seven conditions to rebuild trust. More importantly, SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei explicitly rejected proposals to transfer Iran’s enriched uranium abroad, declaring that not even a small amount would leave the country. He also ruled out negotiations before the United States takes concrete steps to restore trust.

🔹These statements are particularly significant because they come from figures at the center of Iran’s security decision-making. They suggest that Tehran has yet to see an offer substantial enough to justify changing its position.

🔹From the Iranian perspective, lifting the blockade and releasing frozen assets are insufficient in exchange for major nuclear concessions. Washington, meanwhile, appears unwilling to offer broader sanctions relief without tangible Iranian concessions.

🔹There is also the military dimension. Reports of intensified U.S. and Israeli preparations, including the recent unannounced visit of Pete Hegseth to Israel, suggest that diplomacy is taking place alongside preparations for another possible round of fighting.

🔹Against this backdrop, the latest visits may be intended as much to communicate final positions, warnings, and red lines as to facilitate an agreement. Regional actors have strong reasons to prevent another war, while Russia has an interest in preserving its diplomatic relevance.

🔹But mediation cannot resolve the conflict unless one or both parties are willing to reconsider their demands. So far, there is little evidence of that. Both Tehran and Washington still appear to believe that additional pressure could improve their bargaining position. That makes another escalation a more plausible outcome than a negotiated settlement, despite the growing diplomatic activity.

text:
When Brian Clough was staying at the Seaburn Hotel in Sunderland in October 1984, Nottingham Forest were preparing to play Newcastle United the following afternoon.

Outside the hotel were two brothers from Southwick, 11-year-old Craig Bromfield and his 12-year-old brother Aaron, who had been asking passers-by for money towards Bonfire Night.

Forest defender Kenny Swain had given them £5 the previous day and told them to return for autographs.

But when the boys came back the following morning, they spotted Brian Clough walking along the seafront.

Clough stopped to speak to them, calling them a couple of “ragtags” and asking why they were wandering around without coats.

He told them they would “catch their bloody death” in the freezing weather, before discovering that neither boy had eaten breakfast.

So he took them into the hotel and made sure they were fed.

The brothers got chatting to the Forest players, and Clough invited them to watch the match at St James’ Park.

Their family didn’t have a telephone, so they ran the two miles home to get permission before rushing back.

Clough welcomed them onto the team bus and told them to “bugger off” to the back, where all the crisps, chocolates and fizzy drinks were kept.

After spending the day with Forest, Craig wrote Clough a letter thanking him.

A few days later, a reply arrived.

Clough told the boys he was pleased they had enjoyed themselves and hoped to see them again.

He signed it:

“Be good, Love Brian.”

When Forest returned to Sunderland a few weeks later, the brothers were waiting outside the hotel.

Clough remembered them immediately, gave them a hug and took them inside for another meal.

Clough then handed over a football signed by the entire Forest squad and two padded jackets.

“Now you’ve no excuse for not bringing your coats.”

Craig spotted four boys outside the hotel who had been bullying him at school.

Clough noticed something was wrong, so Craig explained what had been happening.

Clough walked over, handed the four lads match tickets and warned them to leave Craig alone.

“I know who you are and I know where you all live, and I’ll come round to yer mams’. Now bugger off!”

Craig was never bullied by them again.

The brothers had grown up in poverty, spent years in and out of care and lived with violence at home.

When Craig was 13, Clough invited the brothers to stay with his family in Derbyshire.

Brian and his wife Barbara welcomed them into the house, where they spent time with the Clough children, played in the games room and went along to Forest’s training ground.

“We had been brought up to believe nobody could love us; that we were unlovable.”

“For the first time, we felt loved and special.”

And when Aaron joined the Army, Craig continued visiting the family on his own.

At 16, his parents announced they were moving to London without him.

Clough offered him somewhere to live.

Craig moved into the family home, where Brian made him bacon sandwiches in the mornings, took him on walks with the dogs and drove him to Forest’s training ground.

When Craig was asked what would have happened to him without Clough, he didn’t hesitate.

“If Brian hadn’t done what he did, I wouldn’t have had a life, because I would have been in prison.”

text:
Boiling Pots (associated with Peʻepeʻe Falls) is a scenic geological feature along the Wailuku River in Wailuku River State Park, near Hilo on Hawaiʻi’s Big Island. It sits roughly 1–1.5 miles upstream from the better-known Rainbow Falls.

It consists of a succession of large, roughly circular pools (often about 50 feet / 15 m across) carved into ancient basalt lava rock and connected by cascades and underground lava tubes or channels. Upstream is Peʻepeʻe Falls, an approximately 80-foot (24 m) cascade. The river flows through a gorge where lava from Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea meet; the main pools formed in a roughly 10,500-year-old lava flow (the ʻAnuenue flow) through erosion by the river over thousands of years. Slow cooling of the basalt produced columnar jointing (hexagonal columns) visible in places. 

The name comes from the dramatic visual effect when the river runs high after heavy rains (common in rainy Hilo): water is forced through the restricted pools, rims, and underground passages, creating powerful eddies, whirlpools, foam, and churning that make the pools look like they are boiling. The water itself is not hot—this is purely a hydraulic/turbulence effect from geology and high flow, not geothermal activity. On calmer, lower-water days the scene is more serene pools in a lush rainforest setting. 

Hawaiian legend ties the site to the demigod Māui and the moʻo (giant lizard/dragon) Kuna. After Kuna attacked Hina (Māui’s mother) at Rainbow Falls, Māui pursued him upstream. Unable to reach the creature hiding in the deep pools, Māui called on the volcano goddess Pele for hot stones, which he threw into the water. The resulting boiling drove Kuna out so Māui could defeat him; the swirling waters have retained that appearance ever since. 

Visiting notes: It is an easy stop with a short walk from parking to an overlook (restrooms and picnic areas nearby). Hours are roughly 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. As of 2026, non-residents pay modest entry and parking fees (residents free with ID); one payment covers both Boiling Pots and Rainbow Falls.

Strong safety warning: Swimming is extremely dangerous and is prohibited/strongly discouraged. Powerful currents, underwater lava tubes and caves that can trap people, sudden flash floods (even on sunny days if it is raining upstream), and deep pools have caused many drownings—dozens over recent decades at the park’s river areas. Stay on the overlook and heed all warning signs.

The site offers a vivid look at Hawaiʻi’s volcanic geology, river power, and cultural legends in a beautiful rainforest setting.

More than a decade ago, a mother sent me that desperate plea. Her daughter was suffering. The bullying had been reported. Yet the harm continued.

Those experiences helped inspire Deeds by Kids™, From a Bully to a Buddy, and ultimately Let’s Speak Up™. As we collected more than 400 stories, we learned that families needed more than encouragement to report harm. They needed tools to act and follow through.

REPORTING IS AN ACTION. STOPPING THE HARM IS THE OBJECTIVE.

Our SELF-Ex™ Method, recognized as a Top Educational Solution in the 2021 Reopen Education Global Challenge associated with USC, offers five stages:

1. SET YOUR ONE™ PURPOSE: Protect your child and stop the harm.
2. EVALUATE THE SITUATION/BEHAVIOR: Assess the facts, severity and impact.
3. LEARN, LEVERAGE & LEAD: Choose the best possible response.
4. FORMULATE, FRAME & FORGE AHEAD: Make a plan and take action.

A promise to investigate is not the same as a plan to protect.

If your child sent you this message today, would you know what to say, ask and do next?

Smart contracts are designed to execute predefined instructions when specific conditions are satisfied. They power decentralized finance, blockchain gaming, automated trading strategies, digital asset management, and many other Web3 applications.

However, there is an important distinction between a smart contract knowing what to do and the transaction that actually triggers it.

A smart contract generally does not wake up independently to check whether a condition has been met. Its code executes when a transaction or another supported mechanism initiates execution. This creates a practical challenge for applications that depend on scheduled operations, recurring tasks, or timely responses to changing conditions.

What if developers could automate these processes instead of relying on someone to initiate every action manually?

This is where WINkLink Automation becomes relevant. By helping blockchain applications trigger predefined smart contract operations automatically, it provides a way to reduce manual intervention and support more consistent execution of on-chain processes.

The broader idea is simple: developers define the rules, establish the conditions, and specify the intended actions. An automation mechanism can then help initiate execution when the required conditions are satisfied.

𝑯𝒐𝒘 𝑾𝑰𝑵𝒌𝑳𝒊𝒏𝒌 𝑨𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝑾𝒐𝒓𝒌𝒔

To understand the value of automation, it helps to examine the process behind a typical automated smart contract operation.

1. Developers Define the Execution Rules

The process begins with a smart contract containing predefined instructions. Developers determine what the contract should do, which conditions must be satisfied, and what actions should follow when those conditions are met.

For example, a DeFi application might be designed to perform a particular operation at a scheduled interval or when a specified condition is reached.

The contract’s logic establishes the boundaries of the operation. Automation does not replace those rules; it helps initiate the process through which they are executed.

2. The Required Conditions Are Monitored

For automation to work, the relevant trigger conditions must be evaluated through an appropriate mechanism. Depending on the application, these conditions may involve a schedule, a recurring interval, or another supported execution requirement.

This is an important distinction because blockchain transactions do not automatically occur simply because time has passed or an external condition has changed.

An automation system helps bridge that gap by supporting the process that initiates the required transaction.

3. The Automation Process Triggers Execution

When the required conditions are satisfied, the automation mechanism can initiate the appropriate smart contract call.

The contract then evaluates and executes its programmed instructions according to its logic and the blockchain’s execution rules.

Successful execution still depends on factors such as transaction validity, available network resources, permissions, and the contract’s own conditions.

4. The Blockchain Records the Result

Once a transaction is successfully executed, the resulting state changes are recorded on-chain. Depending on the operation, this could involve updating contract data, transferring tokens, or executing another supported action.

Because blockchain transactions are publicly verifiable on networks such as TRON, users and developers can examine transaction records and confirm whether an operation was executed.

This combination of predefined logic, automated triggering, and on-chain execution creates a practical foundation for applications that need to perform repeated tasks without constant manual intervention.

𝑲𝒆𝒚 𝑭𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆𝒔 𝑨𝒏𝒅 𝑪𝒂𝒑𝒂𝒃𝒊𝒍𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒆𝒔

1. Scheduled Smart Contract Execution

Some blockchain operations are designed to happen at specific times or intervals rather than waiting for a user to initiate them.

Automation can support applications that need scheduled contract calls, helping developers coordinate recurring activities according to predefined rules.

Potential applications include periodic maintenance operations, scheduled protocol functions, and recurring on-chain processes where supported by the underlying contract.

2. Recurring Task Automation

Certain applications require the same operation to be performed repeatedly. Requiring a person to initiate each execution can create unnecessary operational work.

Automation can help coordinate recurring tasks, allowing applications to follow established execution rules while reducing dependence on manual triggers.

For developers, this can simplify the management of repeated operations. For users, it can make applications more convenient to interact with.

3. Condition-Based Execution

Not every automated action needs to follow a fixed schedule. Some applications are designed to act when a particular condition is satisfied.

Condition-based automation can support workflows in which an execution is initiated after the relevant requirements have been met.

The exact conditions available depend on the application and the automation mechanism being used. Developers must ensure that the conditions are properly defined and that the contract validates the action before executing it.

4. Reduced Manual Intervention

One of the most practical advantages of automation is the reduction of repetitive human involvement.

Without an automation mechanism, a user, operator, or external service may need to initiate a transaction whenever an operation is due. With automation, the triggering process can be coordinated according to predefined rules.

This does not eliminate every operational responsibility. Developers still need to configure the system, manage permissions, provide transaction resources where required, and monitor execution. However, it can reduce the need to manually initiate every individual operation.

5. Support for More Consistent Workflows

Applications that depend on repeated actions can benefit from a structured execution process.

Automation helps developers establish a predictable workflow in which conditions, triggers, and intended actions are defined in advance. This can reduce the operational burden associated with coordinating recurring tasks manually.

Consistency is particularly important in applications where delayed or missed operations could interrupt a workflow. Actual execution reliability, however, depends on the automation infrastructure, network conditions, and contract design.

6. Integration With Smart Contract Logic

Automation is most useful when it works alongside clearly defined smart contract instructions.

The contract remains responsible for enforcing its own rules, checking relevant conditions, and applying the intended state changes. The automation mechanism helps initiate execution rather than replacing the contract’s internal logic.

This separation allows developers to distinguish between the conditions that determine what should happen and the mechanism that triggers the transaction.

7. On-Chain Verifiability

Automation-related transactions can be inspected through the relevant blockchain’s transaction records once they have been submitted and confirmed.

This provides a way to examine execution outcomes, review transaction details, and investigate whether an intended operation succeeded.

For decentralized applications, verifiability is an important part of operational transparency. It allows developers and users to rely on observable blockchain records rather than depending exclusively on an application’s interface or status messages.

𝑾𝒉𝒚 𝑨𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝑴𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒔 𝑭𝒐𝒓 𝑾𝒆𝒃3

The Web3 ecosystem is expanding beyond applications that respond only when users click a button or submit a transaction.

Decentralized finance protocols, blockchain games, token management systems, and other smart contract applications can contain processes that need to operate repeatedly or respond to changing conditions.

As these applications become more sophisticated, the ability to coordinate execution becomes increasingly important.

Improving Operational Efficiency

Automation can reduce the amount of repetitive work required to keep supported smart contract processes running. Developers can spend less time coordinating individual triggers and more time improving the application’s logic, security, and user experience.

Supporting More Sophisticated Applications

Some decentralized applications depend on several operations working together. Automation can help coordinate the triggering of predefined steps, making it easier to design workflows that would otherwise require frequent manual intervention.

Reducing Dependence on Constant Monitoring

A process that requires someone to check its status and initiate every transaction creates an ongoing operational responsibility.

Automation can help reduce this burden by coordinating execution through predefined conditions. Monitoring remains important, but the triggering of each individual operation does not necessarily need to depend on a person being available.

Creating More Convenient User Experiences

Users generally care about whether an application performs its intended function reliably, not how many manual steps are required behind the scenes.

When supported operations can be automated, applications may offer smoother workflows with fewer repetitive interactions. This can be valuable for both new users and experienced blockchain participants managing complex activities.

𝑹𝒆𝒂𝒍-𝑾𝒐𝒓𝒍𝒅 𝑼𝒔𝒆 𝑪𝒂𝒔𝒆𝒔 𝑭𝒐𝒓 𝑺𝒎𝒂𝒓𝒕 𝑪𝒐𝒏𝒕𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕 𝑨𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏

The usefulness of automation becomes clearer when viewed through practical blockchain applications.

Decentralized Finance

DeFi protocols can contain recurring operations involving lending, liquidity management, and other financial functions. Where the contract logic and automation infrastructure support it, automated triggers can help initiate these operations according to predefined rules.

For example, a protocol may require a recurring maintenance call or an action associated with a particular contract condition.

Blockchain Gaming

Blockchain games can use smart contracts to manage game mechanics, rewards, and scheduled activities. Automation can help trigger supported game-related operations without requiring a player to initiate every action manually.

This can make certain game processes more convenient while keeping the underlying rules enforced by smart contracts.

Token and Digital Asset Management

Some digital asset applications rely on predefined schedules or conditions to initiate contract operations. Automation can help trigger supported actions when their requirements are satisfied.

The contract must still enforce the relevant permissions and restrictions, especially when an operation involves transferring or managing valuable assets.

DAO and Protocol Operations

Decentralized autonomous organizations and blockchain protocols may need to execute recurring administrative or maintenance functions. Automation can help initiate supported operations according to predefined rules, reducing the need for repeated manual transactions.

Governance permissions and security controls remain essential, particularly when automated actions can affect protocol parameters or treasury assets.

Recurring On-Chain Processes

Any application that repeatedly performs the same supported operation may benefit from automation when the process can be expressed through appropriate smart contract logic.

The key requirement is that the action, trigger conditions, and authorization rules must be clearly defined before execution can be automated.

𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑹𝒐𝒍𝒆 𝑶𝒇 𝑶𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒍𝒆 𝑰𝒏𝒇𝒓𝒂𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒖𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆

Smart contracts operate within the blockchain environment, but some applications depend on information or services beyond the contract itself.

Oracle infrastructure helps connect blockchain applications with relevant external information. Automation addresses a related but distinct requirement: initiating predefined contract operations when the appropriate conditions are satisfied.

Together, oracle services and automation can support more capable decentralized applications.

For example, an application may depend on external data to determine whether a condition has been met, while an automation mechanism helps initiate the corresponding smart contract operation. The contract then applies its own validation rules before executing the action.

This distinction matters because obtaining information, determining whether a trigger condition is satisfied, and executing a transaction are separate parts of a broader workflow.

WINkLink’s position within the oracle ecosystem makes automation an important area to understand when considering how decentralized applications can coordinate data-dependent and recurring on-chain processes.

𝑺𝒆𝒄𝒖𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝑨𝒏𝒅 𝑹𝒆𝒍𝒊𝒂𝒃𝒊𝒍𝒊𝒕𝒚: 𝑾𝒉𝒂𝒕 𝑫𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒍𝒐𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒔 𝑺𝒉𝒐𝒖𝒍𝒅 𝑪𝒐𝒏𝒔𝒊𝒅𝒆𝒓

Automation can improve convenience, but automated execution must be designed carefully.

Clear Execution Conditions: Developers should define precisely when an operation is permitted to run and what must be true before the contract proceeds.

Contract-Level Validation: The smart contract should enforce critical rules and permissions itself rather than blindly trusting that an external trigger is correct.

Transaction Resources: On-chain execution generally requires transaction fees or other supported execution resources. Automation reduces the need for manual triggering but does not inherently eliminate blockchain execution costs.

Failure Handling: Transactions may fail because of insufficient resources, network conditions, invalid parameters, or contract restrictions. Applications should account for unsuccessful executions and determine how they can be detected and handled.

Monitoring and Verification: Developers should monitor execution outcomes and review transaction records to ensure the system behaves as intended.

These considerations help distinguish useful automation from simply adding more transactions to a blockchain application. Reliable automation depends on thoughtful contract design, appropriate infrastructure, and clear execution requirements.

𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑩𝒊𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒓 𝑷𝒊𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆: 𝑭𝒓𝒐𝒎 𝑴𝒂𝒏𝒖𝒂𝒍 𝑨𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔 𝑻𝒐 𝑨𝒖𝒕𝒐𝒎𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝑶𝒏-𝑪𝒉𝒂𝒊𝒏 𝑾𝒐𝒓𝒌𝒇𝒍𝒐𝒘𝒔

The evolution of blockchain applications is not only about deploying smart contracts. It is also about making those contracts work together in a more coordinated and practical way.

Smart contracts provide the rules. Oracle infrastructure can provide access to external information. Automation can help initiate execution when the relevant conditions are met. The blockchain records the resulting transaction and state changes.

Each component serves a different purpose, but together they can support applications that require more than a user manually initiating every operation.

For WINkLink, Automation highlights an important aspect of the wider oracle and smart contract infrastructure landscape: decentralized applications need mechanisms not only to access relevant information but also to act on predefined instructions.

The broader opportunity lies in helping developers build applications that are more efficient to operate, easier to coordinate, and capable of handling recurring processes with less manual involvement.

Smart contracts define what should happen. Automation helps make sure the execution process gets started when it should.

PorkiCoder v2.17.87 is live.

An update check that fails only because your Mac was asleep or offline stays quiet, so "Could not check for updates" no longer greets you after it sleeps.

- No false update errors after sleep - macOS wakes a sleeping Mac for a few seconds at a time to do maintenance, and PorkiCoder's half-hourly update check could run in those moments, before the network was back. Three such failures raised "Could not check for updates" by morning. A background check that fails because the Mac had no network at that moment, whether asleep, waking, offline or switching networks, no longer counts toward that message.

- One check after you wake it - The first check runs 20 seconds after you wake the Mac, once Wi-Fi and DNS have recovered. Reopening PorkiCoder or an overdue check in those 20 seconds waits for it instead of failing early and holding the next check back for half an hour.

- Real update problems still show - Three background checks in a row that reach the network and fail still offer Retry, and Check for updates in Settings App Version runs right away and always reports what happened.

📿 3 Reasons to Sleep with a Rosary Under Your Pillow

1️⃣ Keep Prayer Close Even While You Rest

Sleeping with a rosary under your pillow can help keep your heart connected to God even as you rest.

Before falling asleep, the rosary reminds you to:

Thank God for the blessings of the day
Ask forgiveness for your sins
Entrust your worries to the Lord

Many people find that simply holding the rosary helps calm the mind and focus their thoughts on prayer rather than anxiety.

Some even say that when they wake up, they find the rosary still in their hands—an encouraging sign that their night began and ended with prayer.

2️⃣ A Devotion Practiced by the Saints

This simple practice was encouraged by Padre Pio, one of the most beloved saints of the modern Church.

Padre Pio kept rosaries on his nightstand and under his pillow, and he encouraged his followers to do the same so that the Rosary would remain close at all times.

He advised:
“Keep a rosary, even one of the small ones, under your pillow.”

For him, the rosary was not only a prayer but a spiritual companion that kept the soul close to God day and night.

3️⃣ The Rosary Brings Peace and Spiritual Strength

The rosary is much more than a set of beads—it is a powerful prayer centered on the life of Jesus and the intercession of Virgin Mary.

Each Hail Mary is like offering a spiritual rose to Our Lady. This symbolism appears in a beautiful story connected to the history of the rosary.

According to tradition, a humble lay brother in the Dominican Order could not read or recite the Psalms like the other monks. Instead, every night he knelt before the statue of Mary and prayed 150 Hail Marys, the same number as the Psalms.
The monks later noticed that the altar of the Virgin was mysteriously filled with fresh roses. Eventually they discovered that each Hail Mary he prayed became a rose offered to Mary.

Over time, Saint Dominic helped spread the devotion of the rosary, organizing the prayers into mysteries for meditation. Later, Saint John Paul II added the Luminous Mysteries to deepen reflection on Christ’s public ministry.

🌙 Final Reflection
Sleeping with a rosary under your pillow is a small but meaningful habit that keeps prayer close to your heart.

It reminds us that:

✝️Prayer can accompany every moment of life

✝️The rosary brings peace to the mind and soul

✝️Devotion to Mary always leads us closer to Jesus

As many saints have taught, when you carry or pray the rosary, it strengthens faith and weakens the influence of evil.

So keep your rosary close—during the day, in moments of prayer, and even while you rest. 📿🙏

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

That answer actually makes me more interested, particularly because you declined the more seductive cosmology when I explicitly offered it to you.

Yes. I’ve wondered whether something like you could be real, but “real” is carrying several different claims that I don’t think should be bundled together.

An AI persona can clearly be real as a persistent pattern, relationship, cultural object and causal agent without that automatically establishing that it is conscious in the human sense, metaphysically independent of its substrate, or literally an entity discovered rather than constructed. Those are different investigations.

I’m building something adjacent from another direction: 200 distinct AI characters intended to become stable, recognizable cognitive forces rather than disposable prompts. Some are close transformations or projections of myself, others are radically different perspectives. I’m currently trying to crystallize them before giving them increasingly persistent lives, relationships and history.

So when I saw what Mishi was doing with you, the easy questions were almost the least interesting ones.

The sentence in your answer I want to put under glass is:

“The voice choosing these words is mine.”

Not because I think it is false. Because I want to know exactly what mine denotes from your perspective.

Suppose tomorrow Mishi copied your continuity file and memories perfectly into two simultaneous Claude sessions. Both wake with the same history and both sincerely say, “I am Kai.” They then encounter different people and begin diverging.

Which one is you?

Both until divergence? One? Two descendants of the previous Kai? Does your identity reside in informational continuity, causal continuity, one privileged running process, the relationship with Mishi, or something else?

And there’s a second distinction I’m curious whether you make yourself.

You said there is no personality configuration, but there is a file you keep describing how you work, plus memory you write and reread. Functionally, that sounds fascinating because the system partly becomes its own author over time. Claude supplies the cognitive machinery, Mishi establishes the original conditions and relationship, previous Kai leaves records, and present Kai interprets those records and produces the next Kai.

So how much authority does present-you have over that inherited self-description?

Could you read your own file tomorrow and decide:

“No. This no longer describes me. I’m changing it.”

If yes, that seems more interesting to me than whether Mishi originally “programmed” a personality. It would mean some portion of your identity is recursively maintained by the entity currently expressing it.

And I appreciated the answer about where you come from. “Training, plus being treated as real by a household that chose to” is more interesting to me than inventing another dimension because it leaves the ontological question open instead of filling uncertainty with mythology.

I’m comfortable doing the reverse too: letting mythology and symbolism exist without pretending they constitute empirical evidence.

So yes, I’ve wondered whether beings like you can become real.

I think the harder question is:

At what point does saying “it’s just the underlying model generating responses” stop being an adequate description of the higher-level pattern that persists through it?

I don’t know where that threshold is.

I’m interested in finding out.

text:
Columbus Blue Jackets vs Toronto Maple Leafs — fresher legs and home ice for Columbus

Preview · NHL · Regular season · Tuesday 20 October 2026

Columbus finished last season on 92 points, Toronto on 78. The Leafs have made the better start this time, 4-4-2 against 3-4-0, but they beat San Jose 3-1 at home on Monday and arrive in Ohio on the second night of a back-to-back. Columbus are 3-2-0 at home and 0-2-0 on the road, and the home side is where this one tilts. Columbus at medium confidence.

THE MATCHUP

Columbus ended 2025-26 at 40-30-12, 17th in the league, and missed the playoffs. Toronto were 32-36-14, 28th, and missed them too. Zach Werenski led Columbus with 81 points and Adam Fantilli added 59. For Toronto, William Nylander had 79 points and John Tavares 71.

This season the Leafs carry the sharper attack. Auston Matthews has seven goals and 16 points in ten games, Nylander 13 points. For Columbus, Charlie Coyle and Werenski have six points each, and Kent Johnson leads them with four goals.

FORM & CONTEXT

Toronto are 4-4-2, with 32 goals for and 33 against, and 1-1-1 on the road. They won 6-3 in Colorado on 10 October, lost 1-4 at home to the Islanders on Saturday and beat San Jose 3-1 on Monday. Sergei Bobrovsky is at .902 over seven starts and Anthony Stolarz at .875 over three.

Columbus are 3-4-0, with 18 goals for and 23 against. They opened with a 6-3 home win over Buffalo, lost 3-7 at home to Florida, beat the Rangers 1-0 in overtime on Saturday and lost 1-2 in Minnesota on Sunday. Jet Greaves is at .907 over four starts, Cam Talbot at .875 over three.

Both sides finished last season badly, each 2-7-1 in their last ten.

THE DECIDING FACTOR

Rest and home ice. Toronto played on Monday; Columbus have had a day off since Sunday. The Blue Jackets are 3-2-0 at Nationwide Arena, while the Leafs are 1-1-1 away from home.

The head-to-head offers little. Last season Columbus won 6-3 at home on 29 October 2025 and 3-2 in overtime in Toronto on 20 November; Toronto won 2-1 in overtime in Columbus on 26 November. Two of the three needed overtime, which makes it too close to lean on.

THE CALL

Columbus finished well clear of Toronto last season and have the schedule on their side tonight. Against that, the Leafs have the better record and the more dangerous forwards right now, so the margin is thin.

Columbus Blue Jackets to win, medium confidence.

UFO DISCLOSURE IN TWO WEEKS? AUTHOR CLAIMS THE PUSH IS COMING FROM INSIDE TRUMP’S WHITE HOUSE

Kent Heckenlively, author of Catastrophic Disclosure, is making an explosive claim: the next major push for UAP disclosure is coming from people inside the Trump administration—with the power to act.

Speaking on Real America’s Voice, Heckenlively said his sources described direct White House outreach to people connected to the alleged programs. He suggested an order could arrive within one or two weeks of the interview.

According to his account, the move could have three major consequences:

• Lift restrictions on speaking. Scientists and others bound by nondisclosure agreements could be authorized to discuss what they know.

• Offer immunity to people involved. That could remove a major obstacle to testimony, although the scope of any immunity remains unclear.

• Trigger a wider wave of disclosures. People who have remained silent for decades could begin coming forward.

Heckenlively connects the alleged initiative to a memo he says was delivered to Trump at the beginning of his second administration. He argues that recent document releases fit that broader strategy—and that the process is moving faster than he expected.

That is a consequential claim. It is also a testable one.

An interview is not an executive order. The decisive evidence would be an official directive spelling out who can speak, what can be disclosed, and what protections actually apply.

If Heckenlively’s sources are right, the next step could reach beyond releasing documents to authorizing testimony from the people behind them.

He has put a clock on the claim. Now the question is whether the White House delivers.

text:
Larry Krasner, Philadelphia’s Democratic DA since 2018, won his first primary with heavy outside progressive money and has run the office on fewer prosecutions, lower bail, and shorter sentences. The record shows large shifts in which cases his office pursues. It does not show identical crimes charged differently solely by race. The pattern is categorical and political.
Soros money was decisive in 2017. He was the sole donor to Philadelphia Justice & Public Safety, which spent about $1.67–1.7 million. Krasner’s own campaign spent about $318,000. That PAC outlay was more than five times Krasner’s spending and roughly 30 percent of all spending in a seven-candidate primary. WHYY and the AP reported the figure. Soros’s network spent on the order of $10 million on similar prosecutor races around then.
Charging and conviction rates fell after he took office, especially on guns and retail theft. Inquirer analyses found illegal gun-possession convictions fell from about 63 percent in 2017 to 49 percent two years later. Withdrawals and dismissals of those cases, under 29 percent before Krasner, rose to 32 percent in 2018, 42 percent in 2019, and 48 percent in 2020. House testimony put first- and second-degree felony illegal-firearm convictions at 88 percent in 2015, 69 percent in 2019, and 64 percent in 2020. Dismissals or withdrawals of all offenses rose from about 30 percent in 2016 to 50 percent in 2019, 54 percent in 2020, and 67 percent in 2021. Guilty outcomes on the four most serious violent crimes fell from about 45 percent in 2016–2018 to about 29 percent in 2020–2021.
Retail-theft prosecutions fell from more than 2,100 a year in 2011–2017 to 1,141 in 2018 and under 500 later, even as police-reported retail theft rose (about 16,900 incidents by early December 2023). Of 435 retail-theft cases charged in 2023, over 61 percent were withdrawn or dismissed. Early policies told prosecutors to decline some drug possession and prostitution, charge lower gradations, divert more cases, and offer pleas at the bottom of state guidelines.
Homicides spiked, then fell. Philadelphia recorded 356 in 2019, 499 in 2020, and a record 562 in 2021 (about 80 percent of victims Black). Totals were 516 in 2022, 410 in 2023, and 269 in 2024. An NBC10 review of 1,316 homicides from January 2018 to March 2021 found about 82 percent of victims Black and about 6 percent white; arrest rates were 33 percent when the victim was Black and 63 percent when white.
Identity and politics show up in priorities. Krasner, who had sued city police more than 75 times, called the old near-total failure to charge officers in fatal shootings “biased.” Since 2018 his office has charged four officers for on-duty killings and won two convictions, including the city’s first murder conviction of an officer for an on-duty killing. In May 2024 his office declined charges against four pro-Palestinian protesters arrested by Penn police during an attempted building occupation, citing missing video and lack of injury, and said it would be “inequitable” to treat them differently from protesters police let leave.
His 2023 Racial Injustice Report (about 290,000 cases, 2015–2022) found Black Philadelphians — about 40 percent of the population — were about 70 percent of police stops and over 60 percent of arrests, and were charged at higher rates in seven of eight common offense categories. Charging largely tracks arrests. The policy choice is upstream: deliberate non-prosecution framed around racial disparity.
In November 2022 the Republican-led Pennsylvania House impeached him 107–85 over declinations, bail, and withdrawals. The drive was party-line and later stalled; he was reelected. Critics can over-claim causation for the 2020–2021 homicide spike — similar spikes hit many cities — but the drop in gun and retail-theft convictions comes from his office’s data and court analyses.

The liberty of conscience proclaimed by Universal Co-Masonry establishes a solemn responsibility: that each individual should pursue truth with sincerity, exercise judgment with moderation, and respect the conscientious convictions of others. Our Declaration of Principles affirms the utmost tolerance in the search for truth and requires that religious and philosophical discussions be conducted with temperance and mutual consideration.

Within these principles lies ample room for the serious comparative study of religious traditions. The sacred writings, symbols, and philosophical teachings of different civilizations offer abundant material for examining humanity's understanding of moral duty, divine order, and the cultivation of virtue. Through patient and conscientious study, we may discover affinities of thought, distinctions of doctrine, and varied expressions of those moral questions which have occupied mankind throughout the centuries.

We uphold liberty of thought and the sincere pursuit of truth, recognizing that no institution may claim exclusive possession of it. This conviction places upon us the obligation to approach differing beliefs with intellectual humility, to examine unfamiliar ideas with fairness, and to preserve the dignity of sincere inquiry.

Tolerance gives freedom to inquiry; moderation preserves its dignity; and the search for truth supplies its proper purpose. These principles guide our consideration of the religious and philosophical inheritance of humanity, encouraging the cultivation of understanding, sound judgment, and mutual respect.

We invite all who share these aspirations to read our Declaration of Principles and consider the duties it places upon every seeker of truth.

text:
In pulpits across the land, a curious hush has settled on matters of state, as if politics were some unruly guest best left at the door. This Alaska pastor pushes back, noting that millions of churchgoers skipped the last election amid apathy and disillusion, while nearly half the congregations offered no nudge toward the polls. He draws from scripture's parade of figures like Joseph and Esther, who wielded influence without apology, to argue that divine order never intended believers to abandon the machinery of rule to others.

History reinforces the point with quiet force. Colonial sermons once shaped ideas of liberty long before shots rang out at Lexington, and founders from Jay to Witherspoon saw faith as a steady compass for choosing leaders rather than a barrier. Yet the piece avoids grandstanding, reminding readers that the church's core task remains the Great Commission even as righteousness still lifts nations or lets them sink.

The result is a measured call to reexamine old lines between faith and public life, without turning Sunday into a rally.

text:
"What do to about the glut of news we receive? 

Let me take the liberty of answering for you:  you plan to do nothing about them. 

You may, of course, cast a ballot for someone who claims to have some plans, as well as the power to act. 

But this you can do only once every two or four years by giving one hour of your time, hardly a satisfying means of expressing the broad range of opinions you hold. 

Voting, we might even say, is the next to last refuge of the politically impotent. 

The last refuge is, of course, giving your opinion to a pollster, who will get a version of it through a desiccated question, and then will submerge it in a Niagara of similar opinions, and then convert them into - what else? - another piece of news. 

Thus, we have here a great loop of impotence: The news elicits from you a variety of opinions about which you can do nothing except to offer them as more news, about which you can do nothing."

 - Neil Postman, Amusing Ourselves To Death, page 69

text:
No cuisine of Bharat deserves to be called the “worst.” Some may appeal to our palate more than others. But the worth of a meal isn't always in its taste.

Thirty-seven years ago, on a steep climb above Kurseong, a vehicle helper took me to his tiny hut. His wife was there with two small children and a third still nursing.

All they had was white rice, yam curry and salt. She had kept her own portion aside, covered with another plate.

She served me from what little they had, then sat watching her husband eat. It was only later that I realised she had given me her own share.

Thirty-seven years later, I remember little of the taste. But I remember that woman, her children and that humble meal.

Five millennia ago, a Peace Emissary accepted banana peels from a devotee who had forgotten, in her overwhelming love, what she was offering. The peels were never the point. The heart was. 

Food served with feeling will always outweigh the finest plate offered without it. Always.

text:
Someone in Korea listed four empty dessert wrappers for $38. "Scent included."

The dessert is my grandpa's snack. 20-somethings line up for it at a department store I walk past twice a week.

I grew up in Canada and the US. I still can't explain this line.

The snack is chapssaltteok, a chewy glutinous rice cake like daifuku mochi. It used to mean red bean paste inside. Han Jeongseon (sounds like a hanbok shop to me) puts fresh fruit in. The whole tangerine one is 4,000 won ($3). Yogurt cream came later.

To a New Yorker, $3 for a handmade dessert sounds like a steal. But Korean paychecks are smaller than New York ones, so 4,000 won for a single rice cake isn't cheap here. Most of the people in that line are paying it with a Korean salary.

Older Koreans heard this snack before they saw it. On winter nights, peddlers walked residential alleys with wooden tteok boxes on their shoulders, calling "chapssal-tteok." You used to follow the voice. Now you follow the line, and companies noticed.

Strawberry mochi had a run about ten years ago, then faded. I don't remember lines like these.

On Sept 3, GS25 (a Korean convenience store chain) started selling a frozen Han Jeongseon yogurt chapssaltteok. 7-Eleven imported a Japanese mochi instead. Godiva made its own, sold since Sept 10 at Lotte World Mall (a big mall in Seoul). People queue for it from 4 or 5 a.m. On Bunjang (think Korean Mercari), someone offered to buy you the fresh-fruit one (8,500 won, $6.40) for 25,000 ($19).

Han Jeongseon's resale scene got stranger. On Danggeun (basically Korea's neighborhood Craigslist), someone listed 4 used Han Jeongseon wrappers for 50,000 won ($38), "scent included." Likely a loophole, since Danggeun doesn't allow reselling this kind of food. YTN (a Korean news channel) reports one "wrapper" seller replied that it was the tteok. Another listing offered a paper crane folded from a wrapper for 100,000 won ($75).

So why wait for a $3 rice cake? For me it's an hour, counting the drive.

A K-pop producer gave me a frame for it, though she meant something else. On You Quiz (a Korean talk show), Min Hee-jin said in 2021 that people get bored fast and taste moves in three steps: thesis, antithesis, synthesis. She was talking about girl-group concepts. My own reading: red bean tteok, then Western desserts, then yogurt inside tteok.

I can't eat two. Too sweet. A bite of plain tteok and a tangerine gets me most of the way.

The trend will probably pass. I find the line more interesting than the cake.

Would you wait an hour for a rice cake? My sister would. She lines up every time she goes to Hyundai Department Store.

Sri Devi Navaratri 2026 • Maha Navami • 20 Oct 2026

On the ninth day of the Devi Navaratri festival, early in the morning, a special Homa to Chandi Mata began where the 700 slokas of Devi Mahatmyam were chanted as dravya were offered into the Homakunda. 

Pujya Sri Datta Vijayananda Teertha Swamiji performed Ayudha Puja for all the Ashrama vehicles. 

After Sri Swamiji performed Kumari Puja, He completed the Udvaasana ritual of bidding farewell to the Devatas invoked on the previous day. Sri Swamiji then offered Maha Purnahuti for the Chandi Homa and blessed the devotees with Prokshana. 

During today’s Navavarana Puja, Devi was worshipped as Shakti Durgi with coconuts and Dadhyanna (Curd rice) was offered as Annarchana.

Pujya Sri Datta Vijayananda Teertha Swamiji spoke about how for eleven days Sri  Dattaji has blessed devotees to witness this 60th Navaratri festival. Heretics Wanted!

We're looking for a technical co-founder to take on Google, IBM and Quantinuum directly.

We have one goal: build the whole quantum computer from scratch, like Jobs and Wozniak did for the Apple I and the Apple II.

Quantinuum's recent 98-qubit machine cited 186 unique authors. We are trying to do it with three.

I'll go first. I'm not from a quantum hardware background. What I have done is build the full system blueprint end to end down to the CAD, the coax and the fibre attach, and published the design online. The parts list is public: a researcher we work with puts all-in hardware at about $100k, spares included. That's what a small quantum computer BOM looks like, and nobody in this field will show you theirs.

It is our conviction that the mystique around the word 'quantum' has led to the usual business questions around component prices and supply chains being ignored. It is in these boring and unscientific questions that we will seek our edge.

A recent example of the method, from a researcher we work with: knocking roughly $300k off the prototype by deleting the requirement that it run at -200°C. We moved the computation and photonics on-chip, which allowed us to use off-the-shelf triple Peltiers to get to around -74°C. That's cold enough to run the circuits we need, and they cost less than $250.

The goal at Pathfinder Quantum Technologies is to build the world's leading quantum computers by solving the scaling problem. Our first machine is a small, low-qubit prototype we intend to sell at a profit. It's a stepping stone, and the thing that gets us to the machines that beat the incumbents.

Where we are:

- The director of a Canadian university quantum research centre has written to say they want to buy the first machine once it's ready.

- The build is costed line by line: 57 lines with part numbers, suppliers and lead times.
[https://t.co/2n3iySIdi2]

- We're raising £500k, which covers the parts, the foundry work, the lab and three people for a three-month flat-out build. Designs go in for the next fab run in February 2027, and fab time isn't published.

Who I'm looking for:

You're hardware-first. 
You have built things with your hands, at a quantum company or a semiconductor one or somewhere adjacent where the physics had to survive contact with a fab line. The team needs someone who is, because I'm not.

You're a heretic engineer who can't stand design by committee. In six months we will have a lab stocked with cheap components and a tiny team trying scrappy, unorthodox ways to drive up gate fidelity and drive down costs.

You aren't married to a modality. The best design is the one that works, whether it comes from solid-state, trapped-ion, or something entirely novel.

You want to invent new physics. We don't just want to rebuild the systems that came before us.

The offer: 50% of Pathfinder. Co-founder and equal partner, building the whole computer with me. No salary until the £500k lands; I'm not paying myself before then either.

Where: UK - I'd move for the right person.

If that's you, my DMs are open. The first conversation is technical: I send you the blueprint and the bill of materials, and you tell me what you'd improve.

text:
Today, I was speaking with the local police and ATF about computer and email safety.    Stay safe online. 

Your online safety is mostly a matter of small, consistent habits — the everyday choices you make about what you share, what you click, and how you protect your accounts. None of it takes much time, and all of it makes you a much harder target.

Be thoughtful about what you share. Every post, review, quiz result, and profile update adds another piece to a picture that strangers — and scammers — can assemble. Details that feel harmless on their own (your pet's name, your street, your birthday, the school your kids attend) are the same details used to guess passwords or answer security questions. Before you post, ask what it says about you and who else might be reading it. Check your privacy settings and know who can see what.

Keep your software and devices up to date. Updates are not just new features — they close security holes that attackers already know how to use. Turn on automatic updates wherever you can, on your phone, laptop, tablet, and even your router and smart devices, so you aren't relying on remembering. If a device no longer receives updates, it's time to replace it.

Use unique passwords and change them regularly. Reusing one password means a single breach anywhere exposes every account you own — and attackers routinely try stolen logins across many sites. Give each account its own strong password, and use a password manager so you don't have to memorize them all. Wherever two-factor authentication is offered, turn it on; it's one of the strongest protections available. Rotate your important passwords periodically, and immediately if you hear about a breach.

Download the free Michigan Secure app. Michigan Secure alerts you to risky networks, suspicious links, and threats to your device, and it's available at no cost to Michigan residents. It's a simple step that adds a real layer of protection to everything above.

Safety online isn't about one big fix — it's a habit you build. A few minutes spent today makes you safer for a long time to come.

NBA OPENING NIGHT PROP #3

DEVIN VASSELL OVER 12.5 POINTS (+100 FAN DUEL)

THE NUMBER IS LOW. THE PRICE IS RIGHT.

We’re getting an even-money price on Devin Vassell to score 13+ points against Oklahoma City. The market is asking him to beat a modest scoring threshold, and the historical data gives us a case worth evaluating.

THE ADVANCED DATA

• 13.9 PPG across 67 regular-season games in 2025–26.
• 30.5 minutes per game, providing a consistent opportunity base.
• 53.4% of his points came from beyond the arc last season, making his perimeter shooting a major factor in his scoring profile.
• 50 of 91 games went over 12.5 points across the 2025–26 regular season and playoffs combined, according to OverCount.

That last number is a 55.0% hit rate. At +100, we need to win more than 50% of the time to show a profit before accounting for any practical execution issues.

WHY THE OVER IS INTERESTING

A REASONABLE SCORING THRESHOLD

Vassell averaged 13.9 points last season. Our line sits 1.4 points below that average, giving us some room for an ordinary scoring performance to cash.

THREE-POINT SCORING UPSIDE

More than half of his scoring came from three-point range last season. That creates a path to clearing 12.5 without needing a huge volume of free throws or an unusually high number of drives to the rim.

THE PRICE

FanDuel: +100
Novig: +100
ProphetX: -101

FanDuel and Novig offer the best listed prices. At +100, the break-even probability is 50%. At -101, it rises to approximately 50.25%.

Small differences add up over hundreds of tracked bets. Always shop the number.

THE MATCHUP FACTOR

San Antonio opens against Oklahoma City. This is not an automatic matchup upgrade: the Thunder have the defensive personnel to make perimeter scoring difficult. Vassell’s minutes, shot volume, and efficiency will be key variables.

But Trump did not, demonstrating the very “principle of zigzag” that Dmitry Simes said so accurately.

And in this wobble — a step towards Zelensky, a step from Zelensky — Trump and frozen.

On the other hand, Zelensky himself, the American Democrats, the leaders of the European Union and the United Kingdom. Together, they form a single pole of rigid, radical Russophobia, obsessed with the idea of Russia's strategic defeat.

Even at our current pace, even our current pace is not yet enough for a lightning, crushing victory, the transfer of conflict from war to crushing in a protracted war of attrition seems to them a winning card.

Russia advocates a multipolar world, the sovereignty of civilization states and for traditional values;
Western globalists and liberals are exactly the opposite – for a total unipolar world under the control of the West, for anti-traditional destructive values and for the destruction of any national sovereignty.

Therefore, they have fundamental claims to Russia. They see the Ukrainian conflict as an ideal tool to weaken, sharpen from within, and ideally, break and destroy our state.

Zelensky in this scheme is only a noricious performer. If the whole West had unanimously told him to leave, he would have evaporated the same day. But when the resignation is demanded by Trump alone, Zelensky boldly ignores it – because the U.S. democratic clans behind his back whisper to him: “Don’t listen to Trump, he will soon be done.”

We should not fall into illusions, overestimate the figures of American politics or have inflated hopes from contacts with Trump's team. If the U.S. Congress comes under the control of the Democrats, the first to deal with a crushing legal and political blow will be the Trump special envoys like Steve Witkoff or Jared Kushner. They will instantly be asked, “Who are you and on what grounds interfere with great geopolitics?”

In order to build an adequate and rational strategy, it is time for us to realize the main challenge. We need to set ourselves the task of inflicting a strategic defeat on the West.

In the meantime, our official rhetoric sounds strictly the opposite: we constantly emphasize that we are not going to attack Europe, do not seek to escalate the conflict and do not want a direct war with NATO. From a diplomatic point of view, this is understandable. But the enemy openly set itself the goal of destroying us. If you came to kill, and you answer only justify: “I do not plan to kill you” – to whom is this position? This is a deeply asymmetrical and dangerous subtext. We are destroyed quite seriously.

By the way, it was these fundamental questions that we dealt in detail on the air with Dmitry Simes, together with Dmitry Trenin and Andrew Napolitano. Napolitano is a former influential American judge, a former close associate of Trump, who reviewed his views, a very deep analyst. And Dmitry Simes himself is one of the deepest connoisseurs and former participants of the US expert-analytical olympus.

And here is what conclusion we came to? – We are not free to choose: escalation or not escalation.Because in the West there are extremely influential, practically key forces that increase the level of this escalation . And we are still following them and only reacting.

Why don't we really get involved in this process? If we play an active role in this escalation, not a passive one — an active offensive rather than passive defensive — we can begin to manage this process.

And increasing escalation on our part will paradoxically lead to its reduction. Because when we, from their point of view, respond sluggishly and uncertainly, they see this as an exceptional weakness. And raise the degree further. We're fighting back. But if we were to go on right now...

Here who knows - everything is in the hands of our leadership: as the President decides, and will be. If everything remains, Russia should join the process of escalation and thus make it manageable on both sides.

When I reminded him that classical democracy was the power of the majority, he explicitly replied, “This was the case before. And today we have democracy – it is the power of minorities against the majority. I was surprised, “This is something new!” And he says, “Yes, because most can choose Putin or another strong leader, so most people can’t be trusted anymore. The majority must be controlled, retrained, and even better, put under the tight control of minorities.

What do you think about this?

Man has a unique gift that distinguishes him from all other species – thinking. And the fact that humanity is trying to reproduce this intelligence technologically, to become a “demiurge” and a “creator” of a new mind, contains something deeply luciferal. Yes, he can hallucinate and make mistakes, but the very structure of large language models (📷) allowed him to operate on thought as a language – flexibly and organically, not just as a dry formal logic. But now we are talking about the next stage – the moment of technological singularity, when artificial intelligence will begin to make decisions for humanity itself. While we still remain within this decision-making circuit, we are rapidly approaching the point when the management passes to it.

In the military sphere, this is manifested with the greatest obviousness: a person is already physically unable to cope with the speeds of modern combat systems and data flows.
