text:
France imposes curfews in cities after weekend of protests

French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities on Monday, including Paris, Lille and Nice, as they faced pressure over security failings after a weekend of riots and looting stemming ​from nationwide anti-government protests.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu had ruled out a blanket curfew in Paris but not a state of emergency, and had said it was more appropriate for now to ‌apply partial and localized curfews.

"My determination to restore order is absolute," he told reporters.

Paris police said they had issued orders barring protests in certain areas of the French capital from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) and had issued a curfew around the Place de la Republique and Les Halles from 11 p.m. Both would remain in effect until 6 a.m. on Tuesday.

"A police deployment is in place to ensure strict compliance with these measures," the police said in a statement.

A source in Lecornu's office said a curfew for minors had been set between ​8 p.m. and 6 a.m. for the next two days in Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain with the agreement of the local mayors.

In Nice, Mayor Eric Ciotti said in a video posted online that he had signed an order imposing a curfew for minors in central Nice overnight.

Marseille banned gatherings and demonstrations. French unions meanwhile called for a new round of strikes and rallies on ⁠November 5.

The weekend of looting and violence between some protesters and police followed weeks of student demonstrations, rocking France six months ahead of its next presidential election and highlighting pressures from a weak economy and surging debt.

Macron rejects minister's resignation amid security, market concerns

Nationwide, more than 2,513 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. He added that 67 had been jailed and "dozens" of criminal cases opened.

After the weekend scenes of chaos, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered his resignation.

But President Emmanuel Macron's office said on Monday he had turned down the offer, telling Nunez instead to put an end to barricades and looting and be transparent over what Macron called "intelligence and foresight failings".

France deployed 60,000 police and other security forces on Saturday, ⁠Nunez told France ​Inter radio, but he acknowledged that was not enough to control violent crowds.

French assets were underperforming broader European markets on Monday, though moves were more contained than at some other moments of recent political friction.

Tensions in Macron's government over apparent security shortcomings – coming as the government needs to pass a budget bill to rein in its finances – could further unsettle investors.

Nunez told reporters that Tuesday evening's Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona would go ahead as planned.

Looting leaves people injured, businesses affected

More than 2,500 people were arrested and nearly 1,000 members of the security forces injured. Protesters were also hurt, with one demonstrator's hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according ⁠to the Interior Ministry.

Lecornu ​blamed far-left groups for some of France's worst unrest in years. "There is, after all, a far-left movement that wants to cause – we can’t put it any more strongly – profound unrest in the country in the run-up to the ​presidential election," he said.

Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon urged him to provide evidence. "Otherwise, he should apologize, keep quiet and stop fanning the flames of unrest," he said on X.

The Federation of Trade and Retail said almost 3,000 shops had been affected over the weekend, as hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest over what many say are declining and dysfunctional public services.

"Behind every ransacked shop are business owners, employees and families who have seen years of work and effort wiped out in a matter of hours," it added, calling for social security and tax relief for affected businesses.

At the Place Vendome in Paris, home to luxury hotels and boutiques, most shops were shuttered and surrounded by security guards on Monday. The front door of a Dior boutique was smashed, while windows belonging to other luxury brands' stores in central Paris, including Rolex, Louis Vuitton, Ralph Lauren and Gucci, were damaged.

In Marseille, Ligue 1 club Olympique de Marseille said its official store on the city's historic main avenue had been looted, while a town hall in central France was torched.

Lecornu said the government would provide furlough measures ​from Tuesday.

The government ordered platforms selling looted goods to take down listings and collaborate to prosecute resellers, Junior Digital Minister Anne Le Hénanff wrote on X.

Cost-of-living issues also drove weekend protests in other European countries including Italy, Belgium ​and Albania.

European governments have advised citizens traveling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution.

As France was busy cleaning up its streets, Macron arrived in Kuwait for a Gulf trip aimed at securing additional petrol and diesel supplies to bring down pump prices.

text:
Trump administration holds back another $1.2 billion in California Medicaid funds 

The Trump administration is deferring an additional $1.2 billion in Medicaid reimbursements to California over concerns about potential fraud in a state program that helps older adults and people with disabilities with everyday tasks, the Los Angeles Times reported. Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, said state officials were notified Tuesday.

“California has been growing that program 24% in the last three years. That is twice the rate of every other state average in the country,” Oz said. Oz did not provide any evidence of fraud but suggested the state was paying people too much taxpayer money to help with services that could be offered for free.

In May, the administration withheld $1.3 billion in federal Medicaid reimbursements to the state over concerns about “fraudsters” in its hospice and in-home care programs. Gov. Gavin Newsom’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but previously called that action “sick” and politically motivated.

text:
THE @Minikothe3rd's LONG ESSAY: CAMPAIGN IN THE GUISE OF PERSONAL OPINION
  - By: 𝐀 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐂𝐄𝐑𝐄𝐍𝐄𝐃 𝐂𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐙𝐄𝐍

1/4

I took time to read everything in your long tweet. You have taken so much time and effort to explain your decision to supporting this government, but you failed in providing substantial, reasonable and convincing arguments on why others should.

I don't think we've ever crossed path. But as someone affected by the actions and inactions of whom you are supporting, and because your long tweet sounds somehow misleading, I will respond to all your points one after the other, and I will try not to be verbose as you were.

RE: THE DEVIL YOU KNOW IS BETTER THAN THE DEVIL YOU DON'T KNOW:

That's not true. All the three candidates that you narrowed your discussion to, have same basic records you can access in public domain; Atiku was a V.P for 8 years, Peter Obi was a governor for 8 years too, the same way Tinubu was also a governor for 8 years.

Before Tinubu assumed power as the president in 2023, nobody knew who exactly amongst the same 3 candidates would do better selflessly. Tinubu was pronounced as the winner even though it was argued that he was not the people's choice. But, let's take it as it is; Tinubu won in 2023. So, if people are not satisfied, they should go ahead and change him with another candidate they feel can do well.

You clamed that the remaining 2 candidates have no record of managing federal machinery, that's the same way Tinubu was in 2023, yet he got to be the president, and people are obviously not satisfied with his way of managing the country. So, let people continue to try others until we get it right in sha Allah. But allowing a person to serve two tenures of continuous hardship and hopelessness, just because he's the one that has held the highest position amongst the other candidates is a political su!c!de

RE: PETER OBI: GOOD INTENTIONS ARE NOT ENOUGH:

You said running a state and running Nigeria as a whole is complete different undertakings. Yes, I agree. But as I said, before 2023, Tinubu has never run anything beyond a state too, yet he was elected to run Nigeria despite his zero prior experience. And, Atiku Abubakar had more experience in this regard than him. Because he was a V.P for 8 years. Yet, he was chosen over Atiku. Therefore, now that people are not satisfied, let them try another person even if he has not run a federal level position.

RE: ATIKU ABUBAKAR: EXPERIENCE IS IMPORTANT, BUT SO IS TRUST:

You acknowledged Atiku's political experience, but do not have trust on him. Let me tell you, the way you do not trust Atiku's judgement is the same way others do not trust your candidate's. Whatever examples you have against Atiku or any of the other candidates, record has its equivalent or even bigger one on your candidate.

Let me give you just one: Since the return of democracy in 1999, Tinubu has been the one ruling Lagos state whether directly or indirectly. He left office since 2007, but since then, anyone that was a governor of Lagos was selected by him. Is there anything that's worse than this? This is 21st century for God sake, and this is democracy. Why not allow people to choose whom they want to rule them? Why turning a whole state's politics into personal possession, that it's whom you want that get to rule and whom you don't want, even if he's the choice of the peole, would not get to rule?

Furthermore, there's nothing wrong in a person running for a position multiple times, if he feels that he has something to offer. Late president Muhammadu Buhari has been running for president since 2003, and you dare not accuse Buhari's good intention and integrity just because he had been contesting for the position for years. He had his flaws and failures in some areas, but you dare not question his integrity and sincerity, especially as at then when he was in the battle. So, multiple seek to be elected into a position does not translate into insincerity.

text:
WHY I SUPPORT TINUBU, IN VERY SIMPLE TERMS. I BELIEVE IT SHOULD BE MORE THAN ENOUGH REASON FOR YOU TOO. 🇳🇬

A THREAD 🧵 

I agree, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not perfect.

I agree, the standard of living has deteriorated under his administration, and millions of Nigerians are struggling to make ends meet.

I agree, insecurity remains a serious menace, threatening lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country.

I agree, inflation has eroded purchasing power, making food, transportation, housing, and other basic necessities increasingly unaffordable.

I agree, the removal of fuel subsidy, though economically justifiable in principle, came with enormous immediate consequences for ordinary Nigerians.

I agree, the naira has lost significant value, and exchange-rate instability has placed additional pressure on businesses and households.

I agree, unemployment and underemployment remain serious problems, particularly among our young people.

I agree, the government has not done enough to cushion the effects of its reforms on the most vulnerable citizens.

I agree, the pace of improvement in electricity supply remains disappointing, despite the country’s enormous energy needs.

I agree, Nigerians have every right to demand better governance, greater accountability, improved security, and tangible results.

I agree, promises are not achievements, and no administration should be praised merely for announcing policies.

But to conclude from all these challenges that President Tinubu has done absolutely nothing is either a failure to examine the facts or a deliberate refusal to acknowledge them.

Let us be honest enough to separate criticism from denial.

SO, WHAT HAS TINUBU ACTUALLY DONE?

I don’t want to bore you, so let’s save that for the end of the thread.

NOW, LET US TALK ABOUT THE 2027 ELECTION.

This is an election season. Nigerians must decide whether to give the incumbent another four years or entrust the country to an alternative candidate.

For me, the serious debate revolves around three names: Tinubu, Atiku, and Obi. Other candidates have every right to contest, but these are the three I consider most relevant to this argument.

So, who would I choose?

Tinubu. Ten times over.

Wallahi, Tallahi, I have my reasons. Let me explain a few of them.

1. THE DEVIL I KNOW IS BETTER THAN THE DEVIL I DO NOT KNOW.

I know Tinubu’s political history. I know his strengths, his weaknesses, his methods, and some of the people and interests surrounding him. I can assess his record, criticise his failures, and demand that he improve on what he has started.

With a new president, particularly one without a comparable record of managing Nigeria’s federal executive machinery, we would be taking a different kind of risk.

This is not an argument that Tinubu is automatically the best candidate because he is already in office. Incumbency is not a qualification in itself. My argument is that, in a country facing deep institutional and economic challenges, continuity can be valuable when there is a credible case for the direction of travel.

And I believe there is such a case with Tinubu.

2. PETER OBI: GOOD INTENTIONS ARE NOT ENOUGH.

I do not have to believe Peter Obi is a bad person to question whether he is the right person for the presidency.

Running a state and running Nigeria are fundamentally different undertakings. Nigeria is a complex federation with competing regional interests, a vast security apparatus, entrenched institutional weaknesses, a complicated political structure, and an economy exposed to global shocks.

The presidency requires more than fiscal discipline, sound public speaking, or a reputation for personal frugality. It requires the ability to build coalitions, manage competing interests, negotiate with powerful stakeholders, make unpopular decisions, withstand political pressure, and maintain the capacity to govern when the opposition is relentless…

text:
A statement from Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston in response to questions about the proposed Point Tupper data centre. Shared by Brian Wong, MLA for Waverley, Fall River, Beaver Bank on Facebook:

"We accept and expect that Nova Scotians have questions and concerns about a data centre. This is a new industry to Nova Scotia and it is normal to have questions. It is our responsibility to provide facts, and we will do the work to keep Nova Scotians informed. This is a first of its kind proposal on a data centre and there will be many checks and balances built into the process. 

There are checks and balances being monitored by the federal government, the provincial government and also the local municipal government. 

The company has been very upfront with all levels of government.  They also took an extremely transparent step of offering opposition MLAs a full technical briefing in advance of their announcement.  Some opposition MLAs accepted the offer and did receive a full technical briefing.  Others made an intentional decision not to receive a technical briefing.  They can individually explain their decision on this but to see elected officials spreading misinformation at this point is unfair to Nova Scotians and harmful. 
A few facts are important to level the discussion. 

The federal Liberal government has established guidelines for data centers.  So have I.  This is not a partisan issue. This project is going through a process to ensure that it meets these standards.  

This is not public, taxpayer money. It is private money and it is the single largest private sector investment in Nova Scotia’s history, more than $10 billion. This private investment is welcomed by all levels of government and Indigenous partners.  

Everwind will be building 80 turbines and generate more than 650 MW of clean electricity through new wind farms. The data centre will be built in phases, with the first being 95 MW and will be fully disruptable. That means that if the Nova Scotia power energy grid encounters any situation where it is reaching capacity, the power to the Datacenter will be shut down long before there is any impact on any household. 

In terms of water usage, the facility is being designed with a closed-loop cooling system that recirculates water and makes extensive use of air cooling, thanks to Nova Scotia's climate. For perspective, the water usage would be less water than a traditional fish plant. Even at full capacity, water usage will represent approximately 5% of the water currently withdrawn, on average, from the existing Point Tupper industrial water system.  We will monitor this but as planned the impact is minimal. 

Nova Scotia Environment and Climate Change will work closely with Everwind to ensure rules under the Environment Act are met and followed.

The bottom line is that there is a process in place. The Department has a range of approvals and regulations to regulate industry on a case-by-case basis depending on the circumstances of each situation. They are stringent and serious and they will be followed. Regulatory decisions are made based using sound technical expertise and evidence, science and facts.

In terms of the misinformation that is being spread that your household power rate will go up, that is completely false. I have been very clear: protecting Nova Scotia ratepayers is an outright condition of our government's support.   In fact, there are scenarios where adding a new customer can actually decrease rates.  This will be built into any agreement that the company enters into with N.S. Power and the NSEB will have to approve these rates. I have been clear on our position. 

There will always be those who will take every opportunity to oppose economic development in Nova Scotia. That is too often the very first reaction of some and that’s ok. We accept that. But it’s not realistic to protest budget reductions and protest economic development. The simple reality is that in order to be able to continue to invest in healthcare, homes, and roads, we can either grow our economy or raise taxes. While the NDP would prefer to raise your taxes our government will support opportunities that can meet world-class environmental safeguards to grow our economy."

text:
Javonte Green did not play a single minute of the first half today.

The Detroit Pistons were down 22 points to the Boston Celtics in the opening game of the season. Green sat and watched all of it.

Then he came in and scored 17 points in the second half, on 5 of 8 from three, and Detroit won 121 to 113.

Here is why a man waiting two quarters is funny.

Javonte Green came out of high school with exactly one Division I scholarship offer. Radford. That was the entire list. He also had a football scholarship offer from James Madison, because he played quarterback too, and at Brunswick High School in Lawrenceville, Virginia he was good enough at both that the choice was real.

His high school coach was Bryant Stith, the 13th pick of the 1992 draft, who played ten years in the NBA and eight of them with the Denver Nuggets. At least one man in that gym knew exactly how far away the thing was.

Green went to Radford University and left as the leading rebounder in school history. 1,064 rebounds. 245 steals. 133 games. Second all time in scoring at 1,911 points. There is not much more a player can do at a school nobody is scouting.

He went undrafted in 2015.

Then came the part that ends most of these stories. A season in Spain. Two years in Italy, at Trieste. A year in Germany, with Ulm. Three countries, four years, playing well enough to keep getting hired and never well enough to get the call he wanted.

On July 25, 2019, the Boston Celtics signed him. He was 26. He won the last roster spot in camp over a player named Max Strus, who went on to a long NBA career of his own.

What Green said that day was this. "My dream has come true. The tears you see are tears of joy."

Since then it has been the unglamorous version of making it. The Boston Celtics. The Chicago Bulls. A year in the G League when the calls stopped. The New Orleans Pelicans. The Cleveland Cavaliers. And now the Detroit Pistons, where he re-signed in July on a one year veteran minimum.

He is 33 years old. Today he sat through two full quarters before anybody called his name.

The honest counterpoint. Seventeen points off the bench in October is one good night, not a turn in the road. Green has never been a star, he is on a minimum deal, and he has been waived, traded and sent down. Nobody is building anything around him.

But a kid with one offer spent four years in Europe waiting for somebody to say yes.

Today he waited two more quarters, and then he went and took the game.

If you love basketball stories like these, follow us on any platform @ontaphoops

text:
Not one Division I program offered Javonte Green a basketball scholarship.

The only scholarship anybody ever put in front of him was to play quarterback.

Tonight, at 33 years old, he made five threes on opening night and Detroit came back from 22 down to beat Boston.

Here is the whole thing.

He moved in with his aunt and uncle when he was twelve, and went across the state of Virginia to a high school in a town called Lawrenceville.

He played there with a fracture in his back.

They managed it two weeks on and two weeks off. Before his senior year his doctors and his coach told him to shut it down and do physical therapy instead.

He played all three seasons.

Here is how he described it.

"Every time I did something, my back used to tighten up."

He never played AAU. Nobody was watching him. In the fall he played quarterback, and he was good enough at it that James Madison offered him a scholarship to come and do that.

In the sport he actually wanted, he had nothing.

His high school coach was Bryant Stith, who had played in the NBA himself. Here is how Stith remembers the kid in the middle of that.

"He was confused because so many people were pulling him in so many different directions."

So Stith told him this.

"Whatever you decide to do, you're going to be successful."

Then he did something about it. He sent Green's highlight tape out to college programs himself, and he put a handwritten note in with it.

Radford got one of them. The head coach there said later it was the note that got Green onto the list at all.

He committed to Radford on the last possible day he could still make it to campus.

CelticsBlog is where that whole chain is written down, from the back to the tape to the note.

Nobody drafted him. He spent four years overseas, in Spain and Italy and Germany, before anybody in this league would look at him. He made his NBA debut at twenty six years old.

Then after two seasons in Boston and two in Chicago, he was sent back down to the G League at thirty. He had already played two hundred games in the NBA by then.

He worked his way back up again.

Now go back to tonight.

Boston led by 22 points. Green went five for eight from behind the line, scored 19.

The only scholarship anyone ever offered him was in a different sport.

A high school coach wrote a note out by hand and put it in an envelope with a tape.

And eleven years after nobody drafted him, he was the best plus minus on the floor on opening night.

text:
Virginia regulators just got their first real look at the $67B Dominion–NextEra merger, and the deal as filed isn't getting through.

In testimony filed Monday at the SCC:
• Commission staff said the petition fails the Utility Transfers Act and recommended rejecting it unless the companies accept 57 conditions, including ring-fencing Dominion Virginia in a bankruptcy-remote entity and keeping NextEra's transmission arm out of future lines in Dominion's Virginia territory
• Gov. Spanberger wants a six-year residential base-rate freeze, $29 a month in bill credits for four years (the companies offered $10), and Dominion's debt share raised from 48% to 60% to cut its return
• She also wants a separate Virginia-based zero-carbon generation company to serve large data centers, financially walled off from other customers

The companies sold this as the cheaper way to build the grid Northern Virginia's data centers need. The governor's version would put data center generation on its own balance sheet.

The evidentiary hearing starts Nov 17, and the SCC has to rule by Jan 11.

text:
My people originated in Germany, then moved to Russia when Queen Catherine offered them free land in the Volga region of Russia. After the Queen died, many of the freedoms she had granted them were quickly suspended. Bands of Russian men came in the middle o the night and conscripted German men and boys into the Russian army. Land was seized and the language changed to Russian. 

It didn't take long for the Germans to come to America. They brought with them hand-picked Hard Red Winter Wheat. (Legend has it that the women spent many evenings going through the wheat picking out only the best wheat berries to carry to America.)

The wheat and the people did well for years in America. They originally settled in the upper mid-west, but eventually moved down to Oklahoma and Kansas.

When I was young, we went to the country church our farmers had built. The sermons were preached in German and hymns were sung in German. I still have my great-grandfather's German/English Bible (German on one side and English on the other.) Both my parents spoke German at home and at church. Mom said the pastor preached nearly 2 hours at their August wedding. The guests endured the summer afternoon heat without complaint listening to the preacher.

As you travel, you may see "Germans-from-Russia" plaques and town halls. Those were/are my people. In fact, I am working on a Germans-from-Russia cookbook.

A COUNCIL OF MANU'A ISLANDS CHIEFS AND TWO COMMUNITY GROUPS SUED YESTERDAY TO BLOCK THE FIRST U.S. DEEP-SEA MINING LEASE SALE, OFF AMERICAN SAMOA.

who sued. Faleula o le Manu'atele, a council of matai, or chiefs, joined Fa'asao Amerika Samoa and the Conservation Council for Hawai'i, represented by Earthjustice. they say the agency running the sale lacks authority under treaty requirements, that the law it's using doesn't allow mineral leasing in U.S. territories, and that it skipped environmental review.

"Deep sea mining threatens the lands and waters we have stewarded, and the federal government does not have authority to sell these leases in American Samoa," said Dr. Malouamaua "Malo" Tuiolosega of the chiefs' council.

THE CHIEFS SAY THE GOVERNMENT HAS NO LEGAL OR TREATY AUTHORITY TO SELL THESE LEASES AND SKIPPED ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW.

the government's side. the Marine Minerals Administration published its final notice the same day and set the auction for Nov. 19, with two areas on offer. "Critical minerals are no longer just commodities; they are a vital strategic asset in global competition," said acting director Mike Olsen, who said the agency is guided by "science, environmental review, and meaningful engagement" with American Samoa.

A LEASE ONLY ALLOWS MAPPING AT FIRST, AND MORE APPROVALS WOULD BE NEEDED BEFORE ANY COMPANY COULD ACTUALLY MINE.

who's cashing in. the whole process started after a formal request from U.S. company Impossible Metals in April 2025. no bidders have been named yet for November. my questions: who's lining up to bid, and who gets the minerals while the islanders keep the risk? to be fair, the government frames this as national security and supply chains. but when a company asks for a sale and the government says yes, follow the money down to the seafloor, dude. heavy stakes for the islands.

The Goddess of Freemasonry-'The Widow'
Pagan religions of ancient times had no god without a goddess. If as we have seen Masonry is a modern 'caricature' of the ancient Barbelonian and Egyptian rites, then we should expect to find a goddess in Masonry.

He intimates that Isis is the holder of the sacred name of Ra, the "ineffable name" of the god of Masonry (Abaddon, Apollyon, or Jahbulon).
Who as Isis? Isis was the Venus of Cyprus, the Minerva of Athens, the Cybele of the Phrygians, the Ceres of Eleusis, the Proserpine of Sicily, the Diana of Crete, the Bellona of the Romans, etc. And like the worshippers of Isis, Freemasons in their ceremonies and initiations perform "the most abominable impurities," and those "initiated into them" are obliged to take an oath of secrecy."

The conclusion of the matter? In establishing their Republic, the Americans could still not escape the ideal of a parallel monarchy — a central focus of non-political, patriotic attachment. George Washington was actually offered kingship, but declined because he had no immediately qualifying heritage. Instead he turned to the Royal House of Stuart. In November 1782 four Americans arrived at the San Clemente Palazzo in Florence, the residence of Charles III Stuart in exile. They were Mr Galloway of Maryland, two brothers named Sylvester from Pennsylvania, and Mr Fish, a lawyer from New York. They were taken to Charles Edward by his secretary, John Stewart. Also present was the Hon Charles Hervey-Townshend (later Britain’s ambassador to The Hague) and the Prince's future wife, Marguerite, Comtesse de Massillan. The interview — which revolved around the contemporary transatlantic dilemma — is doctimented in the US Senate archives and in the Manorwater Papers. Writers such as Sir Compton Mackenzie and Sir Charles Petrie have also described the occasion when Charles Edward Stuart was invited to become ‘King of the Americans’. Some years earlier, Charles had been similarly approached by the men of Boston, but once the War of Independence was over George Washington sent his own envoys. It would have been a great irony for the House of Hanover to lose the North American colonies to the Stuarts. But Charles declined the offer for a number of reasons, not the least of which was his lack of a legitimate male heir at the time. History
James V added to the palace between 1528 and 1536, beginning with the present James V's Tower, which is the oldest surviving part of the palace.[8] This huge rectangular tower, rounded at the corners, provided new royal lodgings at the north-west corner of the palace. Originally equipped with a drawbridge leading to the main entrance (protected with a yett) on the first floor, it may also have been protected by a moat, and provided a high degree of security. The south range was remodelled, and the old queen's apartments were converted into a new chapel, and the former chapel in the north range was converted into the Council Chamber, where ceremonial events normally took place.[3] James IV's west range was demolished and a new west range in the Renaissance style was built to house new state rooms, including the royal library.[9][10] The symmetrical composition of the west range suggested that a second tower at the south-west was planned, though this was never executed at the time.[11] Around a series of lesser courts were ranged the Governor's Tower, the armoury, the mint, a forge, kitchens, and other service quarters.[11] James V's first wife, Madeleine of Valois, died at Holyrood in 1537.[12]

Saint FRANCIS XAVIER (born Francisco de Jasso y Azpilicueta; April 7, 1506 – December 3, 1552) was a Navarrese Roman Catholic missionary who co-founded the Society of Jesus (Jesuits) alongside Ignatius of Loyola.

On 30 January 1788 the de jure King Charles II (fondly remembered as Bonnie Prince Charlie) died, aged 67, at the Mutti Palazzo in Rome. Shortly before his death he wrote his Last Will and Testament. This was witnessed on 13 January 1788 by the Dominican Father O'Kelly and the Abbé Consalvi, both of whom were executors. The Will stated that Charles's offspring, Edward James and Charlotte, were to be co-heirs of the estate; his son Edward was to succeed to the Royal Honours on his 16th birthday, and Cardinal Henry was to be temporary Regent in the meantime.
Following Charles Edward's demise, his ambitious brother Henry wasted no time in proclaiming himself King Henry I de jure of Scots (IX of England). To support this claim he produced not Charles’s Will of 1788 but his earlier Will of 1784 — which suited Britain’s Government since the Cardinal was not likely to have any children. Both O’Kelly and Consalvi were party to the intrigue in return for rapid promotion within the Church. Soon afterwards, the former became Dominican Procurator, while the Abbé was raised to the Cardinalate. Charlotte of Albany was provided with a home in Frascati, and the Mutti Palazzo was retained for Marguerite de Massillan and Prince Edward. Also involved in the scheme was the Abbé James Placid Waters, Procurator of the Benedictines in Rome.
By declaring himself King de jure, Henry sought to nullify the immediate Regency clause in his brother’s Will. But in January 1789 Henry made his own Will in which he redressed his selfish strategy for the future: all his possessions and heritable status were bequeathed to Prince Edward James — that is, ‘to my nephew, Count Stuarton’. Both Cardinal Ercole Consalvi and Cardinal Angelo Cesarini were privy to the Will and were executors, as attested in their memoirs.
As it happened, Henry subsequently lost a great deal of his wealth in the French Revolution and during the Napoleonic advance into the Papal States. In 1799 he became a pensioner of the British Crown at the rate of £5,000 per annum (about £250,000 in today’s terms) - but in return he was required to rewrite his Will. Maryland Man Convicted of $18.7M Medicare Fraud for Respiratory Testing Scheme Targeting Nursing Homes https://t.co/fwPhlbwto0 According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Patrick Britton-Harr, 42, of Annapolis, offered COVID-19 tests to nursing homes across the country in 2020 when these facilities were desperate for COVID-19 testing services. After specimens were collected from nursing home residents and other laboratories performed COVID-19 testing, Britton-Harr billed Medicare for separate, high-priced respiratory pathogen panel (RPP) tests purportedly conducted in a laboratory he owned in Arizona. Britton-Harr falsely claimed to Medicare that treating physicians ordered these extensive RPP tests, which screened for more than 30 respiratory pathogens. In reality, physicians never ordered the tests for their nursing home patients, and several physicians testified at trial they had never ordered an RPP test for any patient during the entirety of their medical careers.

Through his company, Provista Health, Britton-Harr fraudulently billed Medicare $18.7 million for RPP testing purportedly performed in just six months, of which Medicare paid more than $7.2 million. Evidence at trial demonstrated how Britton-Harr exploited inexperienced employees, including a family member and high school and college aged interns, by directing them to bill Medicare for an RPP test every time a COVID-19 test was performed. Britton-Harr further directed the billing of RPP tests supposedly performed at his Arizona laboratory after he had already closed the laboratory, barred staff from working in the laboratory, and no longer had the equipment necessary to run RPP tests. Additional evidence at trial proved that Britton-Harr billed Medicare for RPP tests that were never performed, including billing for tests for nursing home residents who were already deceased.

text:
🏠 What are your thoughts on the New Maryland Rental Laws

A new Maryland law called the Fair Chance Housing Act went into effect on October 1, 2026. It changes how some landlords can look at a renter's criminal history when they apply for housing.

The law applies to landlords who own or manage five or more rental units in Maryland. It does not apply to owner-occupied rentals or landlords who do not run background checks.

Here is what the law does:
✅ Landlords cannot require drug or alcohol testing.
✅ Landlords can only ask about certain criminal convictions before making a conditional offer.
✅ Landlords cannot run a criminal background check until after a conditional offer is made.
✅ If an offer is pulled because of criminal history, the landlord must give the reason, and the applicant can ask for a second review and share more information.
✅ Landlords cannot advertise that they will not rent to people with criminal records.
✅ Violations can bring penalties of up to $500 each.

We want to hear from you. Do you think this new law is fair to both renters and landlords? Tell us what you think in the comments.

text:
Monday, October 19, 2026: 

21 Minutes of Hell to Schedule a Post-Surgery Wheelchair Delivery

I called @ApriaHealthcare to return their voicemail and schedule delivery of a wheelchair after back surgery. What followed was one of the most absurd, inefficient, and patient-hostile customer service experiences I have ever endured.

The agent was clearly offshore (using voice-modulation software that added lag and an unnatural quality to every word) and locked into an aggressively scripted model that treated basic information exchange as an infinite loop. I stated my name, spelled my last name, gave my first name (Kimberly)—which she also needed spelled—provided my zip code, and clearly explained that I was returning Apria’s call to arrange home delivery of a wheelchair.

She then made me repeat nearly every piece of information multiple times while endlessly parroting back “I will be able to help you with this ma’am Kimberly. If I understand you correctly, you are calling today to ask about delivery of your wheelchair, ma’am Kimberly.” Over… and over… and over.

Zip code a minimum of four or five times. Full address multiple times. Confirmation of the purpose of the call literally dozens of times throughout the call. After she brought up my hospital discharge date (two days ago), which I confirmed, and finally got her to understand that I had already been discharged and was home, she still defaulted—again, multiple times—to asking me what time I wanted the wheelchair instead of telling me what delivery windows they actually had available.

When I explained that I live rurally, that I physically cannot come to the door post-surgery, and that my husband needs a real window so he can be present, she continued cycling through the same questions and restating the purpose for the call again… and again… and again.

I said, “My husband has errands to run relating to my surgery. So if YOU tell ME what delivery options are available, we can make sure he’s here.”

Again: “I beg your pardon, ma’am Kimberly. What time would you LIKE your wheelchair to be delivered…”

AGAIN! I repeated that we were home NOW, so could take delivery in ten minutes, or at 11 a.m., or 1 p.m., or 3 p.m., or ANY TIME today that they had available!

Eventually she offered 1 p.m. I asked for the size of the delivery window and whether we would get a call if the driver was running late. Answers were vague, contradictory, or nonexistent (“the driver will call you,” followed by silence when asked whether that meant “on the way” or “late”).

She then gave me a callback number that she had to repeat and correct multiple times before landing on 888-492-7742. When pressed on how to navigate the phone tree or what the realistic odds of an on-time delivery were, the response was more apologies and “I beg your pardon, ma’am Kimberly,” and, finally, “there are no guarantees.”

The agent herself remained polite and even offered the required scripted sympathy about the surgery, multiple times. That is not the problem. THE PROBLEM IS APRIA’S PROCESS. They have designed a workflow that forces agents to reconfirm the same basic facts repeatedly (to the point of nothing less than absurdity), prevents them from simply stating available delivery windows, and creates endless friction for a patient who is already recovering from surgery and trying to coordinate a simple home delivery.

The combination of offshore VOIP lag, voice modulation, and rigid scripting turned what should have been a three-minute scheduling call (max) into a miserable, 21-minute circular ordeal.

APRIA IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THIS. NOT the individual agent.

Companies that outsource customer service for cost savings still own the outcome of the scripts, training, and systems they impose. (Flying your person in charge of outsourcing out there to beat the outsourcer to death is NOT the answer. APRIA’S PROCESS needs to change. Whoever designed it needs to be held accountable, and if you paid a consultant to do it, or hired the same one that RUINED what USED to be great service from Byram Healthcare, fire them. This was beyond ridiculous.)

For a durable medical equipment provider dealing with people who have just had surgery and need equipment to function at home, this model is unacceptable. It wastes patients’ limited energy, creates unnecessary confusion around delivery logistics, and demonstrates a complete lack of respect for the people who actually need the product.

If Apria cannot design a straightforward process for returning a delivery-scheduling call, patients should not be forced to navigate this level of LUDICROUS DYSFUNCTION simply to receive a wheelchair.

I’ve yet to work with a provider who expresses anything less than disdain when they learn my insurance contracts through Apria—some going as far as saying, “They’re the worst.” Insurance companies and hospitals continue to contract with them anyway because of the deep discounts Apria offers. To deliver those discounts, Apria cuts corners at every cost point, and the biggest overhead is labor. I’m not opposed to offshoring for cost containment (in fact, I ran call centers internationally), but a simple cost-benefit analysis should ask whether paying an outsourcer for 21 minutes of exacting misery on a patient—on a call that could have been verified efficiently and effectively in three minutes—makes any sense once you factor in the patient and provider experience.

If someone at Apria with a shred of common sense looked at cost containment against an overlay of “how can we possibly make patients and providers hate us more,” perhaps Apria wouldn’t have to give away the farm just to remain the company people actively hate in the DME industry.

To Apria’s incoming CEO: I ENCOURAGE you to ask for (and listen to via) the dial-in codes which allow you to LIVE monitor random PATIENT (not provider) calls that you can log into, 24 x 7, with NO ONE (including your COO’s) knowledge (otherwise, your people AND your outsourcer is going to feed you cherry-picked calls taken by their best reps). YOU need to EXPERIENCE the patient—and your outsourced agent—experience. LISTEN to the scripting someone on your team has implemented, then let the heads roll.

This was a MASTERCLASS in how NOT to handle a simple post-surgery wheelchair delivery, and leadership at Apria who are responsible for this debacle needs to be held accountable for it. Fire the lot of them and bring in someone with a shred of common sense who has the leadership skills to PARTNER with your outsourcer instead of what I can all but guarantee is going to happen as a result of this letter: BLUDGEON THE OUTSOURCER.

This dead skunk doesn’t land on your outsourcer’s porch. The STINK of this debacle CLEARLY lands at the feet of leadership at Apria.

Shame on ALL of you and WAKE THE HELL UP!

cc. Perry Bernocchi, EVP COO Accendra Health Operational leader. @pbernocc (Were YOU the person responsible for destroying Byram’s once exceptional customer service?! Trustpilot ratings are down to around 1.2/5 based on reviews (although their site boasts of all kinds of awards and accolades), with recurring complaints about long hold times, unhelpful or hard-to-understand agents, rigid/scripted processes, incorrect information, delivery problems, and billing issues. There’s been a NOTICEABLE DECLINE in recent years, often linking it to outsourcing/offshoring and process changes. Were YOU responsible for that, as well?)

cc. Kenneth Gardner-Smith, Incoming President & CEO of Accendra Health

cc. Edward A. Pesicka, Outgoing President & CEO of Accendra Health

cc. Dan Starck, Former CEO of Apria

@ApriaHealthcare @AccendraHealth 
----------------

Update — 1 p.m.–2 p.m. window comes and goes: No call. No chair.

No call. I dialed the number the morning agent gave me (888-492-7742, option 6). After the VRU collected my date of birth and zip code, I reached an agent who sounded U.S.-based. No lag, no voice modulation, and almost none of the endless looping or forced apologies. She started with the usual “Let’s start with the patient’s date of birth,” caught herself, put me on a short hold, then asked again. I re-verified everything I’d already provided the VRU.

She immediately flagged a problem: the order had been set up to ship from the Sacramento branch (the county where the hospital is located). Sacramento does not deliver to my rural county. It should have been routed through a different branch in a different county that actually services my area. She said the driver would not be back in my area until tomorrow, so the 1 p.m. window was dead. My husband had already rearranged his day… for nothing.

She also confirmed the wheelchair being sent is larger than the one I currently have—the one that barely fits through the bathroom door. The morning agent had assured me the unit she was shipping would fit. It will not. The new agent had to rekey the entire order.

She further stated a credit card was required because this is a 10-month rental and I would be responsible for 10% “co-insurance.” I explained that both my individual and family out-of-pocket maximums were met earlier this year, so the item should be covered at 100%. She said she does not handle insurance and could not set up the delivery without a card on file. I gave her my HSA card so the delivery could proceed and told her I would deal with billing separately. She transferred me to billing (866-505-6365).

Which was… back to the outsourcer. ARGH!

After another long VRU and a hold, I reached an offshore agent and an immediate return to the script: constant apologies, full parroting of everything I had just said (repeatedly), and re-verification of name, date of birth, and address even though the system already had it.

After the second or third apology I said, “Looks like I’ve reached the outsourcer again. I’m calling about billing because I just discovered an issue when I reached out to inquire about why my wheelchair delivery still wasn’t here. An outsourced agent set the delivery up incorrectly and confirmed the wrong wheelchair, so I had to start all over. During that process I was told a credit card needs to be put on file despite the fact I’ve exceeded my maximum out-of-pocket for the year.”

Another apology and “Ma’am, may I ask what went wrong with your order?”

I asked her not to change anything on the order—the U.S.-based agent had just fixed the branch and size issues—and explained that the morning outsourcer had it shipping from the wrong county despite multiple confirmations of my discharge and home address.

More apologies (ad nauseam) and restatements of the purpose for my call (over and over) were issued. After a long hold she came back on and immediately read off a  a 12-digit number and asked if it was the right number. 

“Are you asking me to confirm if that’s my insurance information?” “Yes.” She said she verified insurance, removed the credit card / automatic payment, and said, “I’ve removed your HSA card from the file and rest assured, ma’am, we will not bill your credit card for anything unless we get your permission to bill you for it.” (As visions of the chair not being delivered tomorrow because there was no credit card on file floated through my brain.)

When I asked when I would be contacted if there is a problem, the answer was vague: their billing department will verify with the insurance, and if I owe any money then Apria will send a bill; the review team may need more information but she did not know when or if they would reach out.

Bottom line

The U.S.-based agent was competent and fixed the concrete errors created by the earlier outsourced call (wrong shipping branch, wrong wheelchair size, nonexistent delivery window, no promised call telling me they were on their way, no promised call telling me they were going to be late, no call at all to explain that Sacramento County doesn’t deliver to my county). That part of the experience was acceptable. The moment I was transferred back to the outsourced billing side, the circular scripting, forced apologies, and repeated re-verification returned in full force.

I still don’t have a confirmed delivery window for tomorrow (only “it will arrive sometime tomorrow after 9:30 a.m.,” but “you can call tomorrow sometime after 9 a.m. to ask when the delivery has been scheduled”). The correct wheelchair size is not guaranteed until the rekeyed order processes, and the credit-card / co-insurance issue remains unresolved pending some unspecified review.

This is the same process failure as this morning, only now compounded by errors the first outsourced agent introduced and a second outsourced agent who also couldn’t stop apologizing long enough to clearly resolve billing. The systems and scripts force agents into loops, prevent them from simply stating available options or correcting obvious errors on the first pass, and leave the patient to discover and fix the mistakes after the fact. Leadership at Apria owns every bit of that design.

Any bets on whether I’ll get my wheelchair tomorrow?

@apriacareers @ApriaHealthcare @AccendraHealth

Tuesday, October 20: Delivery arrives with 11 minutes’ notice

I was tied up this morning with calls from the surgeon’s office, insurance, and PT scheduling, so I didn’t call Apria for a delivery window.

At 11:53 a.m. the phone rang: “Coming to deliver your wheelchair. Are you home?” I said yes and asked what time. “I’ll be there in 11 minutes.”

We live rurally. My husband was working from home and wasn’t dressed to meet anyone, so he threw on clothes and met the driver. He also rolled out my old, broken-down wheelchair so we could confirm the size. Thankfully, it was the correct 18-inch chair (the one the U.S.-based rep rekeyed yesterday).

The driver was polite enough, but when he saw that the swing-away footrests weren’t attached to my old chair (I’d removed them because I use it to sit and vacuum and don’t need them in the way), he tried to keep them: “You don’t use the footrests? So you don’t want these?”

My husband said we wanted them.

text:
@ElonMaskSpaceX 

 Q3 2026: THE GUIDANCE, NOT THE BEAT, IS THE STORY

Len Watson, Portfolio Manager at Gryphon Investment Advisors Bahamas (GIAB)

20 October 2026

#SpaceX beat estimates on every major revenue and profit line in its second quarterly report as a public company. Expectations were elevated, and investors cared more about what Elon Musk and CFO Bret Johnsen would say on the call than about the Q3 figures. The call delivered: shares rose about 4.5% on Musk's revenue targets and extended to +5.5% once Johnsen gave guidance. Five points will decide how the stock trades from here.
1. Q1 2027 Revenue Guidance of $33–37bn Against a $23.4bn Consensus

Johnsen guided Q1 2027 revenue to $33–37bn, against an analyst estimate of $23.4bn. That is a 40–60% beat on the forward quarter, and the $35bn midpoint is 2.4 times Q3's $14.58bn, reached within two quarters. It implies a run rate of $11–12bn a month by early next year, against roughly $4.9bn a month in Q3.

Johnsen said SpaceX chose to guide this far out because it now has visibility into its compute contract pipeline over the next six months. The backlog supports that: of the $63bn at 30 September, about $42bn is expected to be recognised within a year.
Why it matters: Markets price forward earnings, and this is hard guidance from the CFO rather than a Musk aspiration. Every sell-side model now has to be rebuilt from Q1 2027 onward. It was also the clear trigger for the share move: the stock only extended its gain after the number was given. Delivery depends on compute coming online on schedule. SpaceX expects almost 2.2GW of nameplate compute by the end of October, up from 1.7GW at quarter-end, and 2.5–3GW by year-end.
2. SpaceX and Tesla Form Special Committees to Discuss a Merger

In answer to Edison Yu of Deutsche Bank, Musk confirmed that SpaceX and Tesla have each formed a special committee of independent directors to discuss a combination, at the request of shareholders. As a conflicted party, Musk cannot take part in their discussions. He said the committees have not agreed terms, that there is no guarantee they will, and that people assuming a merger is certain are overstating it. He nonetheless said there is a lot of merit in combining the two, citing superintelligence software, chip design, Terafab, robotics and launch.
The key roadblock is the vote. On the Tesla side, a deal needs approval from 50% of all outstanding shares, not just those voted, which Musk called a high hurdle. Outside estimates already frame the terms: RBC has suggested SpaceX could pay $480 per Tesla share in a $3.74tn deal, while Gary Black expects a $420-per-share stock-for-stock offer.

Why it matters: This is a structural event rather than an earnings one, and it can move both stocks independently of any results. A deal would reshape share counts, valuation and index weightings, and would open arbitrage between SPCX and TSLA on the implied exchange ratio. Formal committees mean a real process is under way, but the Tesla voting threshold makes completion far from assured. Tesla reports on Wednesday, and the merger will dominate that call.
3. First Profit as a Public Company, With AI Now the Largest Business

Revenue was $14.58bn against $12.87bn expected, up 161% year on year, with all three segments ahead of estimates. Super Intelligence (SI), the renamed AI segment, brought in $7.56bn against an estimate of $6.3bn and overtook Connectivity (Starlink) at $5.25bn against $4.86bn expected. Last quarter Starlink was comfortably ahead. Space revenue was $1.77bn against $1.43bn.
Net income was $4.40bn, or 35 cents a share, against $1.88bn and 15 cents expected, a swing from a $541m loss last quarter. That headline was boosted by about $1bn of other income and a $390m tax benefit. The cleaner measures still beat: operating income was $2.79bn against $2.24bn, and adjusted EBITDA $8.81bn against $6.59bn.
SI posted $431m of operating profit, against a consensus loss of $13.5m and a $1.26bn loss in Q2. SI adjusted EBITDA was $5bn, well over half the company total, making SI the largest profit contributor as well as the largest revenue line. Excluding $1.2bn of stock-based compensation tied to Cursor, SI earned $1.6bn of operating profit. That charge is not a one-off: of Cursor's $60bn equity value, $23bn was allocated to retention and replacement awards that vest over roughly three years. Cursor, acquired mid-quarter, contributed $608m of revenue, but excluding it, SI Solutions & Infrastructure revenue still grew 192% quarter on quarter. Most of that growth comes from cloud services agreements, renting data-centre compute to third parties; Bloomberg has reported Google and Anthropic as the main customers.

Connectivity revenue rose 69% year on year. Consumer subscribers rose by 1.6m in the quarter to 13.6m, slightly below expectations, but monthly consumer ARPU rose 5% to $69, and enterprise and government revenue grew 91%. Connectivity gross margin was 55%, including a one-off benefit of about 3 points from tariff refunds. SpaceX has 11,100 satellites in orbit and completed 113 launches in the year to 30 September. The space segment is still loss-making as Starship development accelerates.
Why it matters: This changes how the stock is valued. With SI the largest business by both revenue and EBITDA, SpaceX can be compared with AI infrastructure names, which trade on higher multiples, rather than with a satellite operator. Operating income and the ex-Cursor SI profit matter more than the $4.4bn net income because they show the beat is repeatable. Two cautions temper it: the Cursor charge will weigh on reported SI earnings for about three years, and Johnsen guided Q4 gross margins back towards Q2 levels as Q3's one-off benefits drop out.
4. Q4 Capex of $35–40bn, Roughly Double Q3, Backed by Demand

Q3 capex of $19.59bn was in line with estimates. SI accounted for $16.44bn of it, against $16.9bn expected, and the space segments only $1.61bn. Johnsen then guided Q4 capex to $35–40bn. SpaceX ended the quarter with $51.3bn of cash and $38.6bn of marketable securities, close to $90bn in total, so the Q4 midpoint alone equals roughly 40% of that liquidity.
Asked by Doug Anmuth of JPMorgan how this will be funded, Johnsen cited operating cash flow first, then debt markets accessed through SpaceX's investment-grade rating, plus partnerships across vendors and customers. He committed to keeping the investment-grade rating. He said new compute deployments pay back in under a year, with pricing now slightly above the top of the $30–50 per watt range discussed last quarter. Musk said a six-month payback next year is not impossible.
The contract structure matters as much as the spending. Musk said compute is split roughly 50/50 between internal use and rental to third parties, and that SpaceX deliberately rents on short-term contracts at spot rates rather than locking in long-term deals. He said contracts are renewing at higher dollars per watt, that SpaceX is "hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler" for capacity, and that it could rent its compute several times over.
Execution is visible. SpaceX is deploying about 220,000 Nvidia GB300s a month, moving to the Vera Rubin platform next year. It casts its own turbine blades and vanes, which Musk said lets it bring power online 12–18 months faster than rivals waiting on suppliers. On chips, Musk said ASML and other suppliers are accelerating equipment deliveries for Terafab at Gibbons Creek, which sent ASML ADRs up 2.7% during the call. He expects a first functional test chip in May or June 2027 and volume production in Q3 2028.

Why it matters: Capex is the biggest risk to the thesis, so it belongs alongside the positives. It drives free cash flow and future funding needs. The payback claim, the backlog and hyperscaler demand are what decide whether the market treats the spending as growth investment or cash burn. The short-term contract model cuts both ways: it captures rising prices while compute is scarce, but leaves revenue exposed if spot pricing falls.
5. ARR Targets: $100bn by End-2026 and $500bn–$1tn by End-2027

Johnsen said SpaceX remains on track for its previously stated goal of $100bn of annualised revenue by the end of this year, defined as December revenue multiplied by 12. That requires roughly $8.3bn of revenue in December 2026. Musk went further, putting ARR at $500bn to $1tn by the end of 2027. That implies $42–83bn of revenue in December 2027 alone.
The compute plan behind it: Musk said he is highly confident of adding 10GW in 2027 and would be surprised if SpaceX had less than 13GW online by the end of next year. He sees a small but rising chance of over 20GW, though he called the detailed plan "highly proprietary." He also plans a 440,000-chip Vera Rubin training cluster by the end of Q2 2027.
Why it matters: These targets set the bar the stock will be judged against. The $100bn year-end figure is testable within ten weeks, at the Q4 results, so a hit or a miss will move the price. The 2027 range is what bulls will use to justify the valuation, and the Q1 guidance makes it look less fanciful. Credibility is the swing factor: Musk's Starship cadence has already softened from daily launches next year to twice weekly by H2 2027, and he conceded his internal 2028 goal for a first Louisiana launch is unlikely, with 2029 "highly likely."
What to Watch
Tesla's results on Wednesday, where the merger will take centre stage. Starship Flight 15 in November, when SpaceX will attempt to catch both the booster and the ship; it expects the FAA licence to cover a return to the launch site and tower catch for both stages. The Q4 report, which will test the $100bn ARR target and show whether the capex step-up is converting into revenue. Starlink V3 rollout, where Gwynne Shotwell said users need a few hundred satellites, expected by mid-2027, before the network noticeably improves. Competition, with Europe's top carriers exploring a satellite group to fend off SpaceX. In the background, political risk is building ahead of the midterms in two weeks: Senator Chris Van Hollen plans a bill targeting Musk's election spending alongside SpaceX's defence contracts, and a Wall Street Journal report that Musk ordered a Starlink slowdown affecting Ukraine has drawn congressional attention.

text:
White Stork Travels 5,515 Kilometres From Poland, Dies in #Somaliland

HARGEISA, October 20, 2026 – A white stork that migrated from Poland was found dead in Somaliland’s eastern city of Ceerigaabo, approximately 5,515 kilometres from where it was first identified, highlighting the country’s importance as a passage for migratory birds travelling between Europe and Africa.

The bird, identified by a metal identification ring marked VX 5509 POLAND, was discovered on September 17 in the courtyard of a residential property in Ceerigaabo, according to a report prepared by wildlife conservation activist Muse Said.

The bird’s remains were collected by Mohamed Yusuf, the Sanaag regional coordinator of Somaliland’s Ministry of Environment.

Following the discovery, the ministry’s Wildlife Department contacted the Polish Bird Ringing Centre to establish the bird’s origin and migration history.

In a response received on October 10, the Polish research centre confirmed that the white stork (Ciconia ciconia) had been ringed on June 22, 2026, in northern Poland.

The bird was still a nestling when it was ringed, and its sex had not been determined.

According to the Polish Bird Ringing Centre, the straight-line distance between the ringing location and Ceerigaabo was approximately 5,515 kilometres, with 87 days separating the ringing date and the discovery of its remains

Muse Said, a Somaliland wildlife conservation activist, told Horndiplomat that the discovery demonstrated the ecological importance of Somaliland’s natural habitats and the need to protect migratory birds.

“Birds are nature’s laboratories,” Said told Horndiplomat, emphasising their role in understanding environmental conditions and the health of ecosystems.

“Where birds are present, it is a sign of rich biodiversity and a thriving natural environment,” he said.

“We must protect birds in their natural habitats,” Said added, calling for greater public awareness of wildlife conservation.

Somaliland lies along the Horn of Africa, a region crossed by migratory birds travelling between Europe, Asia and Africa.

Said identified several locations in Somaliland as important habitats and observation sites for migratory birds, including Rabshiga Mountain, Sa’ad ad-Din Island, Daallo, the Wagar Mountains and Gacan Libaax.

He also highlighted the Warsangli linnet, a bird associated with the Sanaag region, as an example of Somaliland’s distinctive birdlife.

The country’s mountains, coastal areas and other natural habitats offer opportunities for birdwatching, wildlife research and biodiversity conservation, Said said.

Bird ringing is widely used by researchers to study migration routes, survival rates and bird populations. Metal rings carrying unique identification numbers allow researchers to trace individual birds when they are encountered elsewhere.

The discovery in Ceerigaabo provides a documented connection between northern Europe and Somaliland through the movement of a single migratory bird, underscoring the importance of cooperation between local wildlife authorities and international research institutions in studying migration and biodiversity across the Horn of Africa.

(Reporting by Mohamed Duale; HornDiplomat News Desk) https://t.co/DCuLiOJVSu via @HornDiplomat

Read your article.  The argument advanced is fallacious. The priorities of states and the character of their alliances are not static; both evolve in response to changing strategic circumstances, domestic pressures, and the distribution of power. Statements or alignments from two decades past therefore carry limited prescriptive force for present policy. The wartime coalition between the United States and the Soviet Union against Nazi Germany offers a clear historical illustration: an alliance of necessity forged against a common existential threat does not confer enduring legitimacy on subsequent Soviet or Russian actions, nor does it constrain the independent judgment of later generations of policymakers.
Assertions that “NATO snipers” were responsible for specific deaths are advanced without supporting evidence. In the absence of verifiable documentation, such claims remain conjectural and cannot serve as a foundation for analysis.
The question of which party bears primary responsibility for the initiation of hostilities is, at this stage, secondary to the nature of the regimes and the stakes of the conflict. The Russian Federation under Vladimir Putin has consolidated an oligarchic authoritarian system that systematically suppresses political opposition, independent media, and civil society. In this respect it belongs in the same category of closed, coercive orders as the clerical regime in Iran and the dynastic dictatorship of North Korea. Populations across Eastern Europe and Ukraine have repeatedly demonstrated a preference for political systems that afford greater scope for individual liberty and accountable government. To accept the subordination of those populations to permanent Russian tutelage would be to consign them to a condition of constrained sovereignty and restricted rights.
The argument under consideration does not withstand scrutiny.

text:
What Americans Should Be Questioning Before November

1. Islam and political Islam: Where is the line between religious freedom and movements seeking to impose religious law through government? The Constitution protects the right to practice Islam, just as it protects other faiths. Political movements that challenge equal rights or constitutional government warrant scrutiny.

2. Communism: What happens to private property, economic independence, freedom of expression, and political opposition when the state controls major parts of society? History offers serious examples of abuses under one-party communist governments.

3. Democratic socialism: How much economic power should government exercise? Supporters emphasize public services and reducing inequality; critics question the costs, incentives, taxation, and potential expansion of state authority. Democratic socialism is not identical to communism.

4. California's fraud and government oversight: Why did fraud prevention fail so badly? California's state auditor reported approximately $1.5 billion in estimated improper unemployment payments during 2023–2024, including more than $500 million in estimated fraudulent payments in 2024 alone. 

5. Minnesota's fraud scandals: How did programs intended to feed children and help vulnerable residents become targets for extensive fraud? Federal prosecutors reported 63 convictions in the Feeding Our Future case by March 2026, while a separate Medicaid housing-services fraud case resulted in a $3.6 million conviction in October. 

6. France and Islamist separatism: France has debated measures against religiously motivated political movements that challenge secular government and equality under the law. French officials have explicitly distinguished ordinary Muslim religious practice from political Islamist movements. 

7. Accountability across party lines: When billions in public funds are mishandled or stolen, who should be held responsible? Criminal perpetrators, administrators, elected officials, and oversight agencies have different responsibilities, and those responsibilities deserve investigation.

8. The Founding Fathers' vision: Are today's political proposals consistent with individual liberty, freedom of conscience, private property, due process, and limited constitutional government?

Republicans are far from perfect. Democrats are not a single ideology. And legitimate criticism of Islamism, communism, democratic socialism, or government fraud should be based on specific beliefs, policies, and documented conduct—not guilt by association.

The essential question this November is whether candidates will protect the constitutional freedoms Americans inherited, exercise public power responsibly, and hold wrongdoing accountable—even when it occurs within their own political ranks.

✨To get professional stability, victory in all battles, & grace of Sri Shanidev, worship the Shami plant/tree on Dussehra (Vijayadashami) or on a Saturday🪔

Follow the traditional steps and rituals below:
1. Required Puja Samagri (Items)
Clean water (in a Kalash or small vessel)
Roli, kumkum, or sandalwood paste (chandan)
Akshat (unbroken raw rice grains)
Fresh flowers
Diya (ghee or oil lamp) and incense sticks (agarbatti)
Sweets or fruits as prasad
Mauli (sacred thread)
Coins or Dakshina

2. Step-by-Step Puja Vidhi
Clean the Area: Clean the space around the Shami tree or plant at your home or a temple.

Purify Yourself: Take a bath and wear clean, fresh clothes.

Offer Water: Gently pour a small amount of clean water at the base of the Shami plant.

Apply Tilak: Apply roli, kumkum, or sandalwood paste (tilak) to the trunk or base of the plant, and tie a sacred mauli thread around it.

Offer Rice and Flowers: Offer akshat (rice grains), fresh flowers, and sweets/fruits as prasad.

Light the Lamp: Light a ghee or oil diya and incense sticks near the plant.

Perform Aarti and Chant the Shami Mantra: Pray for courage, prosperity, the removal of obstacles, and victory over challenges. Recite the traditional Shami prayer:
Shami shamayate papam, 
Shami shatru-vinashini. 
Arjunasya dhanurdhari, 
Ramasya priyadarshini.

Exchanging Leaves: After the puja, pluck or collect a few Shami leaves (or exchange them with family members, elders, and friends as a symbol of "golden leaves" / suvarna representing wealth and goodwill). 

Astrological & Vastu Benefits:-
Appeasing Lord Shani (Saturn): The Shami tree is strongly associated with Shani Dev. Lighting a mustard or sesame oil lamp under the tree on Saturdays is believed to mitigate malefic Saturn effects, Sade Sati, and Shani Dosha.

Stability and Protection: Keeping or planting a Shami tree near the main entrance or in the Vastu-compliant corner of a home is believed to bring positive energy, financial stability, and protection from negative forces.

text:
☀️The Secret Ritual of the ancient Kings on the VijayaDashami Day⚔️

Aparajita Puja is one of the most powerful, ancient, and esoteric rituals performed on Vijayadashami (Dussehra). Worshipping Goddess Aparajita—the "Unconquerable One"—is believed to grant absolute victory (Vijay) over enemies, court cases, obstacles, and negative energies for the entire year. Historically, victorious Kshatriya Kings never marched to war without performing this specific ritual to ensure triumph.

The Secrets and Esoteric Significance:-
The deep mystical layer of Aparajita Puja involves tracking energy cycles and cosmic alignment:
The Origin of the Supreme Shakti: According to scriptures, after Goddess Durga destroyed Mahishasura in Her diverse ferocious forms, She absorbed back into Her absolute, primal source energy—Adishakti Aparajita—and retreated to the Himalayas. Worshipping Her on Dussehra connects directly to this absolute source energy.

Lord Sri Ram’s Secret Weapon: It is hidden in lore that before commencing His march to Lanka, Lord Sri Ram specifically performed the Aparajita Puja to invoke Her energy. Goddess Aparajita materialized, blessed Him, and guaranteed His ultimate victory over Ravana.

The Wrist-Tie Amulet (Aparajita Sutra): One of the closest guarded home rituals involves the Aparajita Vine. After the puja, mothers or priests tie a strand of the Aparajita vine or a energized sacred thread onto the right wrist of family members. This serves as an invisible energetic shield protecting the wearer from evil eye, accidents, and professional failure throughout the year.

The Direction of Manifestation: The ritual strictly leverages the Ishan Kon (North-East direction). The North-East is considered the gateway of divine energies. Activating this corner on Dussehra clears stagnant household energies.

Step-by-Step Puja Vidhi (Ritual Guide):
The puja must be performed during the Aparahna Period (afternoon hours).
Step 1: Cleanse the Sacred Corner: Clean a space in the North-East corner of the house or garden.

Step 2: Draw the Ashtadal Lotus: Use sandalwood paste, kumkum, or rice flour to draw an eight-petalled lotus (Ashtadal Chakra) on the ground or a clean wooden platform.

Step 3: Establish the Deities: In the centre of the lotus, establish the primary energy of Goddess Aparajita (using a clay idol, a picture, or by placing a blue Aparajita flower plant). Invoke Her companions by chanting:
Centre: Om Aparajitayai Namah (Goddess Aparajita)
Right/South Side: Om Kriyashaktayai Namah (Goddess Jaya)
Left/West Side: Om Umayai Namah (Goddess Vijaya)

Step 4: Offerings: Offer Akshat (unbroken rice), Roli, Shami tree leaves, and specifically blue or white Aparajita flowers. Light a ghee lamp (diya) and incense.

Step 5: The Victory Mantra: Recite the specific victory prayer to seal the intentions:
Sanskrit Verse:-
हारेण तु विचित्रेण भास्वत्कनकमेखला ।
अपराजिता भद्ररता करोतु विजयं मम ॥

English Transliteration:-
Hāreṇa tu vicitreṇa bhāsvat-kanaka-mekhalā ।
Aparājitā bhadra-ratā karotu vijayaṁ mama ॥

(Meaning: O unconquered Goddess, adorned with a brilliant golden girdle, bring me ultimate victory and auspiciousness.)

Step 6: Visarjan (Farewell): Conclude by offering sweets or fruits (Naivedya). Slightly nudge the setup or Kalash toward yourself to internalise the generated positive energy before concluding.

🪷Bhagavati Aparajita Durga Maa Ki Jai🪷

text:
Paul George scored 38 points today in his first game for the Boston Celtics.

Nobody in the history of the franchise has ever scored more in a debut. The old mark was 30, by Kristaps Porzingis in 2023.

Boston lost anyway. They led the Detroit Pistons by 22 and lost 121 to 113.

George is 36 years old and this is his fifth NBA team. Here is how he got to this one.

Rewind eighteen years and he was a kid in East Palmdale, California, in the high desert north of Los Angeles, spending his afternoons at Domenic Massari Park because there was not much else to do out there.

His mother, Paulette, had a stroke when he was 10. He wrote years later in Sports Illustrated Kids that basketball became a good distraction. That is the year he started taking it seriously.

He did not make varsity as a freshman at Knight High School. He started on junior varsity as a sophomore and got pulled up partway through the season. By his senior year he averaged 23.2 points and 11.2 rebounds, told a reporter before the season that his team would not lose again, and then closed the year on a ten game winning streak and a league title.

Then recruiting happened to him, which is its own education.

He committed to Santa Clara and backed out on his coach's advice. He committed to Pepperdine in August of 2007 and backed out of that one too, midway through his senior season, after the coach who recruited him resigned. Two schools, two commitments, two exits, none of it his doing.

He finished with offers from Georgetown and Penn State. Georgetown. A blue blood, a national stage, the kind of program that puts a kid from Palmdale on television every week.

He went to Fresno State.

The reasons he gave were that it was close to home so his family could come to his games, and that he liked the campus. That is the whole explanation from a three star recruit with a Big East door standing open.

He has never publicly tied that choice to his mother, and it would be cheap to do it for him. The two facts simply sit beside each other. A mother who got sick when he was a boy, and an 18 year old who picked the school where she could sit in the stands.

Two years later the Indiana Pacers took him tenth overall. Nine All Star teams. Six All NBA selections. A compound fracture of his right leg in 2014 that he came back from.

The honest counterpoint. He is 36, he played 37 games last season, and the Boston Celtics traded Jaylen Brown to get him. Thirty eight points in October does not settle that, and his team still lost a game it led by 22.

But a kid from the high desert once chose the gym his family could drive to.

Today he set a record in a building more than 2,500 miles from it.

If you love basketball stories like these, follow us on any platform @ontaphoops

text:
The original screenplay for Disney's 1992 film "The Mighty Ducks" was considerably darker than the family-friendly movie that eventually reached theaters. Screenwriter Steven Brill originally envisioned a more dramatic hockey story featuring adult romance, darker humor, and Gordon Bombay's troubled personal life as an ex-NHL player instead of a lawyer.

After Disney acquired the project, producer Jordan Kerner encouraged Brill to introduce broader comedy, including flatulence jokes, suggestive humor (like having-sex-with-your-mother gags), and slapstick involving blows to the groin, much of which was dialed back for the final release. 

Another surprising piece of the film's history involves Jake Gyllenhaal, who was offered the role of Charlie Conway but was forced to turn it down when his parents insisted he prioritize his education over several months of filming. The role ultimately went to Joshua Jackson; Leonardo DiCaprio reportedly also auditioned.
