“In a time of universal deceit, telling the truth is a revolutionary act.” ~ George Orwell

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

This digest covers consequential U.S. and world developments from a conservative and center-right vantage. Stories are verified where possible and attributed by outlet. Allegations, announcements, and unconfirmed claims are labeled as such. Analysis is confined to the America First Read.

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

DOMESTIC U.S. NEWS 🦅

Trump unveils fraud whistleblower rewards in Oval Office announcement

President Trump, with VP JD Vance and independent journalist Nick Shirley, announced a Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program on Oct. 20. Trump described a 1% commission on qualifying tips and said he would personally settle competing claims. A White House official had earlier described a $25 million, DOJ-run program paying up to $30,000 per tip, so the payout structure is not yet reconciled. Per the official, a tip must lead to a fraud conviction or a significant federal enforcement action. CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz separately said another $1.2 billion in California Medicaid personal-care payments is being deferred. FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson urged mandatory minimum sentences for benefits fraud.

Source: Fox News

Omar immigration-fraud probe widens; no charges announced

Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a search warrant at Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home on Oct. 12, and the Justice Department confirmed a court-authorized warrant in an ongoing criminal investigation. Fox reports, citing sources, that investigators are examining whether she or her father falsified information on her citizenship paperwork. Fox also reports her sister, Sahra Noor, voluntarily spoke with investigators, and the Wall Street Journal reported her phone, passport, and computer were seized. The New York Times reported about a dozen people, including relatives, were subpoenaed. Border czar Tom Homan said denaturalization is possible if allegations are proven. Omar denies wrongdoing and calls the raid political targeting, and Vance says the probe is not politically motivated.

Source: Fox News; Wall Street Journal and New York Times (as cited by Fox); Scripps/TNND

Philadelphia DA Krasner: federal referral, subpoenas reported

On Sept. 15, U.S. District Judge Paul Diamond referred DA Larry Krasner to federal prosecutors. The judge alleged Krasner and a top aide pressured staff to lie in court and threatened consequences for those who refused. Fox News now reports, citing sources, that the Justice Department has sent grand jury subpoenas. I reviewed only the headline of that report. Krasner disputes the judge’s findings and says he will appeal.

Source: Fox News; Associated Press

UNC settles Trump administration probes

UNC Chapel Hill reached a settlement closing 18 Education Department investigations and a Justice Department compliance review. They concerned alleged campus antisemitism and race-based admissions policies. Settlement terms beyond the closures were not reviewed.

Source: Fox News

Trump approval hits record low in Fox poll as midterms near

A Fox News poll released last week put Trump’s approval at 36% and disapproval at 64%, a low for either term. Only 22% approved of his handling of inflation, while border security was his best issue at 50/50. Among Republicans, 76% approved. Trump rallied for Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas on Monday night. Midterms are Nov. 3.

Source: The Hill (reporting the Fox News poll); Fox News

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS 🌐

Iran diplomacy stalled, though mediators say contacts continue

President Pezeshkian told Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir there will be no return to talks until the U.S. halts sanctions, threats, and pressure. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said no enriched material will leave Iran. Qatar says engagement continues and warns of regional spread if escalation goes unchecked. A Qatari outlet, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, reported a Qatar-Pakistan compromise that would give Iran interest on $6 billion in frozen funds in exchange for an IAEA visit. That report is unconfirmed, and it said a breakthrough could come this week. Trump said the U.S. is “doing very well” and must decide how to win. Russian FM Sergey Lavrov visited Tehran Monday, and Iran’s FM says ties have never been closer.

Source: CBS News (citing AFP/AP)

Houthi-Saudi fighting escalates

Saudi forces intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile and a drone aimed at Riyadh on Tuesday. Houthis claim six operations against Saudi targets in 48 hours, including airports and Aramco sites. A Houthi missile strike on a Yemeni government camp in Shabwa Monday killed at least 73 recruits, per a Yemeni official. That is the deadliest strike since fighting resurged. Riyadh’s “Davos in the desert” investment conference was postponed to 2027. Egypt’s parliament delayed a vote on military support for Saudi Arabia until Oct. 26. Trump has said he is considering joining Saudi operations, and Houthis threaten retaliation if he does.

Source: CBS News (citing AP/AFP)

France riots: curfews, calm Monday night, contested casualty picture

Roughly 550,000 people joined cost-of-living and school-conditions protests Saturday, per PM Sébastien Lecornu. Violent fringes burned Limoges’ city hall and Lyon’s tourist office and looted stores, and nearly 2,400 were arrested, per the Interior Ministry. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said police “lost control” and offered to resign, and Macron refused. Lecornu ordered localized curfews, and Monday night passed without major incidents. Lecornu said no one was killed Saturday, while CNN described the violence as deadly, and I could not reconcile the two. Fox cites nearly 1,000 injured officers, which I could not confirm. Trump blamed immigration, while Lecornu blamed the far left and criminals. Macron is touring the Gulf for fuel, with the Élysée citing 200,000 extra tons of diesel monthly from the UAE and Bahrain. Brussels saw clashes with police.

Source: Al Jazeera; CNBC; CNN; Fortune; Fox News

Trump pauses new Russia sanctions amid Ukraine strain

Trump signed an executive order Oct. 16 putting new Russia sanctions on hold days before they took effect, after an earlier diesel deal with Moscow. CBS reports bipartisan backlash. Trump’s Oct. 11 “energy ceasefire” was confirmed by neither side. Ukrainian figures cited by Al Jazeera put one day’s Russian barrage at 850 drones and 39 missiles. Ukraine says Starlink speed limits disrupted its drone operations, and responsibility for that is disputed. The administration says the moves aim to lower fuel prices.

Source: CBS News; Al Jazeera; Reuters

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

BUSINESS & MARKETS 💹

Stocks rally on earnings, easing yields and oil

The Dow rose about 1% (roughly 529 points) to 52,495 and the S&P 500 gained 0.3% to 7,712. The Nasdaq finished marginally lower at 26,424, per Kiplinger. The 10-year yield slipped to about 5.115%, and front-month WTI fell 0.9% to $102.75, though that contract is up nearly 14% in October. 3M jumped 5.8% on a beat-and-raise quarter and an Amazon data-center agreement. Braze surged about 52% on Salesforce’s announced $5.66 billion all-cash bid, which is not expected to close until fiscal 2028. Netflix and SpaceX reported after the close, and those results are not included.

Source: Kiplinger

Housing weakens

Housing starts fell 5.2% in September to about 1.2 million, and building permits slipped 0.2%. Pending home sales dropped 7.3% month over month and 11.3% year over year. Mortgage rates remain above 7%.

Source: Kiplinger; Inman

Inflation and Fed backdrop

September CPI rose 3.7% year over year (released Oct. 14), with core up 0.3% on the month. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75%–4.00% on Sept. 16 and meets Oct. 27–28. Market odds of another October hike varied by source after the CPI report, and Citi now expects a December hike. InvestingLive reported September payrolls of only 29,000.

Source: Inman; InvestingLive; Bureau of Labor Statistics (as cited)

Oil stays elevated

Brent neared $110 Friday, its highest since mid-May, then eased on Monday after the Russia-sanctions pause. Market reports had it back above $110 early Tuesday before retreating. Strait of Hormuz crude flows ran about 40% below normal in the week ended Oct. 7, per Kpler data cited by Al Jazeera. G7 nations agreed in early October to release up to 100 million barrels from reserves.

Source: CBS News; Al Jazeera

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

SCIENCE & HEALTH ⚕️

Study: delaying newborn hepatitis B shots could raise infections

Researchers estimate a 19% increase in chronic hepatitis B infections among children and young adults if vaccination is delayed to age 2, as HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has recommended. The study was published Monday. It is a modeled estimate, and HHS’s response was not reviewed.

Source: KFF Health News (summarizing the New York Times)

NIH awarded about 12% fewer grants in FY2026

The National Institutes of Health made roughly 7,400 fewer awards than in the prior fiscal year.

Source: CIDRAP (via KFF Health News)

FDA weighing wider access to “wellness” peptides
Washington Post reporting from earlier this month says the FDA is considering broader availability of certain peptides, while FDA scientists and outside experts have raised safety alarms. This is under consideration, and I found no final action.

Source: Washington Post; KFF Health News

FDA expected to approve multi-cancer blood test
The Washington Post reported Oct. 17 that approval of a blood test screening for 50-plus cancers is expected, with doctors warning of drawbacks. It has not been approved as of this reporting.

Source: Washington Post

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

NATIONAL SECURITY 🛡️

Accused Iranian operative allegedly directing plots from jail

Justice Department filings, reported by The Times, allege Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al Saadi used coded phone calls from prison to push new plots and direct $1 million in transfers. He faces six terrorism counts in New York tied to Kataib Hezbollah and the IRGC, including alleged plots against a New York synagogue and Jewish sites in Los Angeles and Scottsdale. His lawyers call the prosecution political and cite solitary confinement. These are allegations, and trial is expected next summer. UK services report more than 50 Iran-linked arrests in the past year.

Source: The National (citing The Times)

German court convicts two in Iran-linked plot; ambassadors summoned

A German court sentenced two men tied to Iran’s intelligence service for plotting to kill a Jewish organization’s leader. Berlin summoned Iran’s ambassador, and Tehran summoned Germany’s, calling the accusations baseless.

Source: Associated Press (via CBS News)

U.S. missions warn Americans in the Middle East
Embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, and elsewhere warned that hostilities could spread without notice. A State Department alert said Iran-backed groups may target U.S. interests worldwide. A Houthi strike on Riyadh’s airport Oct. 10 killed an American.

Source: CBS News

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

MILITARY DEVELOPMENTS 🪖

Hormuz mine strikes and drone-loss claims

Iran’s IRGC says sea mines halted three tankers on a southern route Tuesday, with two set ablaze. It also claims another U.S. MQ-9 shot down. Neither claim was independently confirmed. The CBO’s September report counted at least 24 MQ-9s, two MQ-1s, and an MQ-4C lost since the war began, costing more than $800 million. UKMTO counted 10 attacks on shipping last week, with October the worst month since March. The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports continues.

Source: CBS News (citing AFP/AP); Congressional Budget Office (as cited)

Hegseth confirms Israel visit as post-midterm strike talk persists

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed meeting PM Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced Monday trip, saying he was “visiting our troops.” Trump has called renewed bombing after Nov. 3 “possible,” and Netanyahu told Trump they have “a job to finish.” Iran has asked for an emergency UN Security Council session over alleged U.S. threats to use the “Mother of All Bombs.” I did not review Trump’s underlying remark.

Source: CBS News; TIME (as cited by CBS)

Israel signals open-ended Lebanon posture

Defense Minister Israel Katz said the IDF will stay in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed. He threatened strikes on Beirut’s Dahiyeh after any launch at northern Israel, and a possible ground push near Nabatieh if Hezbollah joins an Iranian attack. These are announced intentions.

Source: CBS News

UK to fly defensive patrols over Saudi Arabia

Britain announced RAF Typhoons will conduct defensive counter-air operations over Saudi Arabia, plus advisers, a transport aircraft, and a 90-day extension of aerial refueling. London said British jets will not strike Houthi targets in Yemen.

Source: CBS News (citing AP)

─────────────── ★ ───────────────

OTHER NOTABLE AND UNUSUAL STORIES 🌀

Ukraine tests an aerial drone built to carry wounded soldiers

Developer SkyFall is moving its StarGate medevac drone to front-line testing, per AP (reported Oct. 15–16). United24 puts its range at 15 km one way with a 150 kg payload. This is testing, not confirmed combat use.

Source: Associated Press; United24 Media

France: looted goods turning up for sale online

France’s digital minister said goods looted in the riots are being sold online and was to meet social media executives Tuesday about removals.

Source: Al Jazeera

AMERICA FIRST READ 🇺🇸

 Analysis, not reporting.

The day’s common thread is the price of the Iran war. Oil near $100–110, 3.7% inflation, a Fed that has already hiked, and mortgage rates above 7% hit American households just as the Fox poll shows Trump’s weakest numbers on inflation. France’s riots are a warning. One reading blames immigration, as Trump does. The French government instead points to fuel prices, school conditions, and far-left agitators, and Fortune notes U.S. inflation is running higher than France’s. Either way, the political cost of energy prices is clear.

The administration is trading strategic leverage for lower pump prices. The pause on Russia sanctions and the diesel deal may ease fuel costs, but they are drawing bipartisan criticism and straining ties with Kyiv. A pressure-first approach on Iran, with its blockade and sanctions, has not reopened Hormuz. Iran’s hard-line statements may reflect hope of outlasting Trump through the midterms, though that is inference. Mediators still see room for a deal, and a deal could ease oil quickly.

The anti-fraud push, the Omar probe, and the Krasner referral fit the accountability theme the right favors. Each is an investigation or an announcement, not a finding, and the whistleblower program’s payout terms are still unsettled. The Iran-linked plot cases are a reminder that the war has a homeland-security front. What happens before and after Nov. 3 is uncertain.

🇺🇦 🇺🇲 Ukraine's US-provided early warnings of incoming Russian ballistic missiles are working again, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced after talks with American and European officials in Oslo on Tuesday.

The restoration follows days of serious concern in Kyiv over disruptions to intelligence sharing, restrictions affecting Starlink/Starshield and delays involving Patriot interceptors.

Zelensky said he discussed all three issues in a telephone call with Secretary of State Marco Rubio while traveling to Norway. He described the conversation as concrete and positive, adding that they may speak again within 48 hours.

In Oslo, Zelensky met US envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb. Jared Kushner participated remotely.

The discussions covered a broader peace framework, including long-term security guarantees for Ukraine, postwar economic recovery and Europe's future security arrangements.

According to a US official cited by Axios correspondent Barak Ravid, Ukraine presented new proposals that were discussed in detail. Washington described the meeting as productive and reported meaningful progress toward a coordinated American, Ukrainian and European negotiating position.

Zelensky said the proposed security guarantees would be incorporated into a document Witkoff intends to present to Russian officials.

Energy attacks remain a central obstacle. Ukraine, Zelensky said, immediately supported the American proposal for an energy ceasefire and offered to suspend strikes on sensitive Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow stopped attacking Ukrainian facilities. Putin refused, according to Zelensky, and Russian attacks continued.

Witkoff is expected to meet Putin in Russia on Wednesday, October 21, with Kushner participating virtually, according to the US official. The objective is to present the proposals discussed in Oslo and explore a path toward direct negotiations involving the leaders of Ukraine, Russia and the United States.

Zelensky has proposed a trilateral leaders' meeting to resolve questions that negotiators cannot settle themselves.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb said the diplomatic process appeared to be back on track after progress made at the technical level.

The immediate improvement is tangible: Ukraine says it is once again receiving warnings of incoming Russian ballistic missiles. Whether the broader diplomatic progress produces concessions from Moscow will become clearer after Witkoff's discussions with Putin.

Sources: Statements by Zelensky; Axios/Barak Ravid; AP; Norwegian Prime Minister's Office, October 20, 2026. https://t.co/gObx55iPdx

▫️✈️ FAA Officially Certifies Boeing 737 MAX 10, Clearing Way for Deliveries After Years of Delays▫️

✈️ Major Regulatory Approval: The Federal Aviation Administration has officially certified Boeing's 737 MAX 10, the largest aircraft in its bestselling 737 MAX family. The approval allows Boeing to begin delivering the aircraft to airlines after years of regulatory setbacks, technical challenges, and heightened safety scrutiny.

🏭 Deliveries Expected Soon: Boeing expects to begin deliveries in the coming months, marking a significant milestone for an aircraft originally scheduled to enter commercial service in 2020. The certification also supports Boeing's efforts to expand production at its manufacturing facilities in Washington state.

💰 More Than 1,550 Aircraft Ordered: Boeing has secured 1,555 orders from more than 30 customers worldwide. The MAX 10 accounts for over 30% of the company's outstanding 737 MAX orders, making its certification critically important to Boeing's financial recovery and future revenue.

🛫 Major Airlines Await Deliveries: United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, Alaska Airlines, and Ryanair are among the major carriers awaiting the aircraft. The MAX 10 can accommodate up to 230 passengers in its highest density configuration, allowing airlines to increase capacity while improving operating efficiency.

🛡️ Stricter Safety Requirements: The FAA required extensive testing and enhanced safety systems before granting approval. Boeing completed nearly 1,000 test flights involving more than 2,000 flight hours, alongside approximately 1,000 hours of ground testing. Improvements include an enhanced angle of attack system designed to strengthen flight control safety.

⚠️ Certification Follows Years of Controversy: The approval comes after Boeing faced intense scrutiny following two fatal 737 MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019 that killed 346 people, along with the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 door panel incident. These events prompted tougher regulatory oversight and additional aircraft safety requirements.

📈 Competition With Airbus Intensifies: The MAX 10 is Boeing's primary competitor to Airbus's A321neo in the high capacity, single aisle aircraft market. Certification strengthens Boeing's ability to compete for airline orders, although the Airbus aircraft offers greater passenger capacity and range in certain configurations.

🇺🇸 Boost for American Aerospace Manufacturing: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy welcomed the certification as a major achievement for American manufacturing. Boeing's expanded Everett production facility is expected to play an important role in increasing 737 MAX output and supporting the company's commercial aviation recovery.

text:
TRUMP IS NEGOTIATING WITH RUSSIA, AND ZELENSKY IS LOSING HIS SEAT AT THE TABLE

Trump is now making his position clear: he wants a peace deal with Russia, and he will not impose measures that could push Moscow away from negotiations.

He points out Zelensky’s attacks on Russian diesel refineries are raising global fuel costs and prolonging the war. So Trump has paused new sanctions and reopened a path for Russian diesel to reach world markets.

The White House calls that leverage. Russia gets market access if it reduces the fighting, accepts an energy ceasefire, or comes to the table.

But Kyiv sees it differently. Ukraine faces Patriot shortages, Starlink restrictions, and weaker defenses. Russia, meanwhile, is being offered sanctions relief.

Zelensky says Ukraine is ready to negotiate anywhere, in any format. Yet after accusing Trump of admiring autocrats and calling him a “killer,” he has made an already damaged relationship harder to repair.

The deal now taking shape includes Russian diesel sales, potential gas exports to Europe, pipeline talks, frozen Russian assets, and possible relief for the “shadow fleet.”

Europe has pushed back on parts of the plan. Washington appears determined to continue anyway.
JD Vance has described Putin as calm, deliberate, and focused on Russia’s interests. A potential Trump-Putin-Xi meeting could discuss Ukraine’s future, with Zelensky outside the room.

Europe says it stands with Ukraine while still buying Russian energy. Zelensky is asking for more money and weapons, but the mood is shifting.

Even MAGA is split. Laura Loomer warns Putin will not stop at Ukraine. Others, including DC Draino, Mike Cernovich, Ian Miles Cheong, and Catturd, argue peace will not come until Zelensky leaves.

Washington is talking to Moscow. Kyiv is trying to stay in the conversation. The question remains whether Trump has already decided to move the deal forward without Zelensky.

$539.19 at the counter, for an inhaler that cost him about $66 the year before.

Cole Schmidtknecht was 22 and had used Advair Diskus or its generics since he was a kid. In January 2024 he was told his inhaler wasn't covered anymore. He walked out without it. Days later came the asthma attack. He died Jan. 21, 2024.

His parents are suing OptumRx, UnitedHealth's PBM, along with the pharmacy chain. The complaint alleges OptumRx dropped the drug and its generics for financial reasons and skipped the 30-day notice Wisconsin law requires, so he never had a chance to ask for an exception.

His employer's self-insured plan was administered by UnitedHealth, and the complaint says he paid no more than about $66.86 in 2023, even in the deductible. OptumRx's own note listed Advair HFA, Breo Ellipta and Symbicort as covered options. The suit says nobody at the counter offered them.

The court's ruling says he spent six days on a ventilator. In July 2025 Judge Byron Conway refused to dismiss, writing that a claim over missing notice of a coverage change "does not implicate any of the policies underlying preemption." The pharmacy chain denies wrongdoing.

Same patient, same prescription, new price. A formulary is a deal between companies, rewritten every year, and patients find out at the register.

The heart of Joseph Smith’s false teaching was that he put his own authority over the authority of Scripture. He added his own revelation to the Bible’s revelation and took it upon himself to identify and correct what he claimed were errors in Scripture.

Smith believed that the Bible was corrupt and insufficient and for that reason both took away from, and added to, God’s written revelation. Regarding the Bible’s corruption he said, “I believe the Bible as it read when it came from the pen of the original writers. Ignorant translators, careless transcribers, or designing and corrupt priests have committed many errors.” These errors were both typographical and doctrinal. To address the Bible’s shortcomings, Smith produced his own translation of the Bible, making many corrections and additions to a variety of Old Testament and New Testament books.

He also claimed that his own revelations from God were the only access point to the true gospel that had apparently been lost. Mormon historian Richard Bushman says the “signal feature” of Smith’s life was “his sense of being guided by revelation.” He placed himself above all previous revelations and interpretations of the Bible—even those of Christ himself.

Followers and Modern Adherents
Joseph Smith gained many devoted followers during his lifetime. Immediately after his death, his followers split into two main groups: those who followed Brigham Young to Utah to become the modern “Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints,” and those who coalesced under Smith’s eldest son, Joseph Smith III to become the modern “Community of Christ” (formerly known as the “Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints”).

These are the two main groups who follow Joseph Smith today. They continue to adhere to his false teachings about the Bible and countless doctrines contained within it. They continue to deny the inerrancy and sufficiency of Scripture while elevating personal experience above the authority of the Bible. In total they number approximately 15 million and their ranks continue to grow through constant and systematic proselytization.

What the Bible Says
The Bible claims that it is the authoritative, infallible, inerrant, sufficient revelation of God. “Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him. Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar” (Proverbs 30:5-6). It offers this dire warning: “I warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book, and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are described in this book” (Revelation 22:18-19).

There is no historical evidence that the Bible was missing information or that it had been corrupted before it was compiled into the Old and New Testaments. The fact that Jesus quotes the Old Testament with such confidence and without any hint that it is lacking or misrepresentative is reason enough to accept it as the pure and true word of God (John 17:17). The New Testament has also been repeatedly proven as unchanged and undefiled since it was first given by God.

The diversity of interpretations and sects among those who claim to follow the Bible, the very context which so confused Smith and led him to create an entirely new religion, does not provide warrant to say that the Bible itself is ambiguous or lacking in any way. We are told to expect divisions and factions among the body, “in order that those who are genuine … may be recognized” (1 Corinthians 11:18-19). Mormonism itself has been cut by endless in-fights and divisions, showing that the problem with the fractured church is not corrupted Scriptures but corrupted hearts.

text:
What these gun-control idiots never took the time to learn about Americans when the Constitution was written, is that private Americans also owned cannons. Cannons were on some merchant ships. 

The Ancient and Honorable Artillery Company of Massachusetts dates to 1638 and was a private organization. In the 1740s, Benjamin Franklin and others helped form volunteer companies of horse, foot, and artillery that were armed and equipped at the members’ own expense, with officers chosen by the members. Similar private artillery companies continued into the early Republic (for example, incorporations in Vermont in 1801–1802). Some wealthy individuals or partnerships owned pieces outright.

In 1777, Brigadier General David Forman loaned three of his own artillery pieces to New Jersey militia. Post-war advertisements (1783 and 1789 in Philadelphia) offered cannons, howitzers, swivels, and related equipment for sale to private ship owners and others.

If we're going to use the writing of the Constitution as a reference, maybe we should be demanding the right to own howitzers.

In 1995, the wolves came back. The plants returned in abundance, and so did the songbirds and butterflies.

text: I’m fine with carriers in Canada, regardless of the brand, offering longer financing terms as options for the customer to select as most smartphones cost over $1,000 with some upwards of $4,000. Example  24 months 0% interest rate, 36 months 3.99% interest rate, 48 months 4.99% interest rate. Preferably keeping their 0% interest rate regardless of the term length would be preferable but it’s not realistic for a business to offer. This would allow more customers to get higher-end models such as the iPhone Pro Max, iPhone Duo, Samsung Fold, etc and not have to pay over a hundred dollars per month in financing on top of their wireless plan. As for device locking for 60 days I can’t see this passing and they would be better to ask the CRTC to restrict this to the carrier 15 days Buyers Remorse period. This would help protect stock from theft (retail, during shipping and at the warehouse). It would also put a stop to those who sign up to buy phones from carriers just to cancel the day after keeping the device instead of ordering through the manufacturer thus depleting stock for existing customers and those who want to sign up and stay with the carrier. If the CRTC agrees to any of this it should come with the specific requirement that all carriers immediately stop charging any fee for dealing with their customer service or retail agents whether that is a service call, sending a tech to fix a residential/business issue or when doing a wireless upgrade or activation (I.e Device Setup Charge). To benefit consumers and carriers any decision should come into effect within 30 days instead of taking months as I believe both are done with the delays caused by excessive red tape 🤔

text:
🏇 ANTZ OFFICIAL | MELBOURNE CUP 2026

13. ENFJAAR | PEDIGREE ANALYSIS

Sire: Lope De Vega
Dam: Tesoro, by Galileo
Second Dam: Theann, by Rock Of Gibraltar

Enfjaar’s pedigree combines the influence of Lope De Vega with Galileo’s exceptional Classic bloodlines and a female family responsible for several outstanding Group 1 performers. The deeper maternal line connects him to Halfway To Heaven, Magical, Rhododendron and Auguste Rodin, adding considerable European breeding depth. 

THE SIRE

Lope De Vega is by Shamardal, a son of Giant’s Causeway, out of Lady Vettori, by Vettori.

Lope De Vega won the French 2000 Guineas and Prix du Jockey Club, demonstrating his ability to combine miling speed with Classic middle-distance quality.

As a sire, he has produced high-class performers across a variety of distances. His pedigree introduces the influence of Giant’s Causeway and the wider Storm Cat line, while his own Classic achievements reinforce the quality of the male side of Enfjaar’s breeding.

For Enfjaar, Lope De Vega contributes class and versatility, with the maternal family providing further depth.

THE DAM

Enfjaar’s dam, Tesoro, is by Galileo, the son of Sadler’s Wells and Urban Sea.

Galileo became one of the most influential sires in European breeding, producing generations of Classic winners over middle and longer distances. His influence is particularly significant in pedigrees where stamina and sustained class are important considerations.

Tesoro is also a sister to Photo Call, a dual Grade 1 winner in the United States. This gives Enfjaar a close maternal relative who demonstrated top-level ability, reinforcing the quality of his immediate female family. 

THE SECOND DAM

The second dam, Theann, is by Rock Of Gibraltar, the outstanding son of Danehill and Offshore Boom.

Rock Of Gibraltar won seven consecutive Group 1 races, including the English and Irish 2000 Guineas. His influence brings speed and high-class performance into Enfjaar’s maternal background.

Theann is a half-sister to Halfway To Heaven, a three-time Group 1 winner who became the dam of champion racemares Magical and Rhododendron. Rhododendron subsequently produced Auguste Rodin, winner of the Epsom Derby and Irish Derby.

This is a particularly distinguished female family, combining Group 1 performance with successful breeding across generations. 

ANTZ OFFICIAL PEDIGREE ASSESSMENT

Enfjaar’s pedigree brings together Lope De Vega’s Classic versatility, Galileo’s stamina influence and Rock Of Gibraltar’s speed, supported by a female family rich in Group 1 performers.

The connections to Photo Call, Halfway To Heaven, Magical, Rhododendron and Auguste Rodin demonstrate the depth and quality of his maternal ancestry.

ANTZ OFFICIAL verdict: Enfjaar possesses an impressive European pedigree, with genuine Classic influences and an exceptional female family. However, while his breeding offers a strong foundation of quality, whether he can stay the full 3200 metres remains a separate question that pedigree alone cannot settle.

text:
🏇 ANTZ OFFICIAL | MELBOURNE CUP 2026

10. SMALL FRY | PEDIGREE ANALYSIS

Sire: Harzand
Dam: Duchess Of Daars, by Zoffany
Second Dam: Fairest Of All, by Sadler’s Wells

Small Fry’s pedigree brings together European Classic stamina through his sire Harzand and an influential Sadler’s Wells maternal line. The combination provides an interesting foundation when assessing the bloodlines behind a horse being considered for the ultimate two-mile test. 

THE SIRE

Harzand is by Sea The Stars, the outstanding middle-distance performer by Cape Cross, himself a son of Green Desert. Sea The Stars won the 2000 Guineas, Epsom Derby and Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, demonstrating exceptional class across a range of distances.

Harzand inherited that Classic influence and established his own reputation by winning both the Epsom Derby and the Irish Derby over 2400 metres. His pedigree therefore supplies a strong European stamina influence, with Sea The Stars and Cape Cross adding depth through the male line.

For Small Fry, Harzand represents a sire line with proven Classic credentials rather than one built solely around speed.

THE DAM

Small Fry’s dam, Duchess Of Daars, is by Zoffany, a son of Dansili, whose sire was Danehill. This introduces another important European bloodline, with Danehill’s influence extending across sprinters, milers and successful middle-distance performers.

Zoffany was a high-class two-year-old who won the Group 1 Phoenix Stakes. As a sire, he produced horses with varied distance capabilities, meaning his influence cannot automatically be interpreted as a guarantee of extreme stamina.

The key feature of this mating is the contrast between Harzand’s Classic staying background and the speed and versatility associated with the Danehill line.

THE SECOND DAM

The second dam, Fairest Of All, is by Sadler’s Wells, one of the most influential European sires of Classic and staying horses.

Sadler’s Wells was by Northern Dancer out of Fairy Bridge, by Bold Reason. His descendants have shaped generations of European breeding, particularly through their ability to produce horses with class over middle and longer distances.

Fairest Of All also brings the female family back to Token Gesture, her dam, who was by Alzao, a son of Lyphard. Token Gesture won the Group 3 Park Stakes at the Curragh, adding black-type quality to the deeper maternal pedigree. 

This gives Small Fry a maternal background featuring Sadler’s Wells and the wider Northern Dancer influence, reinforcing the depth of his European breeding.

ANTZ OFFICIAL PEDIGREE ASSESSMENT

Small Fry’s pedigree offers three important elements: Harzand’s Classic stamina, Sea The Stars’ exceptional middle-distance heritage and Sadler’s Wells’ deep influence through the maternal line.

Zoffany adds a different dimension through Danehill and Dansili, bringing versatility to a pedigree otherwise strongly influenced by established European Classic bloodlines.

On paper, the pedigree provides credible staying foundations. However, breeding alone cannot establish whether a horse will see out 3200 metres effectively. Small Fry’s ultimate suitability will depend on how those inherited qualities translate into his individual capacity for the distance.
